tasks.title: Pin exit codes with guard test
tasks.acceptance:
- internal/cli/exit.go declares the five codes of the §11.2 table: 0 success, 1 validation failure, 2 usage error, 3 file/configuration/external-command failure, 4 state conflict including lock timeout and partial post.
- A guard test asserts each numeric value literally, so a renumbering fails the suite rather than silently shipping.
- The codes are exported constants; no command uses a bare integer literal.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/exit.go declares all five §11.2 codes: ExitOK 0, ExitValidation 1, ExitUsage 2, ExitFile 3, ExitState 4, each carrying the meaning the table gives it, under a comment pinning them to the spec.
- TestExitCodesArePinned in internal/cli/root_test.go asserts each of the five numeric values literally, so a renumbering fails the suite rather than shipping silently; verified by go test ./... .
- All five are exported package-level constants in package cli, reachable by every command.
- No command uses a bare integer exit literal: Execute() maps its error path onto ExitUsage, and a grep over cmd/ and internal/ finds no numeric argument to os.Exit. Gate: go test ./... ok, golangci-lint 0 issues.

tasks.title: Build the cobra root command
tasks.acceptance:
- A spf13/cobra root command named cr exists at cmd/cr with internal/cli holding the command tree.
- Record ids are PR-scoped, so every command that names one takes the pull request as an argument.
- go build ./cmd/cr produces a working binary that prints help with no arguments.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The spf13/cobra root command named cr was already in place from commit 243a344 and is verified intact rather than rewritten: cmd/cr/main.go is a three-line entry point calling cli.Execute(), and internal/cli/root.go holds the tree, the five §11.1 global flags, and the error-to-exit-code mapping onto ExitUsage.
- Record ids are PR-scoped, so internal/cli/pr.go adds the fence every such command will build on: parsePR rejects anything that is not a positive pull request number, prArgs(n) validates the arity and the leading pull request argument, and TestRecordIDCommandsTakeThePullRequest walks the whole command tree and fails any command whose Use names <record-id> without <pr> ahead of it, or that takes a <pr> without validating it. Both halves were proven to bite by temporarily registering violating commands and observing the failures, then reverted.
- go build ./cmd/cr produces a working binary that prints help with no arguments. The root previously emitted only its Short line, because cobra suppresses the usage block for a command that is neither runnable nor populated, so newRootCmd now sets Args cobra.NoArgs and a RunE returning cmd.Help(). The freshly built /tmp/cr-dev/cr run with no arguments prints the usage block and all five global flags and exits 0, while cr bogus exits 2, and TestRootPrintsHelpWithNoArguments pins the behaviour.
Out of scope: registering the §11 command rows belongs to the next task, command-surface-stubs, so the tree-walk guard passes vacuously today and becomes load-bearing the moment those stubs land.

tasks.title: Register every specified command stub
tasks.acceptance:
- Every row of the §11 command table is registered with its documented argument shape and flags: init (--eject-roles), brief, review (--axis), claims record, merge (-o --repo --pr), record, map record, claims set-aside (--note), cells record, sandbox create|destroy, test (--filter), probe run (--kind), draft, post (--confirm --reconcile), answer, note (--remove), context, waivers list|remove (--repo --pr), stats (--repo), rules list (--dead --repo)|check|suggest, status, config (--resolved).
- A table-driven test enumerates the §11 rows and asserts each command resolves with its flag set.
- Unimplemented behaviour returns a not-yet-implemented error carrying a hint; the surface itself is complete.
- Found by intent-file-bypass, assigned here: §11 lists flags on other rows but omits --intent-file from cr brief, though §3.1.4 requires it and CLAUDE.md dogfoods it. cr brief therefore registers --intent-file even though the §11 row does not name it, and the table-driven test records that as a deliberate addition rather than letting the surface follow §11 into the gap.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every row of §11's table is registered with its documented argument shape and flags. Seven top-level commands were added — internal/cli/review.go (--axis), merge.go (-o/--output, --pr, and §11.1's global --repo), post.go (--confirm, --reconcile), status.go, stats.go, waivers.go (list, remove <id>, --pr), rules.go (list --dead, check <pr>, suggest) — plus internal/cli/claims.go's set-aside <pr> <claim-id> --note and internal/cli/config.go's --resolved. The rows already built keep the flags they had: init --eject-roles, test --filter, probe run --kind, note --remove. All twenty-six commands a user can type are in the tree, and `cr --help` lists the twenty-two top-level ones.
- A table-driven test enumerates the §11 rows and asserts each command resolves with its flag set. internal/cli/surface_test.go's specSurface carries one entry per invocable row, and TestTheCommandSurfaceIsTheSpecTable resolves each through cobra's Find, pins the Use line so a dropped positional fails, asserts every flag §11 names resolves, asserts §11's only shorthand -o resolves to --output, and asserts the command's own local flag set is exactly §11's flags plus the declared additions and nothing else. It then compares the table against leafCommands in both directions, so an undocumented command in the tree fails as loudly as a missing one.
- Unimplemented behaviour returns a not-yet-implemented error carrying a hint. internal/cli/stub.go's notImplementedError names the command cobra resolved and carries notImplementedHint, which tells the caller this is a stub rather than a broken install and to check `cr --version` against the release notes. notImplementedFor names a flag instead of a command, so `cr config --resolved` refuses without claiming that `cr config` is missing. §11.2 gives no code to a registered and unbuilt command, so the refusal takes exitCodeFor's fallback of code 2, pinned by TestAStubRefusesWithItsPathAndAHint rather than by a sixth code that would renumber the five invariant 5 fixes.
- The surface itself is complete, which means the argument shape is real ahead of the behaviour. TestAStubStillValidatesItsArguments runs every stub's Args validator and requires it to refuse an argument that is not a pull request, so `cr status HEAD` is answered as the usage error it is rather than as a stub refusal. TestAFlagAheadOfItsBehaviourRefuses covers the one flag registered on a command that works.
- The finding intent-file-bypass raised is confirmed against the spec rather than taken on trust. §11's `cr brief <pr>` row names no flag at all while other rows name theirs, §3.1.4 makes an issue file the stand-in for the tracker command, and CLAUDE.md's manual QA recipe runs `cr brief 1 --repo <owner>/<scratch> --issue CR-1 --intent-file issue.txt`. §11 is therefore incomplete about this row and not silent about a flag that should not exist. The same reading applies to `cr waivers remove`, where §11's row omits a positional that §7.4.7 spells out.
- `cr brief` registers --intent-file and the table records it as a deliberate addition. specSurface's added field maps every flag a command registers beyond §11's row to the section that requires it, and TestTheCommandSurfaceIsTheSpecTable asserts the command's local flag set equals §11's flags plus exactly those declarations, so an addition is either recorded with its section or it fails the test. `cr brief` declares --intent-file for §3.1.4 and --issue for §3.2, `cr claims record` declares --intent-file for the same reason, `cr probe run` declares the four flags §11's trailing ellipsis stands for, and `cr answer` and `cr note` declare §3.6.1's source and pr. `cr waivers remove <id>` carries §7.4.7's positional and says so in the same place.

tasks.title: Exit two on usage errors
tasks.acceptance:
- A missing required argument, an unknown flag, or an unparseable pull request reference exits 2 per §11.2.
- Cobra's own usage errors are mapped to 2 rather than to cobra's default 1.
- Tested for at least three commands taking different argument shapes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A missing required argument, an unknown flag, and an unparseable pull request reference all exit 2: measured on the built binary, `cr record 1`, `cr record 1 x --repo o/r --bogus` and `cr record abc x --repo o/r` each exit 2 with the usage hint, and TestEveryUsageErrorExitsTwoFromTheProcess holds nine such invocations at 2.
- Cobra's usage errors reach the process as 2 rather than 1: Execute passes every error through exitCodeFor, no row of the exit code table claims a usage error so each takes the ExitUsage fallback (TestNoRowClaimsAUsageError), and a hand mutant making Execute exit 1 failed all nine process runs before it was reverted.
- The test covers commands of different argument shapes: record takes a pull request and a file, note takes an issue key and text, status takes a pull request, merge takes variadic files with required -o and --pr flags, and probe run takes a pull request and a valued --kind flag.

tasks.title: Switch JSON output by TTY
tasks.acceptance:
- Output is JSON when stdout is not a terminal or when --json is given, and human-readable coloured text otherwise, per §12.1.
- The decision is made once in a shared writer, not per command.
- Tested by driving a command with a pipe and with a pseudo-terminal.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Output is JSON when stdout is not a terminal or when --json is given, and human-readable coloured text otherwise, per §12.1. internal/cli/output.go settles the shape from cmd.OutOrStdout() and the flag and nothing else, so text is the narrow case and a piped run is JSON without anyone asking. Detection goes through mattn/go-isatty rather than the file mode, because /dev/null and the master side of a pseudo-terminal are both character devices and neither is a terminal, which was measured on this platform before the choice was made. Colour is enabled on the fatih/color instance rather than through its package global, which is set from os.Stdout at init, so a run writing somewhere else is never coloured by a decision about a file it does not touch.
- The decision is made once in a shared writer, not per command. newRootCmd builds one writer and settles it in PersistentPreRunE before any RunE runs, and cr init and cr config emit through it by handing over an initResult or a configResult instead of formatting anything themselves. TestOnlyTheSharedWriterDecidesTheOutputShape parses the imports of every shipped file under internal/cli and fails any one but output.go that names go-isatty, encoding/json or fatih/color, which are the three ways a command could reach a second answer. It was proven to bite by temporarily importing encoding/json into pr.go and observing the failure, then reverted.
- Tested by driving a command with a pipe and with a pseudo-terminal. throughAPipe runs the command on a real os.Pipe and throughATerminal on the slave side of a real creack/pty pseudo-terminal, so nothing anywhere injects a boolean and the answer comes from the kernel. Four cases are covered, a pipe getting JSON, a terminal getting coloured text, --json forcing JSON on a terminal, and --no-color stripping the colour in both directions without moving the shape, plus cr init naming its state directory on a terminal. The terminal helper reads to a sentinel rather than to the close, because the master reports EIO the moment the last slave goes and takes the unread buffer with it, which gremlins caught as an empty read.
Out of scope: §12.2's two-space indentation is already honoured because cr config printed it before this task and regressing it would have been the larger change, but §12.3's never-null slice rule and its walking test stay with output-json-formatting. §12.4's hint field, §12.5's --compact omissions, §12.6's posted boolean and §11.1's seven --quiet exemptions are each their own task and get a seam here rather than an implementation, because results are values the writer encodes and the writer's own comment names it as where finding.HonestyDisclosure will be consumed, the exemption having to be a property of the one thing that writes.

tasks.title: Pretty-print JSON with empty slice rule
tasks.acceptance:
- JSON output is pretty-printed with two-space indentation per §12.2.
- Every slice field serialises as [] and never as null per §12.3; a test walks a fully-zero-valued payload of every output struct and asserts no null array appears.
- Constructors use make([]T, 0) rather than var x []T wherever a slice reaches output.
tasks.closed_reason:
- §12.2: internal/cli/output.go's emit is the one encoder and it calls json.MarshalIndent with a two-space indent, so no command picks its own width. TestJSONIsPrettyPrintedWithTwoSpaceIndentation re-indents the document cr printed and gets it back byte for byte, which holds at every depth the document has and fails for a tab, for four spaces, and for a compact document alike.
- §12.3 is kept at the marshal site rather than the construction site. withoutNilSlices deep-copies each payload on its way into the encoder and replaces every nil slice it can reach with an empty one, following one behind a pointer, inside an any, in a map's value, in an element of another slice, and in a field an unexported embedding promotes. A constructor binds only the payloads somebody has already written, whereas emit is the one door every JSON document leaves by, so the rule holds for output structs that do not exist yet and for a slice reassigned to nil after it was built. The single carve-out is a type that serialises itself, pinned by TestATypeThatSerialisesItselfKeepsItsOwnNull, because filling a json.RawMessage would not print a null but fail to encode at all.
- TestNoOutputStructPrintsANullArray walks a fully-zero-valued payload of every output struct. The set is read out of internal/cli's own source with go/ast rather than kept by hand, every type whose Text method takes the unexported writer being a payload and nothing outside the package being able to implement one, and it is matched against the walked list so a payload added later fails the test instead of going unchecked. Each probe materialises every other position, a pointer allocated, a map given an entry, an any holding a nil list, and is re-run once per layer of slice nesting so a null under a slice of structs is reachable at all. TestANullHidesNowhereInAPayload does the same to a fixture carrying every hiding place at once, which is what caught the fields of an unexported embedding being skipped.
- Constructors use make([]T, 0) rather than var x []T wherever a slice reaches output. The audit found no var x []T on any path to a payload, config.Strings and config.Map each build with append(make([]string, 0, len(value)), value...), and toStrings turns a decoded nil into []string{}, so cr config prints ignore.globs as []. The convention stands and the marshal-site rule now backs it, a slice made empty at construction being reassignable to nil afterwards.

tasks.title: Attach hint to every error
tasks.acceptance:
- Every error carries a hint field naming the next actionable step per §12.4.
- A shared error type makes the hint a required construction parameter, so an error without one cannot be built.
- A test asserts that every error returned by the command tree carries a non-empty hint.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every error carries a hint field: internal/cli/output.go's reportFailure writes {"error","hint"} as a JSON document on stderr whenever stdout is not a terminal or --json is given, and `error:`/`hint:` lines in a terminal; measured on the built binary, `cr record 1 missing.ndjson --repo o/r` piped went from a bare `error: open ...` with no hint to a document whose hint names `cr merge`, and TestAFailureThroughAPipeIsADocumentCarryingAHint and TestAFailureInATerminalIsProseUnlessJSONIsAsked hold both shapes.
- The hint is a required construction parameter: state.FileFailure panics on an empty hint and FileError's fields are unexported, and every row of internal/cli/exit.go's codes table carries its hint as a field that init refuses empty at package load, so neither a file failure nor a mapped error can be built without a step (TestAFileFailureWithoutAHintCannotBeBuilt, TestEveryRowOfTheExitTableNamesAStep).
- TestEveryErrorTheCommandTreeReturnsCarriesAHint walks every leaf of newRootCmd, runs each with no arguments, four junk arguments and an unknown flag, and asserts hintFor is non-empty for every error returned; a hand mutant making reportFailure print prose through a pipe failed it and the two failure-shape tests before it was reverted.

tasks.title: Implement compact flag omissions
tasks.acceptance:
- --compact omits output_tail, input, and ingested thread bodies per §12.5.
- --compact MUST NOT omit evidence or citations: the agent composes every posted body from them, so a compacted payload would leave the composition unfounded.
- Tested against a payload carrying all five fields.
tasks.closed_reason:
- §12.5's three omissions are made in internal/cli/output.go. compactOmits names output_tail and input bare, and an ingested thread body under the key it sits behind (comment.body and replies.body), because a bare body is not one field everywhere and §8.1 gives a drafted record a body of its own. The rule is keyed on the JSON name rather than on a Go type, since §5.5's probe record has no Go type in this repository yet and output_tail belongs to §5.2.4's run record too, so withoutBulk prunes the encoded document and answers for a payload nobody has written. It composes with §12.3's existing deep copy rather than replacing it. withoutNilSlices fills the value first, the document it encodes to is pruned after, and §12.2's two-space indentation still applies to the result.
- evidence and citations are unreachable rather than merely un-listed. omittedFields builds the table and panics on any name whose last segment is a founding field, so a table naming one does not fail a test, it fails to start. Proven by temporarily adding evidence and watching both the test binary and the cr binary abort in package init, then reverting. TestTheOmissionTableRefusesAFoundingField keeps it, and refuses the qualified forms record.evidence and finding.citations so narrowing a name by its key is no way round the rule.
- TestCompactDropsTheBulkAndKeepsWhatAPostedBodyRestsOn prints one payload carrying all five fields, a §5.5 probe stand-in for input and output_tail, a real finding.Finding for evidence and citations, and a real gh.Thread with a reply for the two bodies, both with the flag and without it, so every absence is the flag's doing rather than a field the payload never had. It also asserts the thread keeps its id and author while losing only its bodies, since §3.5.4 suppresses a finding by naming the thread. TestEveryPlaceAnIngestedThreadKeepsABodyIsOmitted reads those keys out of gh.Thread rather than restating them. Both were proven to bite by shrinking the table and observing the failures.
Out of scope: §12.4's hint field is output-error-hints, §11.1's --quiet honesty exemptions are quiet-honesty-exemptions, and §5.5's probe record and §12.6's posted commands are their own later tasks. CLAUDE.md's convention line was corrected in b43284b, having stated that --compact omits evidence, which §12.5 forbids.

tasks.title: Report posted boolean on write commands
tasks.acceptance:
- Every command that could have performed a network write reports a posted boolean per §12.6, so a dry run is distinguishable from a successful post in JSON as well as in a terminal.
- A dry-run cr post reports "posted": false; a confirmed one reports true.
- Commands that can never write omit the field rather than reporting false.
tasks.closed_reason:
- §12.6's boolean is carried by internal/cli/output.go's posting, a marker a result embeds, and by nothing else. Both halves of the sentence are there, the field in the JSON document and posting.line in the terminal rendering, because §12.6 names the terminal as well as the document. TestADryRunAndAConfirmedPostAreDistinguishable drives a payload through the writer in both modes and asserts each shape on its own, a payload being able to carry the field faithfully and still print a line that reads the same whichever way the run went.
- A dry run prints "posted": false, which is what posting carries unset, so §8.5.1's run that validates and sends nothing says so in the document and prints not posted in a terminal.
- A confirmed run prints true. That half is asserted at the seam rather than end to end, because cr post does not exist yet and nothing outside internal/gh can mint the confirmation whose write would set it, so the test drives the payload the gate will hand over instead of building the posting path to give itself something to fail against.
- A command that can never write omits the field rather than reporting false, which is what TestOnlyACommandBehindTheGateReportsPosted keeps true. A "posted": false on cr status would say the command weighed posting and declined, a claim about a decision nothing made, so presence is a property of the command rather than a default on every payload. The set that could have written is derived from the source as the files naming one of nowrite_test.go's mints, the same list TestNothingOutsideTheGhPackageMintsAConfirmation scans with, so §12.6's commands and §8.5's gate are one set rather than two lists free to drift. TestThePostedFieldIsDeclaredInOnePlace refuses a second spelling of the field, so embedding posting is the only way to carry it. Both directions were proven to bite by hand and reverted, embedding posting in initResult and hand-rolling the field each failing the equality, and a temporary mint literal in init.go failing it the other way. Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh. Mutation testing: gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal gives Killed 295, Lived 4, efficacy 98.66%, above the 98.65% baseline, with no new survivor and the two known timeouts unchanged.
Out of scope: cr post itself, so the confirmed half is asserted at the seam and not end to end, which belongs to dry-run-posting, confirm-flag-required and single-review-batching. §12.4's hint field is output-error-hints and §12.5's --compact omissions are output-compact-flag.

tasks.title: Wire the five global flags
tasks.acceptance:
- --json, --compact, --quiet, --no-color, and --repo <owner/repo> are registered as persistent flags with the effects of the §11.1 table.
- --repo overrides repository detection rather than supplementing it.
- Each flag is exercised by a test on at least one command.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/root.go registers all five §11.1 flags as persistent flags on the root command, and each carries the effect its row names. --json forces JSON on a terminal and --compact prunes §12.5's fields, both settled in internal/cli/output.go. --no-color strips the colour and leaves §12.1's shape alone. --repo names the repository, read through repoOf in internal/cli/pr.go. --quiet suppresses nothing, which is the decision rather than an omission and is now recorded where the flag is registered: §11.1 gives it informational messages and then names seven disclosures it may never touch, cr prints no informational message today because every byte on stdout is a command's own result that §12.1 shapes, and a suppression written before the exempt writer of quiet-honesty-exemptions would silence the seven §11.1 exists to protect.
- TestRepoOverridesRepositoryDetection drives cr config with --repo acme/web from inside a git repository whose origin names other/elsewhere, with a configuration layer waiting under each slug. The named repository's layer is the one in force and the repository cr stands in contributes nothing, which is what tells an override from a merge. The two layers set different settings rather than the same one at different values, because an override and a merge agree about post.max_comments whichever wins and disagree about render.lang. Detection is repository-detection's and is unbuilt, so today the working directory is inert and the same run becomes the adversarial one the day detection lands. The assertion was proven to bite by pointing config.go's repository layer at the standing slug and watching both halves fail, then reverting.
- Every flag is exercised through a real command. --json, --no-color and --compact were already covered by TestTheJSONFlagForcesJSONOnATerminal, TestNoColorStripsColourAndNothingElse (which asserts both that a pipe under it is still JSON and that a terminal under it carries no escape sequence) and TestCompactDropsTheBulkAndKeepsWhatAPostedBodyRestsOn. --repo is covered by TestRepoOverridesRepositoryDetection through cr config. --quiet is covered by TestQuietLeavesACommandsResultAlone, which runs cr config under the flag on a real pipe and on a real pseudo-terminal and finds the same document and the same coloured line, and is held honest by TestNoSuppressionUnderQuietArrivesBeforeItsExemption, a walk over the shipped source that fails the moment a file reads the flag while no writer under internal/cli consumes finding.HonestyDisclosure. Both branches of that walk were measured, not assumed: reading the flag in output.go failed the test naming internal/cli/output.go, and adding an internal/cli reference to the interface made it pass, both reverted afterwards. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal is unchanged at Killed 461, Lived 8, efficacy 98.29 percent, with the same three known timeouts and no new survivor.
Out of scope: the exempt writer for the seven honesty disclosures is quiet-honesty-exemptions, repository detection itself is repository-detection, and §12.4's hint field is output-error-hints.

tasks.title: Exempt honesty disclosures from quiet
tasks.acceptance:
- --quiet suppresses informational messages but never an honesty disclosure. The seven exemptions of §11.1 are always printed: the disabled and unavailable axes of §4.5.4, the probe cap of §5.6.4, the forcing counts of §6.3.2, the waiver and duplicate counts of §10.1.6, the sandbox recreation notice of §5.1.6, the stale-round report of §9.3.2, and the comment cap of §1.6.2.
- The exemption is enforced by routing disclosures through a dedicated writer that ignores --quiet, not by remembering to check a flag at each call site.
- A test runs each of the seven situations under --quiet and asserts the disclosure still appears.
- §11.1's always-printed list is 'every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run', matching §8.4.3, §10.1.3, and §10.2 verbatim.
tasks.closed_reason:
- --quiet now suppresses the one informational message cr writes, a test run's live echo to stderr in `cr test` and `cr probe run` (internal/cli/output.go informational, used in test.go and probe.go), and never a disclosure; TestQuietSuppressesTheLiveRunOutputAndNotTheDisclosure shows the runner's output present without the flag and absent with it while the 5.1.6 notice stays.
- All seven are printed under --quiet: the lenses of 4.5.4, the probe cap of 5.6.4, the forcing counts of 6.3.2, the waiver and duplicate counts of 10.1.6, the sandbox recreation notice of 5.1.6 and the stale-round report of 9.3.2 render through writer.disclose, and the comment cap of 1.6.2 reaches the reader as `cr post`'s refusal through reportFailure, which is given no flag; dogfooded, `cr status 1 --repo o/r --quiet` on the built binary prints every lens, the 9.3.1 head sentence and both 10.1.6 counts in a terminal and in the JSON honesty field.
- The exemption is structural: writer.disclose reads no flag, quiet is read only in output.go's settle and informational, and TestEveryDisclosureAResultPrintsGoesThroughTheWriter reads every rendering method taking the *writer and fails on a Honesty or Disclosure() outside a disclose or len call; hand mutants making disclose honour quiet, making informational ignore it, and making status print its Honesty itself were each caught and reverted.
- TestEveryHonestyDisclosureSurvivesQuiet runs all seven situations under --quiet through a pseudo-terminal: a complete status round, a tenth probe filling the cap, a draft of an argued record, a merge dropping a waived finding, a first probe recreating the sandbox, a round whose head moved, and the comment-cap refusal.
- spec/0.1.0.md line 1331 already reads "Every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run", the wording 8.4.3, 10.1.3 and 10.2 use, so no spec change was needed, and the lens case of the test asserts the four lenses that did not run on the shipped generic profile.

tasks.title: Implement the six-step text normalisation
tasks.acceptance:
- normalise() applies exactly the six steps of §1.4 in order: decode UTF-8, replace CRLF and lone CR with LF, strip trailing SPACE/TAB per line, collapse every run of SPACE/TAB anywhere in a line including leading indentation to one SPACE, drop leading and trailing blank lines while collapsing interior blank runs to one, and rejoin with single LF with no trailing LF.
- A one-line input normalises to that line with no terminator.
- Invalid UTF-8 fails with exit code 1.
- Normalisation does not case-fold, does not strip punctuation, and does not reorder lines; a test asserts each negative.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/text/normalise.go's Normalise runs §1.4's six steps in the order §1.4 numbers them, each carrying its step number in a comment: step 1 validates UTF-8 over the bytes, step 2 replaces CRLF then lone CR with LF, step 3 trims trailing SPACE and TAB per line, step 4 collapses every SPACE/TAB run including leading indentation to one SPACE, step 5 drops the leading and trailing blank runs and collapses interior ones to one, and step 6 rejoins with a single LF; TestNormaliseAppliesTheSixStepsOfSection14 asserts each step on its own case.
- TestAOneLineInputNormalisesWithNoTerminator normalises the same line as typed, with a trailing LF, with CRLF and with surrounding blank lines to the bare line, and asserts the result contains no LF at all.
- internal/cli/exit.go maps text.InvalidUTF8Error onto ExitValidation and TestTextThatDoesNotDecodeExitsWithTheValidationCode raises the error through Normalise rather than constructing it, asserting exit code 1 through a wrapping error; the check sits before every other step, because []rune and range decoding replace an invalid byte with U+FFFD and would leave nothing to detect.
- TestNormalisationDoesNotCaseFold, TestNormalisationDoesNotStripPunctuation and TestNormalisationDoesNotReorderLines each assert their negative on an input that would visibly break it — two texts differing only in case, two conditions one operator apart, and a permutation of the same three lines — and each asserts the pair still differs afterwards rather than only that the shape looks right.
- FuzzNormaliseHoldsTheInvariantsOfSection14 states all three negatives as one fuzzed invariant, that striking SPACE, TAB, CR and LF from input and output leaves the same string, alongside idempotence and an iff on the UTF-8 refusal; 3.3M executions found no counterexample and gremlins killed 18 of 18 mutants in internal/text with none lived and none uncovered.

tasks.title: Compute truncated normalised SHA-256 hash
tasks.acceptance:
- A normalised hash is SHA-256 over the normalised text, lowercase hex, truncated to the first 16 characters, per §1.4.
- Every hash in the system routes through this one function; a test asserts a known input maps to a fixed 16-character value.
- The function is the sole hashing entry point, so §3.4.6, §7.4.1, §8.3.3, §9.2 and §6.1 cannot drift apart.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/text/hash.go's NormalisedHash is §1.4's normalised hash exactly: sha256.Sum256 over the normal form, hex.EncodeToString for lowercase hex, sliced to hashLength, which is spelled once as 16 because the truncation is the only number the five sections could drift apart on.
- It takes raw text and runs Normalise itself rather than taking text a caller already normalised, which is what makes routing through it true by construction: a signature taking normalised text can be called correctly on text that was never normalised, and the result is still sixteen deterministic hex characters, so nothing local to the caller could notice; TestNormalisedHashRefusesWhateverStep1Refuses shows step 1's InvalidUTF8Error reaching the caller rather than a digest being taken over bytes §1.4 refuses.
- TestNormalisedHashIsTheValueSection14Pins asserts the literal 46d80e6defec6c66 for the fragment every one of the six steps moves, pinned as a constant rather than recomputed, and asserts it is not 0e8cce8b6619337f, the same-shaped value a site that skipped Normalise would produce; TestNormalisedHashAgreesExactlyWithNormalisation ties hash equality to normal-form equality in both directions over the shared corpus.
- TestNothingOutsideThisPackageCanReachADigest walks every non-test .go file under the module root and fails when any package outside internal/text imports crypto/md5, crypto/sha1, crypto/sha256, crypto/sha512, encoding/hex or anything in the hash tree, reading import paths so an alias does not slip past; it bites on a planted crypto/sha256 file and on an aliased hash/fnv one, and two floors keep it from passing vacuously - over ten files scanned, and internal/text still importing crypto/sha256.

tasks.title: Close the axis id set
tasks.acceptance:
- A shared validator accepts exactly intent, correctness, convention, and test, per §1.5.
- Any other value in a profile, role, or rule axis field aborts the command with exit code 3 naming the offending file and value.
- The axis set is closed in v0.1; no configuration layer can extend it.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/axis/axis.go holds the one shared validator of §1.5, where ids is the literal set intent, correctness, convention, test, Valid and Validate read only that literal, and TestValidateAcceptsExactlyTheFourAxisIDs asserts both the exact set IDs() returns and that Validate accepts every member.
- Any other value returns an *axis.InvalidError carrying the file, the field, and the offending value in its message, and exitCodeFor in internal/cli/exit.go maps that error, through any wrapping, onto ExitFile so Execute aborts with exit code 3, covered by TestValidateNamesTheOffendingFileAndValue and TestInvalidAxisExitsWithTheFileCode.
- The set is closed in v0.1 because the ids literal has no registration entry point and IDs() hands out a copy, which the tamper check in TestNoConfigurationLayerCanExtendTheAxisSet asserts by writing to the returned slice and finding the validator unchanged.
- No configuration layer can extend it, and the same test proves it by resolving a global config file and a CR_ variable that each name a fifth axis, then asserting no resolved setting addresses an axis id and that Validate still rejects the name.

Out of scope: the profile, role, and rule schemas that will call axis.Validate are later tasks, so no schema loader or call site was added here.

tasks.title: Create the global state directory tree
tasks.acceptance:
- cr init creates ~/.cr with every path of the §2.2 table: config.json, profiles/, roles/, rules/, repos/<owner>/<repo>/{config.json,roles/,rules/,triage.ndjson,rule-stats.ndjson}, state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/, context/<ISSUE-KEY>.ndjson, waivers/<owner>/<repo>.ndjson, and locks/.
- Paths are derived from one layout function so no command hand-builds a path.
- Running cr init twice is idempotent.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr init creates the §2.2 tree: internal/state/layout.go names every path of the table and Init() creates the global ones (root, config.json, profiles/, roles/, rules/, repos/, state/, context/, waivers/, locks/), while EnsureRepo, EnsurePR, and EnsureContext create the placeholder-bearing paths (repos/<owner>/<repo>/{config.json,roles/,rules/,triage.ndjson,rule-stats.ndjson}, state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/, waivers/<owner>/<repo>.ndjson, context/<ISSUE-KEY>.ndjson) once a command knows the owner, repository, pull request, or issue key; TestInitCreatesTheGlobalTree and TestEnsureCreatesTheScopedPaths assert each one exists on disk, and the built binary was run against CR_HOME to confirm the real tree.
- Paths are derived from one layout function: the state.Layout type joins every path against a single injectable root resolved by Default() from CR_HOME or <home>/.cr, cr init calls only Layout methods, and TestLayoutDerivesEveryStatePath pins all 25 derived paths against the §2.2 table so no command needs to hand-build one.
- Running cr init twice is idempotent: directories go through os.MkdirAll and files through touchFile, which leaves an existing file byte-identical, verified by TestInitIsIdempotent writing a config and re-running Init, by the repeated EnsurePR assertion in TestEnsureCreatesTheScopedPaths, and by invoking the binary's init twice.
Out of scope: internal/cli/root.go still maps every command error onto ExitUsage, so a file failure from cr init exits 2 rather than the §11.2 ExitFile 3; correcting that belongs to usage-errors-exit-two.

tasks.title: Guard against writes inside the repository
tasks.acceptance:
- cr never writes inside the repository under review, with the single exception of git worktree registration metadata under .git/worktrees/ created by §5.1.
- cr never modifies the repository's tracked files, index, HEAD, stash, or any branch.
- A guard test runs a representative command sequence against a fixture repository and asserts git status is byte-identical before and after, apart from the permitted worktree registration.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/norepowrite_test.go fences both routes a write into the repository under review could take, and §5.1.1's .git/worktrees/ exception is left open by name in the behavioural guard rather than by widening the write surface: TestOnlyTheStatePackageWritesToTheFilesystem walks every non-test Go file cr ships and fails any os write call, any aliased os import, and any syscall-level import outside internal/state, while TestEveryPathTheStateLayoutHandsOutIsUnderItsRoot enumerates internal/state's path methods by reflection and requires each to resolve under the state root, so cr's own filesystem writes can only land in ~/.cr.
- TestEveryGitSubcommandCrRunsIsARead reads internal/git's AST, resolves the head of every argument list reaching the runner through slices.Clone, append and the package-level diffArgs, and holds it to an allowlist of diff and merge-base, so the index, HEAD, the stash and every branch stay unreachable, with the sandbox-worktree task named as the deliberate edit that adds worktree — the guard was checked by removing diff from the allowlist, whereupon it named `git diff`.
- TestNoCommandTouchesTheRepositoryUnderReview builds the binary and runs every leaf command of the cobra tree plus --version, --help and each command's own --help with the working directory set to a git fixture holding a commit, a second branch, a stash entry, an edited tracked file, a staged file, an untracked file and an ignored file, then requires git status, HEAD with every ref and the stash, and a SHA-256 manifest of every file in the repository to be byte-identical, holding .git/worktrees/ out as the permitted write and asserting it empty while no sandbox command exists, and TestTheFingerprintSeesWhatGitStatusAloneWouldMiss disturbs each of §2.2's five in turn and requires the fingerprint to notice, showing that a branch created off the current commit and a HEAD repointed at an identical commit both leave git status byte-identical.

tasks.title: Take advisory locks on writes
tasks.acceptance:
- Every write to per-PR state takes an exclusive advisory file lock via gofrs/flock, per §2.3.1.
- Reads are lock-free per §2.3.2.
- A concurrency test shows two writers serialising and a reader proceeding while a writer holds the lock.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every write to per-PR state goes through the exclusive gofrs/flock lock of §2.3.1: internal/state/lock.go makes Write a method on the held *Lock rather than on the Layout, so no writer can reach a file under state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/ without first blocking in LockPR, whose lock file Layout.PRLockFile nests at locks/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>.lock, where it can never collide with the differently named probe lock of §5.6. A released lock keeps its file, because flock binds to an inode and unlinking it would let the next waiter lock a fresh one while the holder still ran, which TestReleasingTheLockKeepsItsFile pins.
- Reads are lock-free per §2.3.2: Layout.ReadPR calls os.ReadFile and takes nothing at all, which is exactly why every write publishes by rename. writeAtomic writes a temporary file beside the target and renames it into place, so a reader holding no lock sees either the previous document or the whole new one, proved by TestALockFreeReadNeverSeesAPartialWrite over 200 rewrites of a 64 KiB document read concurrently by four goroutines.
- TestConcurrentWritersSerialise drives eight goroutines through 25 locked read-modify-writes each and asserts the counter reaches 200, so a single lost update fails it, and TestAReaderProceedsWhileAWriterHoldsTheLock reads the file while a writer holds the lock and fails if that read has not returned within ten seconds. The gate now runs go test -race, changed in one commit across all three places that must agree: spec/0.1.0.tasks.json, TestQualityGateRunsEveryStep and CLAUDE.md.

Out of scope: the per-PR state files of the §2.3 table and the head and round fields of §2.3.3 belong to a later task, as does the probe lock of §5.6.

tasks.title: Create the per-PR state files
tasks.acceptance:
- The per-PR directory holds every file of the §2.3 table: meta.json, claims.ndjson, units.ndjson, mapping.ndjson, posted-index.ndjson, intent-gaps.ndjson, runs.ndjson, threads.ndjson, findings.ndjson, probes.ndjson, coverage.ndjson, transitions.ndjson, and waivers.ndjson.
- meta.json carries PR identity, issue key, profile id, active roles, round index, recorded head, and post_unresolved.
- Each file has a typed reader and writer; no command parses NDJSON inline.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Layout.EnsurePR now creates every file of the §2.3 table — meta.json, claims.ndjson, units.ndjson, mapping.ndjson, posted-index.ndjson, intent-gaps.ndjson, runs.ndjson, threads.ndjson, findings.ndjson, probes.ndjson, coverage.ndjson, transitions.ndjson, waivers.ndjson — named once in internal/state/prfiles.go and asserted in table order by TestEnsurePRCreatesEveryStateFile; creating them is a write to per-PR state, so it happens inside LockPR's exclusive lock (§2.3.1) and publishes through writeAtomic, and TestEnsurePRKeepsRecordedState proves a second ensure never discards a recorded round.
- internal/state/meta.go's Meta carries every part of the §2.3 meta.json row: owner, repo, and pr for the identity, issue_key, profile_id, active_roles, round, head, and post_unresolved, with round 0 documented as a directory no round has been opened in since §9.3.3 starts the count at 1; TestMetaSurvivesARoundTrip asserts all of them survive the writer and the reader, and TestMetaNeverWritesANullRoleList pins active_roles to [] rather than null (§12.3).
- Every file has a typed reader and writer: Layout.ReadMeta and Lock.WriteMeta for meta.json, and the generic ReadRecords, WriteRecords, and WriteStamped for the twelve NDJSON files, which each later schema task instantiates with its own record type. NDJSON is one JSON document per line, an empty file decodes to an empty slice rather than nil, and a line that does not decode is reported by its path and line number.
- No command parses NDJSON inline, because there is no route to a per-PR file that does not pass through these functions: writes are methods and package functions taking the held *Lock, and reads go through Layout.ReadRecords. The head and round stamping of §2.3.3 is a property of the writer rather than of its callers — WriteStamped sets the pair on every record and overwrites whatever it arrived with, WriteRecords refuses one of the eight §2.3.3 files, and WriteStamped refuses a file outside that list, so the four agent-input commands cannot disagree about who owns the fields; a record type opts in by embedding state.Stamp, whose unexported setStamp makes the Stamped interface unimplementable from outside the package. The later stamp-head-round-fields task adds its rejection of an agent-supplied head or round in that one writer. Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh. Mutation testing: gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal gives Killed 125, Lived 2, efficacy 98.43%, above the 98.25% baseline and with no new survivor — the two survivors are the documented internal/config words pair.

tasks.title: Create per-round artefact directories
tasks.acceptance:
- rounds/<n>/ holds draft.md, rendered.json, posted.json, and summary.json, per the §2.3 table.
- The directory is created on demand for the current round index and earlier rounds are never touched.
- A test asserts round 2 artefacts do not disturb round 1.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/state/rounds.go names the rounds/<n>/ part of the §2.3 table in table order, draft.md then rendered.json then posted.json then summary.json, and EnsureRound publishes all four inside one round directory, the three JSON artefacts carrying an empty document rather than the unparseable empty file an NDJSON artefact starts from, with typed access through RoundDir, RoundFile, ReadRound, WriteRound and UpdateRoundJSON, whose read-modify-write shape lets each of §10.3's three writers set its own counts without rewriting the whole document. TestARoundDirectoryHoldsEveryArtefact asserts the set, the order and the initial contents, TestLayoutDerivesEveryRoundPath the paths, TestEachWriterUpdatesOnlyItsOwnSummarySection the accumulation, and TestOnlyTheTablesArtefactsReachARoundDirectory refuses any name the table does not give a round.
- A round directory appears only when that round is first written. EnsurePR opens none, and EnsureRound creates exactly the round index it is handed, under the §2.3.1 lock and through the atomic publish of §2.3.2, leaving an artefact that is already there as it is. No path it composes names another round and the package offers no way to clear or enumerate rounds, so §9.3.5's requirement that a command replacing or clearing a file leaves earlier rounds intact holds by construction. Round 0 is refused on every route in, because §9.3.3 opens the count at 1 and meta.json's 0 means no round has been opened, which TestRoundZeroIsNotARound pins together with the absence of rounds/0 on disk.
- TestASecondRoundLeavesTheFirstIntact fills all four of round 1's artefacts, snapshots them, writes all four of round 2's, and asserts round 1's files come back byte-identical while round 2 holds its own.

tasks.title: Stamp head fields on state records
tasks.acceptance:
- Every record in claims.ndjson, units.ndjson, mapping.ndjson, findings.ndjson, probes.ndjson, runs.ndjson, intent-gaps.ndjson, and coverage.ndjson carries head and round, per §2.3.3.
- Round 8 finding head-round-stamping-unassigned: head and round are stamped by cr on write for every file §2.3.3 lists, and MUST NOT be supplied by the agent. A record arriving with either is rejected with exit code 1 naming the line and the field, exactly as §6.1.4 rejects grade.
- The stamping happens in one shared writer so the four agent-input commands (claims record, map record, cells record, record) cannot disagree about who owns the fields.
- A test supplies head and round through each of the four commands and asserts all four reject.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every record of claims.ndjson, units.ndjson, mapping.ndjson, findings.ndjson, probes.ndjson, runs.ndjson, intent-gaps.ndjson and coverage.ndjson carries head and round per §2.3.3: a record type opts in by embedding state.Stamp, and state.WriteStamped, the only writer those eight files accept, sets the pair on every record on the way out. TestAFileIsWrittenThroughTheWriterItsSchemaRequires pins the routing in both directions and TestDecodedRecordsAreStampedOnTheWayOut reads the stamped pair back off disk.
- Round 8 finding head-round-stamping-unassigned is assigned. Spec §2.3.3 now states that cr writes head and round on every write to the eight files it lists and rejects a record that arrives carrying either, so the authorship the finding found unassigned is written down in the normative document as well as in the code, and state.WriteStamped overwrites whatever a record arrived holding.
- A record supplying either field is refused at decode time on the wire, because §2.3.3 fields arrive inside agent-authored NDJSON and a struct that already decoded cannot report which keys were present. state.DecodeStamped refuses any line whose JSON object holds the key head or round, returning a state.ReservedFieldError that names the file, the one-based line counted over the file as handed in, and the field, and internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto ExitValidation, which is exit code 1 exactly as §6.1.4 rejects grade. The check is presence rather than a non-zero Go field, because an empty head and a zero round are values the agent chose. TestAnAgentMayNotSupplyHeadOrRound covers both degenerate values, a null head, real values, and a record supplying both, and TestASuppliedStampFieldExitsWithTheValidationCode asserts the code survives the wrapping a command adds on the way out.
- The stamping and the rejection live in one shared writer, so the four agent-input commands cannot disagree about who owns the fields: state.WriteStamped is the only function that sets the pair, state.DecodeStamped is the only road from an agent file into it, WriteRecords refuses the eight §2.3.3 files and WriteStamped refuses every other file. cr claims record, cr map record, cr cells record and cr record inherit both behaviours the day each lands instead of restating them.
- Reported rather than faked: none of the four commands exists yet, so no test can supply head and round through them today, and a test against a stub would assert nothing. The rejection is instead implemented and tested at the single point all four must pass through, by three state tests and one cli test covering the presence check, the line number, the field name and the exit code. Gate: go test -race ./... ok, golangci-lint 0 issues, scripts/deadcode.sh clean. Mutation testing with gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal moved from the recorded baseline of Killed 125, Lived 2, 98.43 per cent to Killed 131, Lived 2, 98.50 per cent, with no new survivor. The two survivors remain the documented internal/config words pair, and the single TIMED OUT mutant at state/layout.go:233, where negating the LockPR error check returns early while still holding the flock, was confirmed pre-existing by running gremlins on HEAD~7 in a scratch worktree.
Out of scope: the end-to-end assertion the fourth criterion asks for belongs to the tasks that build the commands, and each must assert that a supplied head or round exits 1 naming the line and the field: claims-record-command, map-record-command, cells-record-command, and finding-required-field-validation, which owns the validation for cr record.

tasks.title: Resolve configuration through five layers
tasks.acceptance:
- Effective configuration resolves at read time in the §2.7 order, highest first: command-line flags, CR_-prefixed environment variables, per-repository config, global config, built-in defaults.
- cr config prints the effective configuration.
- A test sets the same key at each of the five layers and asserts the winner at every depth.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Effective configuration now resolves at read time in internal/config/config.go, where Resolve seeds the built-in defaults and then applies the global config, the per-repository config, the CR_-prefixed environment, and the command-line flags in that order, so the highest layer of §2.7 wins, and any CR_ variable or config key whose name addresses the confirmation gate, the argued forcing, or the question label is rejected naming the decision it would reach, while CR_HOME passes through as the state root rather than a setting.
- cr config prints the effective configuration as pretty JSON keyed by the dotted §2.7 names, wired in internal/cli/config.go and internal/cli/root.go, reading the global config from the state layout and the per-repository config when --repo owner/repo is given, exercised with the freshly built binary against a scratch CR_HOME where the repository layer beat the global layer, 7 over 9, and a protected CR_POST_AUTO_CONFIRM was refused with exit code 2.
- TestResolutionPrefersTheHighestLayer sets post.max_comments at all five layers and strips the winning layer at each step, asserting 30 for flags, 25 for the environment, 15 for the per-repository config, 10 for the global config, and 20 for the built-in default, with TestProtectedNamesAreRejected, TestLayerValuesAreCoercedToTheSettingType, and TestConfigCommandPrintsTheEffectiveConfiguration covering the refusal, the per-layer typing, and the command output.
Out of scope: cr config --resolved and its per-setting layer annotation belong to config-resolved-annotation, so the resolver records no layer origin yet.

tasks.title: Annotate settings with their source layer
tasks.acceptance:
- cr config --resolved annotates every setting with the layer that supplied it, per §2.7.
- The annotation names the actual file path or environment variable, not just the layer's rank.
- A test asserts the annotation changes when the same key is moved between layers.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `cr config --resolved` annotates every setting with the layer that supplied it, per §2.7: internal/config's Resolve now keeps the provenance it already settled, Config.Origins hands it back, and internal/cli's annotated joins it to the values so every key of the plain listing carries a layer.
- Every setting is annotated and not only the overridden ones: the origins map starts with §2.7's lowest layer for each key of the table, so a setting no file, variable or flag touched reports "built-in default" rather than leaving a reader to infer it from an absence.
- The annotation names the actual file path or environment variable, not just the layer's rank: a file layer carries the config.json it read, the environment layer carries the CR_-prefixed variable envName spells, and the two layers that are not a place a reader can open — the built-in defaults and the command line — carry none.
- The flag stopped refusing, so the surface guard changed with it: TestAFlagAheadOfItsBehaviourRefuses became TestTheResolvedFlagChangesWhatConfigPrints, which holds the flag to producing a listing that differs from the plain one and names the file, and notImplementedFor was removed with the refusal it existed for.
- A test asserts the annotation changes when the same key is moved between layers: internal/cli/config_test.go's TestTheResolvedAnnotationFollowsAKeyBetweenLayers writes post.max_comments into the global config, then the per-repository one, then the environment, and reads the annotation after each move, asserting the layer and the source each time.
- The derivation is held at its own level too: internal/config/origin_test.go sets one key in all four layers at once, which separates recording the highest layer from recording the last one read, and adds the two file layers told apart by name and by path, an unknown name annotating nothing, and Origins handing back a copy.
- The measurement behind those tests: dropping the file path from the recorded origin fails four of them across the two packages, and leaves nothing else in the tree red.
- One structural guard was met rather than weakened: internal/role's TestNothingOutsideThisPackageCanNameTheLayerARoleResolvedFrom fences the bare identifier `Layer` to that package for §2.5.5's corpus order, so the new field is `From` with the JSON tag `layer`, and both declarations say why.
- Dogfooded against an isolated CR_HOME and a local scratch repository: with the key in the global config the annotation read {"value": 9, "layer": "global config", "source": ".../.cr/config.json"}; moved to the per-repository file it read {"value": 7, "layer": "per-repository config", "source": ".../repos/qa/shop/config.json"}; set in the environment it read {"value": 5, "layer": "environment", "source": "CR_POST_MAX_COMMENTS"}; and cluster.gap_lines stayed {"value": 12, "layer": "built-in default", "source": ""} throughout. At a terminal the same run printed `post.max_comments = 7  (per-repository config /.../config.json)`.
- Invariant 2 verified by hand: `git status --porcelain` in the scratch repository was empty after every run.
- The gate is green at 6 commits: `go test -race -count=1 ./...`, `golangci-lint run` at 0 issues, `./scripts/deadcode.sh` silent, and `gofmt -l internal cmd` empty.

tasks.title: Reject configuration keys addressing protected rules
tasks.acceptance:
- The confirmation gate of §8.5, the argued forcing of §6.3, and the question label of §8.1.4 are not settings and MUST NOT be readable from any layer.
- cr rejects and reports any CR_-prefixed variable or config key whose name would address any of them.
- The rejection is a deny-list check on key names at read time; a test asserts each of the three is unreachable from an environment variable and from both config files.
- Round 11 finding unprotected-disclosure-channel, assigned here: §2.7's protected list names the gate, the forcing, and the §8.1.4 label but not the §8.1.6 provenance or §8.1.7 evidence regions, though both are the sole channels carrying disclosure and checkability to the author. The implementation protects all five from every configuration layer.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The confirmation gate of §8.5, the argued forcing of §6.3 and the question label of §8.1.4 stay unreadable from every layer of §2.7: internal/config/config.go keeps the whole configuration surface in the settings table, no entry of which names any of them, and TestNoFlagLayerCanIntroduceAProtectedSetting fails the moment a built-in key does, so no config file, environment variable or flag can reach one.
- cr rejects and reports any CR_-prefixed variable or config key addressing one: checkProtected raises ProtectedError naming the variable or key as written and the decision it would have reached, the file layers prefix the path, and internal/cli/exit.go maps ProtectedError onto ExitFile because §11.2 codes a configuration failure 3 rather than a usage error the invocation could fix, proven by TestProtectedConfigNameExitsWithTheFileCode and by the built binary exiting 3 on CR_POST_AUTO_CONFIRM and on a config.json carrying render.evidence_region.
- The rejection is a deny-list check on names at read time inside Resolve, before any value is used: §2.7 refuses a name that would address a decision, which I read as neither an exact key list, defeated by any synonym, nor any occurrence of the letters, which would refuse rules.aggregate_min and blame the confirmation gate for it, so a name is split into its words and a word carrying a token is refused, leaving post.gate_timeout_seconds and post.labels refused, since over-refusing costs a rename while under-refusing costs an implicit network write.
- A test asserts each protected decision is unreachable from an environment variable and from both config files: TestProtectedNamesAreRejected drives seven names through the environment, the global config and the per-repository config and checks the reported name and subject, TestOnlyTheStateRootIsExemptFromTheProtectedScan proves CR_HOME is exempt by equality against one constant and that the exemption grants no immunity because CR_HOME passes the scan on its own spelling, TestNoFlagLayerCanIntroduceAProtectedSetting proves the flag exemption §8.5.2 requires cannot leak into the environment or file layers, and every guard was watched failing with the gate token removed, the forcing token removed, the exemption widened to a prefix and a protected built-in key added.
- Round 11 finding unprotected-disclosure-channel named the gap: §2.7 protects the gate, the forcing and the §8.1.4 label but not the §8.1.6 provenance region or the §8.1.7 evidence region, the two channels through which disclosure and checkability reach the author, so a config key silencing either would have removed the honesty the assertion register rests on.
- The implementation protects all five from every configuration layer: the token table now carries provenance and evidence beside confirm, gate, argued, forcing and label, the package comment records why, TestProtectedNamesAreRejected covers all five across the environment and both config files, and flatten now keeps the key an empty object leaves behind so a name cannot slip past the scan by carrying no value.

tasks.title: Guard that no model client exists
tasks.acceptance:
- Invariant 1: cr never calls a language model. No API client, no model name, no inference.
- A guard test greps the module's dependency graph and source for model provider clients and model identifiers, failing when one appears.
- go.mod carries no model SDK dependency.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Invariant 1 is enforced in Go rather than documented. internal/cli/nomodel_test.go fences the three ways a language model can reach cr — an SDK sitting in the module graph, an SDK inside the compiled closure, and a model endpoint or identifier written by hand — so §2.1.1's reproducibility now has a mechanical reason to hold rather than a stated one, and the register cr asserts in stays backed by what it established itself.
- No API client, no model name, and no inference survives any of the three checks. A constructed client is caught as an import, a hand-rolled call is caught by its host and request path, and a model name is caught by its family prefix, with credential names listed alongside the hosts because they are the same call one step earlier. The scope is what executes, not what is written: prose is deliberately outside, because CLAUDE.md, §1.3.4, §2.1, and thirteen rounds under spec/.tp-review/ are the documents that state the invariant and a repository-wide grep would convict exactly them. §3.1's tracker command and a user's own profile are outside for the opposite reason, being argv the user supplies at runtime, while §2.4.5's built-in profiles are inside, because they ship in the binary and name commands cr runs itself.
- A guard test reads both the dependency graph and the source, failing when a provider client or a model identifier appears. TestNoModelSDKSitsInTheModuleGraph scans go.mod and go.sum as text, which needs no network and catches a transitive module nobody chose. TestNothingCrBuildsImportsAModelSDK scans go list -deps -test ./..., which sees through a dependency in a way cr's own import blocks cannot. TestNoModelEndpointOrIdentifierReachesTheBinary walks every .go file plus the assets they //go:embed, with the guard file excluded from its own surface and a floor on the files scanned so a misresolved root cannot pass vacuously. Each was watched to fail on a real violating input and then reverted: a fake anthropic module appended to go.sum, then that module required and replaced with a local package and blank-imported from internal/cli, then a hand-written api.anthropic.com constant in a .go file together with a gpt-4o string added to the embedded generic profile. The graph guard alone fired for the required-but-unimported case, which keeps the weaker fault distinguishable from the stronger one while still failing it, since the distance between the two is one import line.
- go.mod carries no model SDK dependency. Its require blocks hold cobra, flock, testify and their indirects and nothing else, and that is now asserted rather than observed, proven by appending a fake anthropic-sdk-go line to go.sum and watching the graph guard name the file, the line number, and the matched fragment.
Out of scope: §2.1.2's network-write boundary and §2.1.3's six agent-only judgements are network-write-boundary-guard and agent-only-judgement-guard. The guard does not scan scripts/ or .github/workflows/, which execute in CI rather than inside cr. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal is unchanged at Killed 260, Lived 4, efficacy 98.48% with the one known state/layout.go timeout, as expected from a unit that adds no production branch.

tasks.title: Guard network writes to posting only
tasks.acceptance:
- cr performs no network write except the GitHub calls of §8, and those only behind the §8.5 confirmation gate, per §2.1.2.
- Every outbound call goes through one gh-invoking helper that refuses a write verb unless the caller presents the gate's confirmation token.
- A test asserts a write attempt from any other path fails.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr performs no network write except §8's GitHub calls, and only behind §8.5's gate: internal/gh is the single route out, asserted in internal/cli/nowrite_test.go by parsing every shipped Go file's imports — os/exec appears only in internal/gh/run.go and internal/git/run.go, and no network transport (net, net/http and their neighbours, golang.org/x/net; net/url excepted as parsing only) appears anywhere, so cr cannot address GitHub in process or start gh around the boundary.
- Every outbound call goes through one gh-invoking helper that refuses a write without the gate's token: internal/gh/run.go's unexported invoke is the only exec site, and the two doors above it are asymmetric. Run is the read door, closed by default — it admits only api, judges a GraphQL call by its operation keyword rather than its verb (gh POSTs every query, so the verb decides nothing), and judges a REST call by --method, --input, and the field flags that make gh default to POST. Confirmation.Write is the write door, a method rather than a function taking a token, so no call shape omits it; Confirmation's granted field is unexported and Confirm is its only constructor, so a token composed outside internal/gh is the zero value and writes nothing, and a confirmed token still runs only an api call because §8.3.1 and §8.4.1 need one atomic review that gh pr comment and gh pr review cannot express.
- A write attempt from any other path fails: TestNoWriteReachesGhThroughTheReadDoor refuses seventeen shapes — a verb in each spelling gh accepts, a body from --input, a field with no GET, pr comment and pr review, a mutation, a mutation behind a leading query, and one behind a leading comment — and proves gh was never started; TestOnlyAConfirmedTokenOpensTheWriteDoor refuses a fabricated and an unconfirmed token; TestAWriteFromOutsideTheGateIsRefused asserts the same from internal/cli, where the zero value is all Go can build; TestNothingOutsideTheGhPackageMintsAConfirmation keeps the mint to one site. The guard was proved to bite by making the real ingestion call --method POST and then making threadsQuery a mutation: TestAReadIgnoresTheAmbientGhEnvironment failed on both, and both were reverted.
Out of scope: end-to-end assertion that cr post reaches this door belongs to single-review-batching, dry-run-posting, and confirm-flag-required, which build §8.5's gate and the payload it presents.

tasks.title: Guard the six agent-only judgements
tasks.acceptance:
- The six judgements of §2.1.3 belong to the agent alone and cr makes none of them: whether a rule hit is a real violation, whether a candidate symbol is semantic reinvention, whether a note explains an unmapped unit, whether an existing human thread already covers a finding, whether a unit is covered by tests, and whether a posted concern has been addressed.
- For each, cr locates the candidate, supplies it, and records the decision — and has no code path producing a verdict.
- Every cr command is reproducible given the same state directory, head SHA, and inputs, per §2.1.1; a test runs a command twice and compares output byte for byte.

tasks.title: Define the profile field schema
tasks.acceptance:
- The profile struct carries every row of the §2.4 field table with its required flag: id, match.files, match.globs, axes, sandbox.copy, sandbox.setup, tests.cmd, tests.globs, tests.filter_flag, tests.timeout_seconds (default 900), tests.output_tail_bytes (default 4096), tests.count_pattern, tests.probe_path_template, rules, symbols.lang.
- tests.globs is required when tests.cmd is present.
- A profile is mechanical, language-specific configuration and is data, never prompt text; the struct carries no free-form instruction field.
- A malformed profile file aborts with exit code 3 naming the file and the offending field.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/profile/profile.go carries every row of the §2.4 field table with its required flag: ID, Match.Files, Match.Globs and Axes are required and named individually when absent, Sandbox.Copy/Setup, Tests.Cmd/Globs/FilterFlag/TimeoutSeconds/OutputTailBytes/CountPattern/ProbePathTemplate, Rules and Symbols.Lang are optional, and TestParseAppliesTheDocumentedDefaults proves an omitting profile comes back with TimeoutSeconds 900, OutputTailBytes 4096 and empty lists rather than nil, while TestParseKeepsExplicitOptionalValues proves a set value survives.
- TestTestsGlobsIsRequiredWhenTestsCmdIsPresent proves the conditional row of the table: a tests.cmd with no tests.globs, and one with an empty tests.globs, both abort naming tests.globs, an absent tests.cmd asks for nothing because it disables the test axis, and a present-but-empty tests.cmd aborts naming itself so absent and empty stay distinguishable.
- The struct is mechanical, language-specific data only: every field is a marker list, a glob, an axis default, a shell step, a runner setting, a rule object carried verbatim for §2.6, or a language hint, and nothing is addressed to an agent.
- TestProfileCarriesExactlyTheSpecFields walks the struct reflectively and asserts its dotted json field set equals the fifteen §2.4 rows exactly, so no free-form instruction field can be added without the guard failing; proven to bite by temporarily adding an instructions string and observing the failure, then reverting.
- A malformed profile aborts with exit code 3 naming the file and the offending field: *profile.MalformedError carries File, Field and Problem, exitCodeFor maps it onto ExitFile via errors.As beside the existing axis mapping, and TestParseNamesTheMissingRequiredField, TestParseRequiresTheIDToEqualTheFileStem, TestParseRejectsAnAxisIDOutsideTheClosedSet, TestParseRejectsUnusableFiles and TestMalformedProfileExitsWithTheFileCode cover each fault; §2.4's file-stem rule is enforced, axes keys are judged by axis.Validate as axes.<key> so its own exit-3 mapping applies, and a wrong-typed field is named from the decoder's own path.
Out of scope: profile selection by match.files with its most-markers-wins rule and tie abort, the tests.count_pattern group-arity check, the tests.probe_path_template default, and the laravel-pest and generic profiles are each their own later task and are untouched here. Two validations were added that §2.4 implies rather than states: a non-positive tests.timeout_seconds or tests.output_tail_bytes is malformed, since a run with no timeout budget or no retained output cannot produce the evidence §5 asks of it.

tasks.title: Select a profile by marker files
tasks.acceptance:
- Profile selection is automatic via match.files, and overridable by profile in the per-repository config, per §2.4.1.
- When more than one profile matches, the one with the greatest number of matched marker files wins, per §2.4.2.
- A test covers automatic selection, config override, and the greatest-match rule.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/profile/select.go Select reads the profiles directory and chooses by match.files alone, counting with os.Stat the marker files present in the repository under review, while a non-empty configured value, which is the profile setting internal/config already resolves through the five §2.7 layers with the per-repository config among them, loads that profile by id and consults no marker at all, so §2.4.1's override has one path to the value and a named profile cr cannot read stays a MalformedError mapped to exit 3.
- §2.4.2's greatest-match rule is the count comparison in Select, where a profile matching more markers than the current best replaces the winners, an equal count joins them, and a zero count never enters, so an empty match.files matches nothing rather than everything and the shipped generic profile can never win automatically. On a tie Select selects nothing and returns Tied naming both profiles in ascending id order, the seam the separate profile-tie-abort task turns into the exit-3 abort, because silently picking either one is exactly the failure §2.4.2 forbids and no later layer could detect it.
- internal/profile/select_test.go covers the three: TestSelectionFollowsTheMarkerFilesInTheRepository for automatic selection and for a marker-less profile never winning, TestConfigurationOverridesTheMarkerFiles for the override beating a matched marker, TestTheGreatestMarkerCountWins for the count rule in both directory orders, plus TestATieSelectsNothingAndNamesTheTiedProfiles and TestAProfilesDirectoryIsEitherReadOrReported. Gate green, and gremlins holds at Killed 197, Lived 2 with only the two documented internal/config survivors.

tasks.title: Abort on a profile selection tie
tasks.acceptance:
- On a tie in matched marker count cr aborts with exit code 3 and names the tied profiles rather than picking one, per §2.4.2.
- The generic profile declares an empty match.files and therefore is never selected automatically; it applies only when named by configuration, per §2.4.3.
- Tested with two profiles matching the same single marker file.
tasks.closed_reason:
- §2.4.2's abort now exists: internal/profile/select.go gives Selection an Err that turns a tie into a *TieError naming the tied profiles in the ascending id order Select reports them in, and internal/cli/exit.go maps that type onto ExitFile, the code 3 of §11.2. It is deliberately its own type rather than a *MalformedError, because every tied profile was read, parsed and validated, so there is no file to open and no field to correct, and its message carries the next actionable step, naming a profile in the per-repository config.
- The shipped generic profile still declares an empty match.files and is still never selected automatically, re-checked rather than rebuilt: TestTheShippedGenericProfileIsNeverSelectedAutomatically asserts the emptiness against the file cr writes and that Select chooses nothing, and the new TestTheShippedGenericProfileNeverJoinsATie extends that onto the tie path, where a universal-match reading would abort in exactly the two repository shapes §2.4.4 requires cr to report and carry on from.
- Configuration remains the only route to generic: TestSelectingGenericByConfigurationTakesOutExactlyTwoLenses and TestConfigurationOverridesTheMarkerFiles both still pass, so naming it beats a marker file that would otherwise decide and nothing else reaches it.
- TestATieBecomesAnAbortNamingTheTiedProfiles builds laravel-pest and symfony both marking the single file artisan in one repository and asserts the *TieError names both and is not a *MalformedError, TestOnlyATieAborts holds the abort to the tie alone, and TestAProfileTieExitsWithTheFileCode pins the exit code through a wrapping error. The deciding equality was mutation-checked by hand as well: flipping matched == best to matched != best fails both tie tests, and gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 297, Lived 4, efficacy 98.67 percent with the same four pre-existing survivors and two known timeouts as the baseline.

tasks.title: Disable axes when no profile matches
tasks.acceptance:
- If no profile matches, cr reports the situation and disables every axis that requires one, rather than guessing, per §2.4.4.
- The disabling is reported through the §4.5.4 honesty channel, so it survives --quiet.
- Tested against a repository carrying no marker file.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/profile/none.go answers §2.4.4 for the third state of Selection: Missing returns a MissingProfile naming the test axis disabled per §4.5.2, because a repository with no profile has no tests.cmd to declare, and the convention/reinvention lens unavailable per §4.3.1, because there is no symbols.lang to build a symbol index from. Nothing else is taken out, and that exactness is the rule's other half. §4.5.3 settles the intent axis on an issue key rather than on a profile, §4.2 reads claims and units and asks a profile for nothing, and §4.3.5 leaves the convention axis its rule corpus, whose per-repository and global layers of §2.6 outlive any profile, so reporting any of those as dead would be the guess §2.4.4 forbids, aimed at the review instead of at the language. Falling back to generic would be the same guess, and §2.4.3 keeps it out of automatic selection.
- MissingProfile.Disclosure is the §4.5.4 entry and satisfies finding.HonestyDisclosure, the contract internal/finding/cap.go declares for the writer that will hold the §11.1 --quiet exemption, so the report reaches the reader as a disclosure rather than as an informational message a flag can silence. The text is derived from the Disabled and Unavailable fields rather than written beside them, so the JSON a caller reads and the line a human reads cannot drift, and it names `profile` in the per-repository config as §12.4's next actionable step.
- TestARepositoryNoProfileMatchesDisablesOnlyTheAxesThatNeedOne drives Select over the two shipped profiles against a repository carrying no marker file, asserts the exact two-entry result in both directions, and checks that a selected profile and a tie are not the missing state. TestTheMissingProfileReportIsAnHonestyDisclosure pins the finding.HonestyDisclosure conformance at compile time and asserts every field entry reaches the printed text.
Out of scope: no command selects a profile yet, so Selection.Missing and MissingProfile.Disclosure are test-only on deadcode ./... exactly like Select and Selection.Err beside them. The end-to-end assertion that a run with no profile really skips those two lenses belongs to axis-activation-rules, and the always-printed half belongs to quiet-honesty-exemptions, which builds the exempt writer. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 305, Lived 5, efficacy 98.39%, up eight killed from the 297 baseline. The one new survivor is ARITHMETIC_BASE on the capacity hint in Disclosure, an equivalent mutant that changes how often append reallocates and nothing a test can observe, commented at the site alongside the NOT COVERED report on the constant string concatenation in ReinventionLens, whose mutated form does not compile.

tasks.title: Validate count pattern group arity
tasks.acceptance:
- tests.count_pattern is a regex with exactly two capture groups yielding the executed and failed test counts, in that order, per §2.4.
- Any other group count aborts with exit code 3 naming the profile.
- Tested with zero, one, two, and three groups.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/profile/profile.go validateCountPattern holds tests.count_pattern to §2.4's arity: the pattern is compiled and Go's NumSubexp, which counts capturing groups only, must equal countPatternGroups 2, the executed count then the failed count that §5.2.1 reads out in that order. An absent pattern, spelled as the empty string, stays optional and is not checked.
