- Any other count returns a *MalformedError carrying the file and tests.count_pattern, which internal/cli/exit.go's exitCodeFor already maps onto ExitFile 3, so the abort names the profile file and the offending field per §2.5 item 3. A pattern that fails to compile aborts the same way with its own message, following §2.6.1.2's ruling for cr's other configured regex.
- TestCountPatternMustCaptureExactlyTwoGroups walks the arity from zero to three, accepting only two, and adds the cases that separate parentheses from captures: (?:...) does not count, (?P<name>...) does. TestAnUncompilableCountPatternIsMalformedToo covers the uncompilable pattern and asserts its message is not the arity one. gremlins kills every mutant in the new function.

tasks.title: Define the probe path template
tasks.acceptance:
- tests.probe_path_template determines where a gap probe's file is placed. Its default is <root of the first tests.globs entry>/cr_probe_<probe-id><ext>, where the root is the longest leading path prefix free of *, ?, and [.
- Round 8 findings template-placeholder-syntax-undefined, undefined-template-token, undefined-placeholder and round 9 finding undefined-template-placeholder: <ext> is defined mechanically as the literal suffix following the last wildcard segment of the first tests.globs entry, or empty when it has none. It MUST be resolvable with no supplied test file, since §5.1.6's cleanliness scan resolves the template without one; a profile whose <ext> cannot be resolved aborts with exit code 3 naming the profile.
- The template's placeholder vocabulary is enumerated and closed: <probe-id> and <ext>, nothing else. <probe-id> MUST appear exactly once, as §5.1.6 requires.
- Each shipped profile sets the template explicitly so the result matches its own tests.globs; a test asserts the resolved path for each shipped profile satisfies its own globs.
- A test asserts the §5.1.6 leftover glob — the template with every placeholder substituted except <probe-id>, which becomes * — matches a real artefact path on disk.
tasks.closed_reason:
- tests.probe_path_template now decides where a gap probe's file is placed: Profile.ProbePath in internal/profile/probepath.go returns the sandbox-relative path §5.4.2 writes the supplied test to, substituting the probe id into the template resolved at parse time.
- The default is <root of the first tests.globs entry>/cr_probe_<probe-id><ext>, filled in by probeTemplate whenever the profile leaves the field unset, with probeRoot returning the longest leading path prefix free of *, ? and [ and ending on a segment boundary, and TestProbePathTemplateDefaultsToTheFirstTestsGlob pinning six glob shapes including a rooted one, a wildcarded middle segment, one with no root at all, and a multi-entry list where only the first entry seeds the default.
- probeExt defines <ext> mechanically as the literal suffix following the last wildcard segment of that first entry and returns it empty when the entry carries no wildcard, which the "nothing follows the last wildcard" and "no wildcard at all" cases of the same test pin.
- <ext> is read from tests.globs alone and never from a supplied test file, so §5.1.6's cleanliness scan resolves the template with none in hand, and TestProbePathTemplateVocabularyIsClosed shows it by parsing a template ending in <ext> and getting tests/Feature/cr_probe_<probe-id>Test.php back with no file involved.
- TestProbePathTemplateAbortsWhenExtIsUnresolvable proves both ways <ext> fails to resolve, a glob whose last wildcard is followed by a path separator and an explicit <ext> with no globs to answer it, each aborting as a *MalformedError naming the profile file and the field, which internal/cli maps onto exit code 3.
- The placeholder vocabulary is closed to <probe-id> and <ext>: placeholderToken finds every <...> token and rejects any other, proven over an invented token, a misspelt one and a plausible cousin.
- TestProbePathTemplateNeedsExactlyOneProbeID rejects zero and two occurrences of <probe-id>, because §5.1.6 recognises a leftover artefact by replacing exactly one position.
- The laravel-pest profile of TestShippedProfilesPlaceTheProbeInsideTheirOwnGlobs sets tests/Feature/cr_probe_<probe-id>Test.php explicitly rather than taking the default, and the generic profile ships no runner, so it has no template to set and no probe to place.
- assertProbePathSatisfiesGlobs is that test's property: it matches the resolved ProbePath against every entry of the profile's own tests.globs and fails naming the profile when none of them claims it.
- TestLeftoverGlobFindsTheProbeArtefactOnDisk writes a real probe file at ProbePath("a1b2c3") with a repository-owned test file beside it and asserts that filepath.Glob over LeftoverGlob(), the resolved template with <probe-id> replaced by *, returns the artefact and nothing else.
Out of scope: the laravel-pest and generic profile files are a later task, so the shipped-profile property is stated over profile fixtures here rather than over files on disk, and that task must point assertProbePathSatisfiesGlobs at the real files.

tasks.title: Ship the laravel-pest profile
tasks.acceptance:
- v0.1 ships laravel-pest per §2.4.5, with match.files, match.globs, axes, sandbox.copy, sandbox.setup, tests.cmd, tests.globs, tests.filter_flag, tests.count_pattern, tests.probe_path_template, and symbols.lang populated for a Laravel/Pest repository.
- tests.probe_path_template is set explicitly so the placed probe file satisfies tests.globs and Pest's own discovery finds it.
- tests.count_pattern captures the executed count then the failed count from real Pest output; a test asserts extraction against a captured sample.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/profile/builtin/laravel-pest.json ships the §2.4.5 profile as an embedded file, so cr init writes the reviewed bytes rather than whatever a JSON encoder produces that day: match.files selects on artisan, composer.json, phpunit.xml and tests/Pest.php, match.globs owns the PHP a Laravel repository keeps under app, config, database, routes, tests and resources/views, axes answers all four ids of §1.5 with true, sandbox.copy takes the two untracked paths a git worktree cannot carry (.env and vendor) and sandbox.setup reconciles them with the head under review through composer install, tests.cmd is ./vendor/bin/pest with --colors=never so the recap reads the same on a terminal and through a pipe, tests.globs is tests/**/*Test.php, tests.filter_flag is --filter, and symbols.lang is php. internal/cli/init.go writes every shipped profile through the new state.EnsureProfile, which fills an absent path and leaves an edited one alone, and TestInitWritesTheShippedProfiles asserts the bytes on disk equal the built-in and still load under profile.Load.
- tests.probe_path_template is set explicitly to tests/Feature/cr_probe_<probe-id>Test.php because both halves of §5.4.2 fail on the default. The default roots at the first glob's literal prefix, placing the file directly under tests/, which Laravel's phpunit.xml registers under no testsuite, and the Test.php suffix is what makes Pest collect the file at all. TestTheLaravelPestProbePathSatisfiesItsTestGlobs reads the glob's two literal anchors off the profile itself through probeRoot and probeExt, asserts the placed path carries both, asserts its directory is the registered tests/Feature, and pins the §5.1.6 leftover glob. Pest 4.7.8 on PHP 8.5.9 was observed collecting a file written to exactly this path in a real Pest project.
- The spec repair at 2eaa338 replaced the single two-group pattern with two one-group patterns summed over every match, and the shipped profile follows it: tests.count_pattern sums a count of executed tests and tests.failed_pattern a count of failed ones, each anchored on the recap's own delimiters so a test whose name happens to read '3 passed' cannot inflate either. Executed counts every Collision status whose test body ran (deprecated, failed, warning, risky, incomplete, notice, passed) and omits todo and skipped, which are selected but never executed. Counting them would let a run of nothing but skipped tests report zero failures and hand §5.3.5 the no-test-failed proof a gap finding rests on, so those runs instead match nothing, leave both counts undetermined, and stop §5.3.4 at rung 5, inconclusive, which supports no grade either.
- TestTheLaravelPestPatternsCountCapturedPestOutput asserts extraction against six recap files under internal/profile/testdata/pest, captured from real Pest 4.7.8 runs rather than written by hand, failure diffs and bare line numbers included: all-passing yields 2 executed and 0 failed from a run that never writes the word failed, which is the baseline §5.2.5 must be able to pass, some-failing yields 4 and 1, mixed-statuses yields 6 and 2 from '2 failed, 1 todo, 1 skipped, 4 passed', and no-tests-found, skipped-only and todo-only each leave the executed count undetermined. The test carries §5.2.1's summing arithmetic itself, since running the patterns belongs to count-pattern-extraction.

Closed-task code touched, both forced by the spec repair and both left with meaningful tests rather than deleted ones: profile-schema (internal/profile/profile.go gains tests.failed_pattern in Profile.Tests and the wire shape, and TestProfileCarriesExactlyTheSpecFields gains the row) and profile-count-pattern-validation (validateCountPattern becomes validatePattern, serving both fields at exactly one group, and the arity walk in TestACountPatternMustCaptureExactlyOneGroup moves its boundary from two to one, with TestAFailedPatternIsRequiredBesideTheCountPattern added for the new required-when rule). Neither closure's claim is weakened: the schema still carries exactly §2.4's table and the arity is still enforced, at the number §2.4 now states.

Mutation testing: gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 203, Lived 2, efficacy 99.02%. The two survivors are the documented internal/config words pair at config.go:149 and :152, and the one TIMED OUT is the known state/layout.go case. Every mutant in the code this task added or changed was killed. No new survivor.

Out of scope: the generic profile and the §2.4.2 tie abort and §2.4.4 axis disabling are their own tasks, and the production implementation of §5.2.1 count extraction belongs to count-pattern-extraction.

tasks.title: Ship the generic profile
tasks.acceptance:
- v0.1 ships generic per §2.4.5 with an empty match.files, so it is never auto-selected.
- It declares no tests.cmd, which disables the test axis per §4.5.2, and no symbols.lang, which makes the reinvention half of §4.3 unavailable.
- A test asserts selecting it by configuration produces exactly those two honest disablings.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/profile/builtin/generic.json ships the second profile §2.4.5 requires, embedded and registered in profile.Builtins() so cr init writes the reviewed bytes, and its match.files is the empty list, which §2.4.3 makes the whole mechanism of never being selected automatically. TestTheShippedGenericProfileIsNeverSelectedAutomatically runs Select over the shipped files themselves: a repository carrying no marker selects nothing rather than falling back to generic, and one carrying artisan and composer.json selects laravel-pest. TestV01ShipsExactlyTheTwoProfilesOf245 pins the shipped set to exactly generic and laravel-pest and parses both.
- The file declares no tests block at all, so §4.5.2 disables the test axis on the absent tests.cmd, and no symbols.lang, so the reinvention half of §4.3.1 is marked unavailable rather than skipped silently. It is the first profile to exercise §2.4's conditional requirements in the absent direction and it validates cleanly, tests.globs being required only when tests.cmd is present and tests.failed_pattern only when tests.count_pattern is. axes still answers all four ids of §1.5 with true, because §2.4 makes it the default enabled state while §4.5.1 checks prerequisites separately. Declaring test false would attribute the dead axis to configuration instead of to the missing tests.cmd that §4.5.2 names, and would leave a user who adds a runner to their own copy with the axis switched off in a second place.
- TestSelectingGenericByConfigurationTakesOutExactlyTwoLenses selects generic by configuration in a repository whose marker file names laravel-pest, and asserts the list of lenses the profile alone takes out equals exactly two entries, the test axis on the absent tests.cmd and the reinvention half of §4.3.1 on the absent symbols.lang, with laravel-pest read the same way as a control that yields none. Setting axes.test to false in the shipped file was observed failing the assertion with a third entry, so the exactness bites.
Out of scope: the assertion stops at the profile and the conditions that drive the disablings, because §4.5's activation and the coverage report §4.5.4 requires do not exist yet. Task axis-activation-rules must add the end-to-end assertion that a round selecting generic reports both lenses with their reasons.

tasks.title: Define the role field schema
tasks.acceptance:
- The role struct carries every row of the §2.5 field table: id (kebab-case, equal to the file stem), title, axis, instructions, focus, profiles.
- A role customises the prompt for one axis; cr owns the output contract and a role only supplies persona and focus.
- A malformed role file aborts the command with exit code 3, naming the file and the offending field, per §2.5.3.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/role/role.go carries every row of the §2.5 table as Role.ID, Title, Axis, Instructions, Focus and Profiles, with the id required to equal the file stem and to match ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, and TestRoleCarriesExactlyTheSpecFields walks the struct reflectively and asserts the json names equal the table in order.
- A role customises the prompt for one axis: the axis field is required and goes through axis.Validate, the one §1.5 closed-set judge, so no role can name a lens of its own, asserted by TestAnAxisOutsideTheClosedSetIsRejected.
- cr owns the output contract and a role only supplies persona and focus, made structural rather than stated: the struct has no field an output path or record schema could land in, and checkKeys refuses every top-level key outside §2.5's table by name, with TestARoleFileCannotCarryAKeyCrDoesNotDefine rejecting output_path, schema, record, grade, state and prompt and pinning the deterministic first offender.
- A malformed role file aborts with exit code 3 naming the file and the offending field: role.MalformedError carries File, Field and Problem, internal/cli/exit.go maps it and axis.InvalidError onto ExitFile, and TestAMalformedRoleExitsWithTheFileCode, TestTheIDMustBeTheKebabCaseFileStem, TestEveryRequiredTextFieldIsNamedWhenItIsBlank and TestAFileCrCannotReadOrDecodeSaysWhatItCan cover the field-named and whole-file forms.

tasks.title: Ship four default axis roles
tasks.acceptance:
- v0.1 ships four default roles, one per axis, per §2.5.1: intent-coverage on intent, correctness on correctness, convention on convention, and test-adequacy on test.
- Each carries instructions and focus written for its axis and nothing else; project conventions live in the rule corpus per §4.3.5, never in role prose.
- A test asserts each shipped role names a valid axis and that the four axes are covered exactly once.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/role/builtin holds the four roles §2.5.1 requires v0.1 to ship, one per axis: intent-coverage on intent, correctness on correctness, convention on convention, and test-adequacy on test, each embedded with go:embed and returned by Builtins() in internal/role/builtin.go keyed by role id, the shape profile.Builtins() already ships the §2.4.5 profiles in.
- Each file carries its own lens and no other: intent-coverage measures the diff against the claims in both directions, correctness judges a unit against the claims mapped to it, convention weighs a resembling symbol and the rules attached to the unit, and test-adequacy classifies coverage and asks for an experiment before it asserts, with focus questions phrased for that axis alone and §6.2 and §6.3's register visible in all four.
- No role names a project standard, because §4.3.5 leaves those to the rule corpus of §2.6 and the convention role points its reader at the attached rules rather than listing any, and TestTheShippedRolesGiveALensAndNeverAStandard in internal/role/division_test.go refuses role prose carrying a path, a file name, a code identifier, or a command, which is the shape a standard arrives in.
- TestTheShippedRolesCoverEveryAxisExactlyOnce in internal/role/builtin_test.go parses every shipped file through the same Parse a user's own role goes through, asserts axis.Valid on each axis it names, and fails both when two roles serve one axis and when any of §1.5's four is left unserved.

tasks.title: Eject built-in roles as files
tasks.acceptance:
- cr init --eject-roles writes the defaults as editable files that are byte-identical to the built-ins, per §2.5.2.
- A test ejects and compares each file byte for byte against the embedded built-in.
- Ejecting twice is idempotent.
- Builtins() returns the on-disk builtin/<id>.json bytes, asserted against the file itself: comparing the eject only against Builtins() passes even if Builtins() later marshals a struct, which §2.5.2 forbids.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr init --eject-roles writes the four shipped roles into ~/.cr/roles/ byte-identical to internal/role/builtin/<id>.json, routed through the new state.Layout.EnsureRole so every write stays inside internal/state per invariant 2, and gated on the flag because §2.5.4 reads an unejected role from the built-in layer.
- TestEjectRolesWritesTheBuiltinsByteForByte in internal/cli/init_test.go ejects through the real command tree and compares every written file against role.Builtins() byte for byte, and TestInitWritesNoRoleWithoutTheEjectFlag pins that a plain cr init leaves the roles directory empty.
- The same test ejects a second time over a role edited to {"id": "correctness"} and asserts the edit survives while the other three stay byte-identical, because §2.5.2 makes the ejected file the user's and cr still holds the default in the binary.
- TestBuiltinsReturnsTheFilesOnDisk in internal/role/builtin_test.go reads internal/role/builtin/<id>.json off disk, at a path relative to the package directory go test runs in, and asserts Builtins() returns those bytes and that the directory holds no file Builtins() does not embed, so a Builtins() that marshalled a struct would fail here rather than pass by moving with the eject.

tasks.title: Resolve roles across three layers
tasks.acceptance:
- Role resolution order is per-repository, then global, then built-in, per §2.5.4.
- More than one role may serve the same axis, per §2.5.5.
- A test places the same role id at all three layers and asserts the per-repository copy wins whole.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/role/corpus.go resolves per-repository, then global, then built-in per §2.5.4, and corpus.add is what makes the per-repository copy win whole rather than merge: a parsed Role enters entire or is discarded entire, and no field of any role is read anywhere in resolution, so an override omitting `focus` has none. TestThePerRepositoryRoleWinsWholeAcrossAllThreeLayers and TestTheGlobalRoleWinsOverTheBuiltinOne cover the two pairs of the order, and TestAMalformedRoleAbortsResolutionWhicheverLayerHoldsIt shows a malformed file at either on-disk layer aborting per §2.5.3 rather than resolving to the layer below.
- The corpus is a list and never a lookup keyed by axis, so §2.5.5's more than one role may serve the same axis holds. TestMoreThanOneRoleMayServeTheSameAxis places two correctness roles at different layers and asserts both survive beside the shipped correctness role, and TestCorpusOrderIsLayerThenAscendingRoleID pins the order §6.4.2 reads: resolution layer first, then ascending lexicographic role id, sorted by id and not by file name, with a shadowed id appearing once at its winning layer's position.
- TestThePerRepositoryRoleWinsWholeAcrossAllThreeLayers puts the id correctness at all three layers, the built-in one being shipped, and asserts the resolved entry equals the parsed per-repository file exactly, with the global copy's focus and profiles absent and even the axis taken from the winning file.

tasks.title: Order the role corpus deterministically
tasks.acceptance:
- Corpus order, used by §6.4.2 to pick a duplicate group's representative, is resolution layer first — per-repository before global before built-in — then ascending lexicographic role id, per §2.5.5.
- The ordering is exposed as one function so §6.4.2 cannot reimplement it.
- A test fixes the order for a corpus spanning all three layers with colliding ids.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Corpus order is resolution layer first then ascending lexicographic role id per §2.5.5: internal/role/corpus.go's Resolve appends RepoLayer, GlobalLayer and BuiltinLayer in that sequence and sortByID orders each layer by role id rather than by file name, which was already in place from role-resolution-order and is verified intact rather than rewritten.
- The ordering is exposed as one function so §6.4.2 cannot reimplement it: role.Order(corpus) returns a cmp-shaped func(a, b string) int over role ids, reading positions out of the corpus Resolve produced rather than re-deriving layer and id, with an id no layer resolved sorting behind every resolved one instead of at rank zero, and TestNothingOutsideThisPackageCanNameTheLayerARoleResolvedFrom walks every non-test Go file in the module and fails when any file outside internal/role names Layer, RepoLayer, GlobalLayer or BuiltinLayer, so no other package can see the layer §2.5.5 orders by. The fence was probed both ways and reverted: a role.Resolved layer comparison planted in internal/cli failed it, and a fifth name added to the fenced list failed the staleness floor that requires each name to still be spelled that way inside internal/role.
- A test fixes the order for a corpus spanning all three layers with colliding ids: TestCorpusOrderIsLayerThenAscendingRoleID pins a, a-b, correctness, zz, convention, intent-coverage, test-adequacy with correctness shadowing the built-in from the global layer, and TestOrderComparesRoleIDsByTheirPlaceInTheCorpus sorts the reversed ids through Order and requires the corpus back.

tasks.title: Define the rule field schema
tasks.acceptance:
- The rule struct carries every row of the §2.6 field table: id, title, rationale, axis (default convention), class, severity (default medium), kind (default question), detect, fix, globs, exempt, profiles.
- A rule is one normative statement about how code in a repository must be written; it is data and kept separate from roles.
- A malformed rule file aborts with exit code 3, per §2.6.5.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/rule/rule.go's Rule struct carries all twelve rows of §2.6's table in table order (id, title, rationale, axis, class, severity, kind, detect, fix, globs, exempt, profiles), with applyDefaults filling the three optional scalars from DefaultAxis (convention), DefaultSeverity (medium) and DefaultKind (question) before validation runs, so what is validated is the value the rule actually carries. TestARuleCarriesExactlyTheSpecFields walks the struct reflectively against a literal copy of the table and holds the runtime allowlist to the same literal, TestTheOptionalScalarsTakeTheDefaultsTheTableGives asserts each default, and TestAStatedScalarIsCarriedRatherThanDefaulted asserts a stated value survives.
- One rule is one normative statement, and every row that states it is required and checked. validateID holds id to kebab-case and to the file stem, validateText refuses a blank title, a blank rationale and a class outside §6.1's form, and validateEnums holds axis, severity and kind to their closed sets. TestTheIDMustBeTheKebabCaseFileStem, TestEveryRequiredRowIsRequiredAndMayNotBeBlank, TestTheClassMustBeTheFormSection61Fixes and TestTheAxisSeverityAndKindSetsAreClosed cover each one, and the rationale refusal quotes §2.6 item 4 so the author is told the record from this rule has to be able to quote it.
- A rule is data and stays separate from a role, and the separation is a fence rather than a convention. checkKeys refuses any top-level key outside §2.6's table by name and checkBlocks refuses any key outside detect.pattern, detect.mode, fix.replace and fix.with, both reporting the rejected key under its full path and naming the set they checked against. TestARuleFileCannotCarryAKeyCrDoesNotDefine rejects instructions, focus, prompt, output_path, schema, grade, state and probe, TestTheDetectAndFixBlocksCannotCarryAKeyCrDoesNotDefine rejects five inner keys, and TestTheRefusalNamesTheSetItCheckedAgainst holds each message to the list its check reads. Detect and Fix are pointers so §2.6.1.4 can tell a rule with no detect block from one with an empty one.
- A malformed rule file aborts with exit code 3 per §2.6.5. rule.MalformedError carries the file and the offending field, axis.Validate raises §1.5's own error for a bad axis, and internal/cli/exit.go maps rule.MalformedError onto ExitFile beside the profile and role files. internal/cli/rulefile_test.go asserts the code for a missing required row, an invented key, a file that is not JSON, and an axis outside §1.5, each through a wrapping error as a command would raise it.

Out of scope: internal/cli/exit.go belongs to the closed exit-code-constants task and took the two-line import plus one mapping branch that the exit-code criterion requires, and nothing else. deadcode ./... rises from 92 to 104 entries, all twelve in internal/rule, because the package is test-only until rule-layer-resolution and the cr rules commands call it, which is the wiring those tasks own.

tasks.title: Resolve rules across three layers
tasks.acceptance:
- Rules resolve in layers, highest first: per-repository, then global, then the resolved profile's rules array, per §2.6 item 1.
- A rule id is unique after resolution; a lower layer carrying the same id is overridden whole, never merged field by field, per §2.6 item 2.
- A test asserts a lower-layer rule's untouched fields do not survive into the winning record.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/rule/corpus.go Resolve returns one repository's rule corpus in the order of §2.6 item 1, reading the per-repository rules directory first, then the global one, then the resolved profile's rules array carried verbatim by §2.4, with each layer ascending by rule id because §2.1.1 requires the same inputs to give the same result and a directory listing is the operating system's order. TestRulesResolveInLayersHighestFirst asserts the sequence and the layer each rule resolved from.
- A rule id is unique after resolution because corpus.add records every id it has taken and appends a lower layer's rule only when no higher layer claimed it, and the override is whole rather than field by field because a rule reaches the corpus only through that one append of an entire parsed Rule and no field of any rule is read anywhere in resolution. Two elements of a single profile carrying one id are refused as malformed rather than resolved, since §2.6 item 2 settles a collision between layers and leaves none inside one.
- TestALowerLayersUntouchedFieldsDoNotSurviveIntoTheWinner furnishes the losing rule with a value in every optional row of §2.6's table, an axis, a severity, a kind, both blocks and all three lists, and then asserts the winner equals the winning file parsed with no other layer in sight. That equality is the assertion rather than a list of fields, because a field-by-field list defends the fields it names and passes a merge that leaks any other.
- internal/rule/rule.go parts a rule file from a rule embedded in a profile, which differ in exactly one requirement of §2.6, the id equalling the file stem. Parse delegates to a shared parse told which of the two it is reading, so an embedded rule is held to every other row of the table and reports its faults against the profile file and its array position.
- The layer type is named Source rather than Layer because internal/role fences the Layer identifiers to itself so that §6.4.2 cannot rebuild §2.5.5's corpus order instead of calling role.Order, and that fence reads identifiers rather than types.
- Run against a real CR_HOME tree with a global rule carrying a detect block, a fix, a critical severity, globs, exempt and profiles, and a per-repository rule of the same id stating only the required rows. The resolved corpus held one entry from the repository layer with no detect, no fix, empty lists and the §2.6 defaults, so nothing of the shadowed rule survived.
- Gate green at go test -race ./... and golangci-lint run with zero issues and scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Carry rule id onto records
tasks.acceptance:
- Every record produced by a rule carries the rule id, per §2.6 item 3.
- The id is carried on the record itself, separately from any citation, per §2.6.1.3.
- A test asserts a rule-produced record round-trips its rule id through merge and record.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every record produced by a rule carries the rule id. internal/finding/attribution.go's ruleAttributed reads the two fields that say a rule stands behind a record — §2.6.2.4's `suggestion_origin: rule` and §6.2.5's `origin: rule` on a citation — and checker.ruleAttribution refuses such a record when `rule` is absent, with the RejectedRecordError §6.1.3 gives every record fault and §11.2 codes 1. It runs at finding.Decode's door, so `cr record` and the `cr merge` merge-command builds are held to it alike rather than one of them. Only the suggestion mark can be true on arrival, because §6.1.4 rejects a citation supplied with any origin at all; the citation half starts biting when citation-origin-stamping lands §6.2.5's stamping, and reading both here is what keeps that from needing a second copy of §2.6 item 3 elsewhere. An id nothing produced is deliberately not refused here: §6.2.5 answers a forged id by stamping origin positionally from rule-stats.ndjson rather than from the id the record supplied, so a forgery buys nothing instead of being caught.
- The id is carried on the record itself, separately from any citation. checker.citationCarriesNoRule refuses a citations entry supplying `rule`, naming the entry by its index, and internal/rule's Hit.Citation emits path, line and origin and nothing else. The entry is refused rather than quietly ignored because a silently dropped key is still a second copy of the id sitting in a file a human reads, free to disagree with the record carrying it — and §6.2.5 matches a citation to a hit on head, rule id, path and line together, so the copy would be one quarter of a match with two possible answers. TestTheCitationTypeHoldsNoRuleID closes the other half by reading finding.Citation's own wire names against §6.1's four-field list, since a field on the struct would be filled by cr's code and never appear on a wire line.
- A test asserts a rule-produced record round-trips its rule id through merge and record. internal/cli/ruleid_test.go builds two per-role fan-out files whose records share §6.4.1's dedup key and both name the same rule, runs the merge §6.5.1 describes through the machinery merge-command will call — finding.DecodePerRole per file, then finding.MarkDuplicates under role.Order over the resolved corpus — writes the merged file, runs `cr record` against it, and reads findings.ndjson back. Both records keep the id, the suppressed duplicate included, which is the one a merge is likeliest to lose it on because §6.4.3 keeps it deliberately. The command `cr merge` itself is a registered stub owned by merge-command, so the test drives its machinery rather than claiming a command that does not run; the merged file it writes strips §2.3.3's head and round, because state.Stamp carries neither with omitempty and state.DecodeStamped refuses a wire line supplying either — a step merge-command will have to make for the same reason. Dogfooded against the built binary: both refusals exit 1 naming the line and the field.

tasks.title: Make rule rationale quotable to authors
tasks.acceptance:
- A record produced by a rule can quote the rule's rationale, so the author learns the standard and not only the violation, per §2.6.4.
- The rationale reaches the reader through the §8.1.6 provenance region rather than through agent prose.
- A test asserts the rationale text survives from the rule file to the rendered comment.
- §8.1.6 cites §2.6 item 4 for the rationale. §2.6 is the only section carrying both a numbered list and subsections, so §2.6.<n> would otherwise resolve to a heading that does not hold the cited obligation.
- When the rule's rationale cannot be read at draft time, cr says so rather than drawing the provenance region without it. Found by mutation testing on 2026-09-11: with the provenance guard inverted the draft drew rule: no-panic and no rationale line, and raised nothing. The same output arises in practice if the rule file is removed or renamed between cr record and cr draft. 2.6 item 4 has every rule-produced record able to quote its rationale, so a region silently missing it is the one outcome not acceptable; refuse the draft naming the rule and the record, or disclose the missing rationale in the region, whichever 2.6 item 4 and 8.1.6 support.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A record produced by a rule quotes the rule rationale: draft.Provenances.of fills render.Provenance.Rationale from the round corpus (cli/provenance.go draftProvenances), and render.ProvenanceRegion writes `rule: <id>` then `rationale: <text>`, per §2.6 item 4; dogfooded in a scratch repo, the drafted f1 block reads "rule: no-panic / rationale: A panic in a library takes down every caller's process."
- The rationale reaches the reader only through the cr-owned §8.1.6 provenance region, regenerated by draft.commentOf, the single renderer that draft.Render and draft.PostBodies both call, and never through the agent body, which carries only summary and evidence.
- TestARuleOriginCitationReachesTheDraftNamingTheRuleAndItsRationale and TestARoundCitingOnlyARuleHitStillQuotesTheRulesRationale take the rationale from panicRule written to the global rule file, run cr rules check, cr record and cr draft, and assert the rendered block's provenance region carries it verbatim.
- §8.1.6 in spec/0.1.0.md already reads "the rule id with its `rationale` per §2.6 item 4", and every code comment citing the obligation (draft/provenance.go, cli/provenance.go, render/provenance.go, rule/rule.go) cites §2.6 item 4 rather than a §2.6.<n> subsection.
- §2.6 is the section carrying both the numbered list and subsections, so the item form is the one that resolves to the cited obligation; no §2.6.4 citation exists in the tree.
- When the rationale cannot be read at draft time, draft.Provenances.of now returns draft.MissingRationaleError naming the record and the rule instead of drawing the region without the line, and cli/exit.go maps it to exit 3 with a hint to restore the rule (`cr rules list` shows the corpus).
- The 2026-09-11 mutation is reproduced by hand: with the refusal condition disabled, TestARuleCitationWhoseRationaleIsGoneIsRefusedNamingTheRecordAndRule (draft) and TestADraftWhoseRuleFileWasRemovedRefusesNamingTheRecordAndRule (cli) both go red, and both pass with it restored.
- The removed-or-renamed case is the cli test: the rule file is deleted between cr record and cr draft, and the draft exits 3 naming f1 and "no-panic" and leaves draft.md empty; dogfooded, `cr draft 1` and `cr post 1` both exit 3 with that error once no-panic.json is moved away, and post renders the rationale again once it is restored.
- §2.6 item 4 makes a region silently missing its rationale unacceptable, and refusal is the outcome both it and §8.1.6 support: the region is template substitution of stored values, so a cr-composed "rationale unavailable" line would put cr prose into a body render.lang governs, and the refusal follows the existing MissingProbeError precedent for §8.1.7.
- The refusal names both the rule and the record in its message, as the acceptance asks.

tasks.title: Detect only over right-side changed lines
tasks.acceptance:
- A rule carrying a detect block is evaluated mechanically by cr over the added and modified RIGHT-side lines of the diff only — never over removed lines, and never over the whole repository, per §2.6.1.1.
- globs narrow the paths a rule applies to and exempt excludes paths for legacy areas.
- A test asserts a pattern matching a removed line and a pattern matching an unchanged repository line both produce no hit.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/rule/detect.go Evaluate is §2.6.1.1's mechanical evaluation, and it holds the scope structurally in two ways. Its parameters are matchers and hunks, so there is no repository root, no head and no path to open, which means a pattern matching an unchanged repository line cannot reach it at all. Inside a hunk it skips every changed line whose side is not RIGHT, so the removed lines a deletion hunk carries on §9.2's LEFT are never evaluated, and a unified diff has no marker for a modification so the added RIGHT-side lines internal/git collects are exactly the added and modified lines the section admits.
- Rule.Applies reads §2.6's globs and exempt rows for one repository-relative path, asking exempt first because excluding is what that row means and the other order would enforce a rule against the legacy area its author wrote the row to keep out. An empty globs list means all source, which is the opposite reading from §2.4's tests.globs, so both are asserted rather than inferred from each other. The matcher itself is the new internal/glob package, moved whole out of internal/profile so that app slash star star reads the same way in a profile and in a rule by construction.
- TestDetectEvaluatesOnlyTheAddedAndModifiedRightSideLines runs on a real unified diff parsed by git.ParseHunks whose context line, removed line and added line all match the same pattern, and asserts exactly one hit on the added line. TestARemovedLineProducesNoHit uses a deletion-only hunk, requires that the parse really made it LEFT-sided before concluding anything, and asserts no hit. TestDetectionCanReadNothingButTheDiff reads detect.go's own import list and pins it at regexp, internal/git and internal/glob, so a package able to open a file fails the guard rather than a later comment landing on untouched code.
- TestGlobsNarrowThePathsARuleAppliesTo covers no globs, a covering glob, a glob over another tree and one of several. TestExemptExcludesAPathThatGlobsSelected asserts the legacy tree inside the rule's own globs produces nothing while the rest of the same globs still does, so the exemption is a hole rather than a switch.
- Compiling detect.pattern is left outside as §2.6.1.2's obligation. A Matcher arrives already compiled, so detection can never silently pass over a rule whose pattern was unusable, because it never receives one.
- Dogfooded over a real diff of this repository taken with the pinned git flags, five hunks and thirty nine RIGHT-side lines. A rule scoped to the test glob returned four hits, a rule over the same tree exempting that glob returned the four complementary ones, and a pattern present on an unchanged context line of the diff returned none.
- Gate green at go test -race ./... and golangci-lint run with zero issues and scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Compile detect patterns as Go regexp
tasks.acceptance:
- detect.pattern is a regular expression in Go regexp syntax and detect.mode is regex in v0.1, per §2.6.1.2.
- A pattern that fails to compile aborts with exit code 3, naming the rule.
- Any detect.mode other than regex aborts with exit code 3.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/rule/compile.go Compile reads detect.mode against the ModeRegex constant and compiles detect.pattern with Go's regexp package, so §2.6.1.2's two requirements are held in one place and every Matcher handed to §2.6.1.1's evaluation carries a pattern that compiled. TestCompileProducesTheRulesOwnPattern asserts the compiled pattern is the rule's own by matching a line it should catch and one it should not.
- A pattern that fails to compile returns a rule.MalformedError naming the rule id, the field detect.pattern and the file the rule is written in, which internal/cli/exit.go already maps onto ExitFile. TestAPatternThatDoesNotCompileAbortsNamingTheRule pins the field and the id, and internal/cli/rulepattern_test.go asserts exitCodeFor gives the file code both bare and wrapped. TestTheAbortNamesTheFileTheRuleIsWrittenIn checks the named file per layer, a rule file naming itself and an embedded rule naming its profile.
- Any detect.mode other than regex returns the same error type on the same code, covered by TestAModeOtherThanRegexAborts over glob, literal, substring, REGEX, Regex, a leading space and the empty string. The upper and mixed case rows are there because a value accepted case-insensitively would make the closed set larger than the one word the section wrote.
- A blank mode is refused rather than defaulted, and that decision is written into the constant's comment. §2.6's table gives axis and severity and kind a default in the table itself and gives mode none, because §2.6.1.2 states the requirement in the section that runs the pattern instead. Reading regex into a blank mode would be cr choosing a semantics for a detector its author never finished describing, which is right today and wrong the first time a second mode exists.
- The mode is read before the pattern, asserted by TestAnUnsupportedModeIsReportedBeforeThePatternIsRead. A block declaring a mode cr does not have is a block whose pattern cr has no way to read, so compiling first would report a pattern valid in another dialect as a broken regular expression.
- internal/rule/corpus.go now records the file each resolved rule was read from, which the abort needs to name one. That closed a gap the previous task left, where Resolved's own comment claimed §2.6.3 could say which file a dead rule is written in while carrying only the layer and the id.
- Dogfooded against real rule files under an isolated CR_HOME. A good rule compiled and produced eight hits over a real diff of this repository, a rule with a blank mode reported detect.mode of rule prefer-value-objects is empty and §2.6.1.2 admits only regex in v0.1, and a rule with an unparseable pattern reported detect.pattern of rule handle-every-error is not a Go regexp with Go's own parse error, each naming its file.
- Gate green at go test -race ./... and golangci-lint run with zero issues and scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Record a hit as citation
tasks.acceptance:
- A hit is recorded as a citations entry per §6.1 carrying the matched path, line, and origin: rule, which grades the record cited per §6.2, per §2.6 item 1.3.
- The rule id is carried separately on the record per §2.6 item 3, not inside the citation.
- A test asserts a hit produces a citation whose origin cr stamped, never one the agent supplied.
- §2.6.1.3 says a hit may grade the record cited per §6.2 — not that it does, since §6.2 now excludes the test axis.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/rule/citation.go Hit.Citation renders one §2.6.1.1 hit as the §6.1 citations entry §2.6.1.3 requires, carrying the matched path, the matched line and origin rule and nothing else. TestAHitBecomesACitationCarryingPathLineAndRuleOrigin asserts the whole struct rather than field by field. No content hash is written, because §6.2.3 has cr compute and store that at record time against the head the record is being written for, and §6.2's cited row reads its presence as the mark of an entry cr actually resolved.
- The rule id is left out of the citation and belongs on the record's own rule field per §2.6 item 3. TestTheRuleIDIsCarriedOnTheRecordAndNotInTheCitation walks the citation reflectively rather than naming its fields, so a rule key added to §6.1's citation shape later fails there. §6.2.5 matches a citation to a hit by head and rule id and path and line together, so an id inside the citation would be a second copy of one of the four halves of that match, able to disagree with the record carrying it.
- TestTheOriginIsStampedByCrAndCannotBeSupplied asserts the signature and not only the value. Citation takes nothing but the receiver, so there is no parameter through which an agent could supply an origin, and the only way to obtain a rule-origin citation is to have run detection and be holding its Hit. That matters because §6.2.5 rejects a record arriving with any origin at all, and because origin rule is what buys §6.2's cited row for a citation inside the record's own unit.
- TestARuleCitationMayGradeCitedRatherThanDoes gives one citation four fates through finding.ComputeGrade. It grades cited on the convention axis once cr has stamped the content hash, and argued on the test axis, argued before cr resolved it, and argued on an axis cr never computed. The test axis row is the one §2.6.1.3 is misreadable about, since §4.4.2 has a test-adequacy finding assert only with an experiment.
- Dogfooded the whole chain against an isolated CR_HOME and a real diff of this repository. One rule file resolved, compiled to one matcher, produced one hit, and serialised to the citation path internal slash rule slash detect_test.go line 52 with origin rule and no other key. The same record then graded cited on convention and argued on test, and argued again before the hash was stamped.
- A full mutation run over internal with a timeout coefficient of five and four workers reported 1387 killed, 25 lived, 138 not covered and 9 timed out. Two survivors fell in code this unit wrote. The arithmetic on the capacity hint in Resolve is equivalent, confirmed by applying the mutation by hand and watching the suite stay green, and the same line survives in internal/role where the pattern was taken from. The negation on MalformedError.Error was a real gap, so internal/rule/message_test.go now asserts both sentence shapes and the reachable field-less case a profile's rules array produces, and inverting the branch by hand fails it.
- Gate green at go test -race ./... and golangci-lint run with zero issues and scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Inject detect-less rules into prompts
tasks.acceptance:
- A rule without a detect block is injected into its axis role's prompt as text, and any record it produces is graded normally per §6.2, per §2.6.1.4.
- The injection reaches the prompt through §4.6.1's fan-out, not through the role's own instructions file.
- A test asserts a detect-less rule's title and rationale appear in the emitted prompt.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A rule without a detect block is injected into its axis role's prompt as text, and any record it produces is graded normally per §6.2. internal/rule/injection.go's Injected returns every resolved rule of one axis carrying no detect block, in §2.6 item 1's corpus order, and Resolved.Injection renders one as the text §2.6.1.4 puts into the prompt. It is Compile's other half, and TestEveryResolvedRuleIsEitherCompiledOrInjected holds the two to being exhaustive and disjoint, so no rule can fall between them and be enforced by neither while the coverage report says the axis ran. Normal grading is a property of what the injection withholds rather than of a rule applied later: a detect-less rule compiles to no matcher, so §2.6.1.1 records no hit and §6.2.5 has nothing to stamp origin rule against, and the text names no path and no line for a citation to be built out of. TestAnInjectedRuleHandsTheRecordNoEvidence asserts both halves.
- The injection reaches the prompt through §4.6.1's fan-out, not through the role's own instructions file. TestTheRolePackageCannotReadARule reads the imports of every file under internal/role and refuses one that names internal/rule, so the other route is closed by construction rather than by nobody having taken it. TestEjectingRolesCarriesNoRuleText runs cr init, plants a detect-less rule in the state tree, ejects the roles and asserts every file is the built-in byte for byte with neither the title nor the rationale in it. That is the case worth running: §2.5.2 forbids overwriting an ejected role, so a standard folded into one on eject day would be frozen there, unreachable by an edit to the rule, by §2.6 item 2's layering and by §2.6.3.4's dead-rule report. TestNoBuiltinRoleCarriesARuleAsProse closes the shipped corpus against the same mistake.
- A test asserts a detect-less rule's title and rationale appear in the emitted prompt. TestTheInjectedTextCarriesTheTitleAndTheRationale asserts both, and alongside them the rule id §2.6 item 3 requires every record from the rule to carry, the resolved path §2.6 item 2 makes the answer to which layer won, and the class, severity and kind §2.6's table gives records from the rule. It asserts them of what Injected hands the fan-out and not of a rendered prompt, because §4.6.1's emission is review-prompt-emission's and cr review is a registered stub in this build. This is the shape testadequacy.Attach and PerUnit already take for §4.4.1's half of the same prompt, and deadcode ./... lists Injected and Resolved.Injection as test-only for the same reason it lists those two: the task that wires them is review-prompt-emission.

tasks.title: Drop hits the agent never confirms
tasks.acceptance:
- Detection reports hits, never verdicts. A hit reaches a draft only when the agent explicitly confirms it; an unconfirmed hit is dropped, not posted, per §2.6.1.5.
- Confirmation is what a rule cannot supply for itself, so no detect block buys the assertion register of §6.3 on its own.
- A test runs detection producing three hits, has the agent confirm one, and asserts two never reach findings.ndjson.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Detection reports hits, never verdicts: cr rules check <pr> is built in internal/cli/rulescheck.go, resolves the round's rule corpus, evaluates it over the round's diff at the recorded head, attaches each hit to its unit per §4.3.6, and prints round, head, hits and units with no kind, severity or grade (rule.Hit gained JSON tags rule, path, line, text); it moved from the stub tables to the built ones in surface_test.go, norepowrite_test.go and output_test.go, and refuses an unbriefed pull request with exit 4 naming cr brief.
- A hit reaches a draft only when the agent explicitly confirms it by writing a record naming the rule and citing the matched line, which cr record stores; cr rules check writes no record at all, so findings.ndjson, the only thing §7.1 drafts from, holds only what the agent wrote.
- An unconfirmed hit is dropped, not posted, per §2.6.1.5, because nothing in cr turns a hit into a record: TestNothingInTheRulePackageMakesARecord proves from the AST that internal/rule holds no finding.Finding literal, no new of it and no function returning one, and it was verified to fail on a planted violation.
- Confirmation is what a rule cannot supply for itself, so no detect block buys the assertion register of §6.3 on its own: TestAHitCarriesNoVerdictWhateverItsRuleDeclares runs detection twice with a rule declaring kind finding and severity critical and asserts each hit object carries exactly rule, path, line and text and findings.ndjson stays empty.
- A test runs detection producing three hits, has the agent confirm one, and asserts two never reach findings.ndjson: TestTwoOfThreeHitsTheAgentNeverConfirmsNeverReachFindings runs cr rules check over a real checkout adding three panics on lines 4, 5 and 6, records one confirming record through cr record, and asserts findings.ndjson holds that one record and no stored record anchors or cites lines 5 or 6.

tasks.title: Append rule events idempotently to ledger
tasks.acceptance:
- Every hit, record, and dismissal is appended to rule-stats.ndjson with the rule id, the matched path and line, the round, and the head, per §2.6.1.6. The path and line are load-bearing: §6.2.5 matches a citation against this file positionally, and a rule id alone would let any citation claim any hit.
- Round 8 finding cross-pr-round-ordering-undefined: each entry also carries pr and a UTC timestamp, so entries can be grouped by pull request and ordered across pull requests — round indices are per-PR and carry no repository-wide meaning on their own.
- Round 9 finding rule-stats-event-producer: events are keyed by (rule id, path, line, round, head, event type) and overwritten rather than appended on re-run, mirroring §7.3.1's idempotency, so running cr rules check and cr review in the same round cannot double-count a hit.
- Round 9 finding rule-stats-event-producer: cr record is named as the producer of a dismissal event, writing one per current-round hit that no recorded record cites — the observable moment §2.6.1.5's drop otherwise lacks.
- A test runs detection twice in one round and asserts the ledger holds one entry per hit, not two.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every hit, record, and dismissal is appended to rule-stats.ndjson with the rule id, the matched path and line, the round, and the head, per §2.6.1.6: internal/rule/stats.go's Stat carries rule, path, line, event, pr, round, head and at; cr rules check writes a hit entry per hit through rule.RecordHits, and cr record writes a record entry at the anchor of every stored record naming a rule and a dismissal per unconfirmed hit through rule.RecordRecords, all through state.UpdateRuleStats, the ledger's one locked read-modify-write door (TestTheRuleLedgerHasOneWriter asserts rule's update is its only caller).
- The path and line are load-bearing: a hit is confirmed only by a record naming its rule and citing its exact path and line (TestAHitIsConfirmedOnlyByItsRuleAtItsLocation covers the rule at another line, at the same line of another file, another rule and no rule), and TestAHitEntryCarriesEveryFieldTheLedgerIsKeyedAndOrderedBy asserts the whole entry, so §6.2.5 has a positional record to match a citation against.
- Round 8 finding cross-pr-round-ordering-undefined: each entry also carries pr and a UTC timestamp (at, normalised with UTC() and asserted both in rule tests and off the raw file bytes in TestRulesCheckRunTwiceInOneRoundLeavesOneLedgerEntryPerHit), and TestAHitOfAnotherRoundOrPullRequestIsItsOwnEntry keeps entries of other rounds and pull requests apart.
- Round 9 finding rule-stats-event-producer: entries are keyed by rule id, path, line, round, head and event type, with the pull request and record id added to the key because a round index means nothing across pull requests and two records of one rule on one line are two records, and an entry with an existing key is overwritten in place rather than appended, so cr rules check and cr review in the same round cannot double-count a hit; TestAWriteCarriesEveryEntryItDoesNotOwnThroughUnchanged asserts every other entry survives.
- Round 9 finding rule-stats-event-producer: cr record is the producer of dismissal events, writing one per current-round hit that no record of the round cites (read back from findings.ndjson after the append, so an earlier confirmation counts), and it restates the round's dismissals so a later confirmation takes one back (TestRecordWritesTheRecordAndDismissesTheHitsNoRecordConfirms, TestALaterConfirmationInTheSameRoundTakesTheDismissalBack).
- A test runs detection twice in one round and asserts the ledger holds one entry per hit, not two: TestRulesCheckRunTwiceInOneRoundLeavesOneLedgerEntryPerHit runs cr rules check twice over three hits and reads three entries off the file, and TestDetectionRunTwiceInOneRoundLeavesOneEntryPerHit asserts the second run's timestamp is the one kept.

tasks.title: Generate a suggestion from fix
tasks.acceptance:
- A rule may carry fix.replace and fix.with as a regular expression and its replacement, applied to the matched line to produce a suggestion, per §2.6.2.1.
- A generated suggestion passes the validation of §8.2 before drafting; one that fails validation is dropped while its record survives, per §2.6.2.2.
- A test asserts a record outlives its dropped suggestion.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A rule may carry fix.replace and fix.with as a regular expression and its replacement, applied to the matched line to produce a suggestion: internal/rule/fix.go's Matcher.Replacement applies the compiled fix.replace to a Hit's Text with fix.with as the replacement, expanding capture groups through Go's own Regexp.ReplaceAllString, and TestAFixRewritesTheMatchedLineIntoASuggestion asserts the rewritten line while TestAFixWithNothingToRewriteProducesNoSuggestion asserts the three cases that produce nothing.
- fix.replace compiles beside detect.pattern in internal/rule/compile.go, for every rule of the corpus rather than only for one that detects, so a pattern cr cannot run is a malformed rule file under section 2.6 item 5 with the field named, asserted by TestAFixPatternThatDoesNotCompileMakesTheRuleFileMalformed in both the detecting and the detect-less shape.
- A generated suggestion passes the validation of section 8.2 before drafting: Matcher.Suggest offers the generated text to the record only once placeable admits the anchored range under section 8.2 item 1's contiguous RIGHT-side range existing in the diff and section 8.2 item 2's containment in one hunk, and TestAValidatedSuggestionReachesTheRecord asserts the passing case.
- One that fails validation is dropped while its record survives: Suggest returns false and writes nothing on the failing path, leaving the record whole.
- A test asserts a record outlives its dropped suggestion: TestARecordOutlivesItsDroppedSuggestion requires Replacement to have produced text first, so each case is a suggestion that existed and was dropped, then asserts the record compares equal to the copy taken before the call across four section 8.2 failures, and TestADroppedRuleSuggestionDoesNotClearTheAgentsOwn asserts the agent's own suggestion is not deleted by a rule that generated nothing usable.

tasks.title: Never apply a fix to files
tasks.acceptance:
- cr never applies a fix to any file. A fix only ever produces suggestion text for the author to accept, per §2.6.2.3.
- A test asserts the working tree is unchanged after a fix-carrying rule hits.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr never applies a fix to any file: internal/rule/fix.go's Matcher.Replacement is handed a Hit and returns a string, so there is no path, no file opened, and nothing written, and TestTheRulePackageNamesNoCallThatCouldApplyAFix reads the package's own source and asserts it names exactly os.ReadDir and os.ReadFile as an allowlist rather than as a list of forbidden writes.
- A fix only ever produces suggestion text for the author to accept: TestASuggestionIsTextAndNamesNoFileToWrite asserts the record carries the replacement line and no destination, and TestAGeneratedSuggestionDoesNotRewriteTheLineItReads asserts the hit and the hunk it came from still hold what the diff held.
- A test asserts the working tree is unchanged after a fix-carrying rule hits: TestAFixCarryingRuleLeavesTheWorkingTreeUnchanged builds a real git repository, takes the real diff of its head commit, drives the whole path to a suggestion on a record, and then reads the checkout back file by file and through git status --porcelain, which also answers for the index and for a file cr might have added rather than changed.

tasks.title: Stamp machine-generated suggestion origin
tasks.acceptance:
- cr cannot establish that a generated replacement compiles, parses, or preserves behaviour. A suggestion produced by fix carries suggestion_origin: rule, is labelled as machine generated in the draft, and is dropped when the agent does not confirm it, per §2.6.2.4.
- For a suggestion cr generated from a rule fix, suggestion_origin: rule is minted by cr and no function in internal/rule accepts an origin as input. The field itself stays optional on the wire per 6.1, where an agent may supply agent or rule for a suggestion it wrote.
- A test asserts an unconfirmed machine suggestion never reaches the payload.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr cannot establish that a generated replacement compiles, parses, or preserves behaviour, and nothing in internal/rule claims otherwise: Matcher.Suggest writes text and an origin and forms no judgement about either, which is why the origin exists at all.
- A suggestion produced by fix carries suggestion_origin rule: Matcher.Suggest sets record.SuggestionOrigin to finding.OriginRule on the same statement that writes the suggestion, and TestASuggestionProducedByAFixCarriesTheRuleOrigin asserts it.
- A suggestion produced by fix is labelled as machine generated in the draft: internal/draft renders the label above the fenced suggestion block for a record carrying that origin, which is section 7.1.3's own requirement and is closed by draft-suggestion-block, the task that depends on this one, with TestOnlyAMachineGeneratedSuggestionIsLabelled asserting both directions.
- A suggestion produced by fix is dropped when the agent does not confirm it: Matcher.confirmedBy requires the record to name this rule, per section 2.6 item 3, so a record naming another rule or none receives nothing, and a hit no record was written for has nothing to travel on because Suggest is the only function that puts suggestion text anywhere and it is handed a record.
- suggestion_origin is stamped by cr, never supplied by the agent: the value is minted from the matcher rather than read off the record, TestTheRuleOriginIsMintedRatherThanCarriedOver asserts a record arriving with the agent's origin is stamped rule once a fix's suggestion lands on it, and TestNoSignatureInThisPackageAcceptsASuggestionOrigin reads the package's own source and asserts no function takes an Origin at all.
- A test asserts an unconfirmed machine suggestion never reaches the payload: TestAnUnconfirmedMachineSuggestionNeverReachesARecord covers the two record shapes, and TestAHitNoRecordWasWrittenForLeavesNoSuggestionBehind runs a round where two rules hit the same line, the agent confirms one, and the other rule's generated replacement appears in no record that exists afterwards, which is what a payload is rendered from under section 8.1.

tasks.title: Harvest rule candidates from comment history
tasks.acceptance:
- cr rules suggest --repo <owner/repo> scans the bodies of comments posted from recorded rounds and groups them by class and by normalised body per §1.4, per §2.6.3.1.
- A group reaching rules.harvest_min occurrences, default 3, is reported as a candidate rule together with the comments that formed it, per §2.6.3.2.
- A test seeds three matching comments across two rounds and asserts one candidate.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/rulessuggest.go's `cr rules suggest --repo <owner/repo>` scans every pull request under the repository's state root in ascending numeric order, takes every record that reached `posted`, reads the body its round's draft.md carries for it through the new draft.Bodies, and hands the pairs to internal/rule/harvest.go's Harvest, which groups them by class and by text.Normalise's §1.4 normal form — the dogfood run against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1 scanned three posted comments across rounds 1, 2 and 3 and grouped all three although round 3's body differed by an interior whitespace run, a doubled blank line and trailing spaces, and although rounds 1 and 2 carried a `cr:label` region that render.AgentRegion dropped.
- A group reaching `rules.harvest_min` is reported as a candidate carrying the class, the shared normal form, the occurrence count and every comment that formed it: the same dogfood run printed one candidate, `dropped-error` at 3 occurrences with f1@round 1, f2@round 2 and f3@round 3 named and quoted, while the default of 3 left a single posted comment reporting `"candidates": []` and a repository config lowering the threshold to 1 turned that same comment into a candidate, so the layer resolution is the §2.4 one rather than a constant.
- internal/cli/rulessuggest_test.go's TestThreeMatchingCommentsAcrossTwoRoundsAreOneCandidate seeds five posted comments across rounds 1 and 2 of one pull request — three that differ only in what §1.4 collapses, one of another class, one of another wording — and asserts one candidate of three naming f1@1, f2@2 and f3@2, which is the round crossing §9.3.5 would otherwise have hidden.

tasks.title: Report rule candidates without writing files
tasks.acceptance:
- Candidates are reported only. cr never writes a rule file by itself, per §2.6.3.3.
- A test asserts ~/.cr/rules/ is unchanged after cr rules suggest.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Candidates are reported only, and that was verified rather than assumed: internal/cli/rulessuggest.go's newRulesSuggestCmd reads `rules.harvest_min`, scans the posted comments, hands them to rule.Harvest and emits the report, and no path from it opens a file for writing; the result type carries no field through which a rule could be written, and the terminal rendering says so in as many words.
- cr never writes a rule file by itself, per §2.6.3.3, and the guard on that is now one an overwrite cannot pass: TestSuggestWritesNoRuleFile seeds a rule named for the class the harvest reports into both of §2.6's on-disk layers, so a write has an existing file to land on.
- A test asserts ~/.cr/rules/ is unchanged after cr rules suggest: rulesTree walks the global rules directory and the per-repository one and records each file's bytes, and the map is compared before and after the run, so a file added under any name and a file rewritten in place are both visible.
- The strengthening was measured, not reasoned: a `cr rules suggest` made to write `<class>.json` into the rules directory by hand passed the previous paths-only shape and fails the new one on the seeded file's contents; the hand mutation was reverted and internal/cli/rulessuggest.go is unchanged at HEAD.
- Dogfooded against an isolated CR_HOME and a local scratch repository with three posted comments of one class: `cr rules suggest --repo qa/shop` reported "1 candidate rule(s) from 3 posted comment(s), at 3 occurrence(s) or more / unchecked-error: 3 occurrence(s) / Candidates are reported only (§2.6.3.3); cr wrote no rule file", and the seeded ~/.cr/rules/unchecked-error.json kept its sha256 prefix 93261784ad1c12d9 across the run.
- Invariant 2 verified by hand: `git status --porcelain` in the scratch repository was empty after the run.

tasks.title: Report rules dead across recent rounds
tasks.acceptance:
- cr rules list --dead --repo <owner/repo> reports rules that produced no hit and no record across the last rules.dead_after rounds, default 20, so the corpus can be pruned rather than growing without limit, per §2.6.3.4.
- Round 8 finding cross-pr-round-ordering-undefined: the window is defined as the last rules.dead_after distinct (pr, round) pairs ordered by the rule-stats timestamp descending, because round indices are per-PR and PR 7 round 3 is not PR 12 round 3. A rule counts as alive when it produced a hit or a record in any of them.
- cr rules list without --dead reports the effective rules with the layer each came from, per §11.
- A test seeds hits across two pull requests with interleaved timestamps and asserts the window spans both.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr rules list --dead --repo <owner/repo> is built in internal/cli/rules.go: it resolves rules.dead_after through the config layers (default 20, confirmed in dogfood as dead_after=20), reads the repository rule-stats.ndjson lock-free with rule.ReadStats, and internal/rule/dead.go Dead reports every effective rule with no hit and no record in the window, each with its layer and the file to prune.
- Round 8 cross-pr-round-ordering-undefined: rule.Dead groups the ledger by distinct (pr, round) pair, dates each pair by its latest at timestamp, orders pairs by that timestamp descending (then pr, then round, for determinism), and takes the last rules.dead_after pairs, so PR 7 round 3 and PR 12 round 3 are two rounds.
- A rule is alive when a hit or record entry of any window pair names it; a dismissal alone keeps nothing alive (TestARecordKeepsARuleAliveAndADismissalDoesNot), and a ledger holding fewer pairs than rules.dead_after calls no rule dead and discloses why (TestAShortLedgerCallsNoRuleDead), since the silence across that many rounds cannot be established.
- cr rules list without --dead reports the effective rules, after profile scoping, with layer repo, global or profile (rule.Source.String) and path; TestRulesListReportsTheEffectiveRulesWithTheirLayer seeds all three layers plus a shadowed global and asserts each layer and a single no-panic entry.
- TestTheDeadWindowSpansTwoPullRequestsByTimestamp seeds hits on PR 7 and PR 12 with interleaved timestamps at rules.dead_after 4 and asserts the window is PR 12 r3, PR 7 r2, PR 12 r2, PR 7 r3 and that the dead set is exactly no-panic and no-sleep; reversing the sort by hand turns it and TestAPairIsDatedByItsLatestEntry red.

tasks.title: Read intent through a configured command
tasks.acceptance:
- intent.cmd is an argv array with a {key} placeholder, defaulting to ["jira", "issue", "view", "{key}", "--plain"], per §3.1.1 and §3.1.2.
- A non-zero exit fails with exit code 3 and surfaces the command's stderr, per §3.1.3.
- cr carries no tracker authentication code; the tracker is read only through this command.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/intent/run.go reads the issue through intent.cmd as argv: expand substitutes the {key} placeholder into every element that carries it, per element and with no quoting or splitting, and run hands exec.Command the whole array, so a key with a space and a shell metacharacter stays one argument instead of becoming a second command. An argv that is empty, or that carries no placeholder and would therefore read the same issue for every key, is refused as a MalformedCommandError before anything is started. TestTheDefaultTrackerCommandIsTheArgvTheSpecNames pins the resolved default to the five elements of 3.1.2 and expands it, tying the config table entry to the reader that runs it, and TestTheKeyIsSubstitutedIntoEveryElementThatCarriesIt puts a key reading CR-1; rm -rf / through a stub that prints its own argv.
- A non-zero exit fails with exit code 3 and surfaces the command's stderr whole: internal/cli/exit.go maps intent.CommandError and intent.MalformedCommandError onto ExitFile, asserted through the wrapping a command adds by TestAFailedTrackerCommandExitsWithTheFileCode and TestAMalformedIntentCmdExitsWithTheFileCode, and TestAFailedTrackerCommandSurfacesItsStderr asserts both lines of a two-line refusal survive untrimmed and reach Error() alongside the pasteable argv. Nothing summarises the stderr, because cr knows nothing about the program it started and a summary would be cr guessing at a tool it has never heard of.
- cr carries no tracker authentication code: the command authenticates itself, and to make that possible the tracker runner hands it the ambient environment whole, which is where this runner deliberately departs from internal/git and internal/gh. Those pin an allowlist because they are cr's own tools and cr knows which of their variables redirect a read; here the credentials live in variables cr cannot enumerate for a tool it has never heard of, and an allowlist would strip the first one that matters. TestTheTrackerCommandKeepsTheEnvironmentItAuthenticatesWith asserts JIRA_API_TOKEN and JIRA_AUTH_TYPE reach the command. The cost is 2.1.1: a run is reproducible given the same environment rather than the state directory alone, and 3.1.4's --intent-file is where a run needing the stronger guarantee goes.
- The tracker is read only through this command: internal/intent/run.go is the third and last file allowed to start a process, added to the runners list nowrite_test.go confines os/exec to, and the guard over what those files start was extended rather than relaxed. TestTheRunnersStartGitGhAndTheConfiguredTracker now accepts two forms, a plain string literal for git and gh and wholeArgv for the tracker: exec.Command(argv[0], argv[1:]...) where argv is a []string parameter of the enclosing function, with no argument after it. Everything the literal rule rejected it still rejects, and it now also rejects an appended argument and a program taken from a package-level variable rather than from the caller; both were tried against internal/intent/run.go and both failed the guard, which is what keeps a fourth dependency from being smuggled into a runner. Tests need no jira installed: each writes a /bin/sh stub and configures its absolute path as argv[0], which is an ordinary intent.cmd value and touches no PATH.

tasks.title: Bypass the tracker with intent file
tasks.acceptance:
- --intent-file <path> bypasses the command and reads the issue text from a file, so the loop works with no tracker access at all, per §3.1.4.
- A test drives a full brief with --intent-file and no tracker command configured.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/intent/run.go now takes both of §3.1's sources through one entry point: Read(Source{File, Cmd}, key) returns the file's bytes when File is set and never expands, validates, or starts intent.cmd, so TestAnIntentFileNeedsNoTrackerCommandThatCouldEverRun reads an issue with §3.1.2's default argv, with a program that does not exist, with an argv expand refuses, and with no intent.cmd at all, while TestAnIntentFileBypassesTheTrackerCommandEntirely proves the command was not run and its output merely discarded by asserting a stub tracker never touched its sentinel, and an unreadable file fails as intent.FileError, which internal/cli/exit.go codes 3 alongside the command failure it replaced.
- The full-brief assertion is driven at the intent layer rather than through cr brief, which does not exist yet (brief-creates-state, brief-payload, brief-no-judgement and brief-idempotent-at-head are later tasks), and --intent-file is deliberately not registered as a flag because §11.1 fixes exactly five persistent flags without it and command-surface-stubs owns the §11 rows, so the mechanism is in place and the flag lands with cr brief.

tasks.title: Resolve the issue key from sources
tasks.acceptance:
- The issue key resolves from the first source that yields a match, in order: the --issue <KEY> flag, the PR branch name, the PR title, the PR body, per §3.2.
- The pattern defaults to [A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+ and is overridable by intent.key_pattern.
- A test asserts each of the four sources wins in turn when the earlier ones carry no match.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/intent/key.go's ResolveKey walks §3.2's four sources in the order the section fixes them — the --issue flag, then the PR branch, then the PR title, then the PR body — and returns the first non-empty match together with a KeyOrigin naming where it came from, so a later source never wins over an earlier one. The sources arrive as plain strings in a KeySources value rather than being fetched here, keeping resolution beside the {key} placeholder it fills without internal/intent reaching for GitHub.
- The pattern is the resolver's second argument and comes from the configuration layer, whose table already carries [A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+ at intent.key_pattern. TestTheKeyPatternDefaultIsTheOneTheSpecNames pins the resolved default to the literal §3.2 names and extracts CR-123 from a branch with it, and TestAnOverridingKeyPatternReplacesTheDefaultShape puts a #-shaped override past a default-shaped key in an earlier source to prove the override replaces the default rather than joining it. An override that will not compile is a KeyPatternError naming intent.key_pattern, which internal/cli maps to exit code 3, the answer §2.6.1.2 already fixed for a rule's detect.pattern and a profile's tests.count_pattern.
- TestEachKeySourceWinsInTurn runs all four cases with the earlier sources populated but keyless, so a skipped source cannot pass as a working fall-through, and the boundary tests walk the other side: an earlier stray key beating a better-looking later one, a flag the pattern does not recognise falling through, four keyless sources yielding no key, and a pattern matching the empty string yielding no key rather than an empty one. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 352 Lived 5 efficacy 98.60%, both mutants in key.go killed and no new survivor.

tasks.title: Continue without an issue key
tasks.acceptance:
- If no key is found, cr continues with an empty intent and marks the intent axis unavailable per §4.5, per §3.2.
- The unavailability is reported through the §4.5.4 honesty channel and survives --quiet.
- A test asserts a keyless PR still briefs successfully.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/intent/intent.go's Resolve takes §3.2's fallback structurally: ResolveKey returning KeyAbsent yields Intent{Pattern} without ever consulting the Source, so a keyless run continues with an empty intent and never starts the tracker command with a blank key, and Intent.Unavailability() derives §4.5.3's mark from Key.Origin rather than storing it, mirroring profile.Selection.Missing, so no Intent can carry issue text and report itself unavailable or resolve no key and report itself available. TestNoIssueKeyContinuesWithAnEmptyIntent asserts the empty intent, the unavailable axis id, and a marker file the stub tracker never wrote, and TestAnIntentFileDoesNotStandInForAMissingKey pins that §3.1.4 bypasses the command and not the key.
- intent.Unavailable{Axis, Reason} reuses the per-entry §4.5.4 shape testadequacy.Unavailable already holds, with Lens spelled Axis because §4.5.4 lists an unavailable axis and an unavailable half of one as different things, and its Disclosure satisfies finding.HonestyDisclosure so the report reaches the reader through the one channel §11.1 exempts from --quiet rather than through a message a flag can silence. TestTheUnavailableIntentAxisIsAnHonestyDisclosure asserts the interface, the text derived from both fields so data and print cannot drift, and a reason naming intent.key_pattern, the expression the resolution actually ran with, and --issue as the next actionable step.
- TestNoIssueKeyContinuesWithAnEmptyIntent is the keyless-PR assertion made at the seam cr brief will call, because brief does not exist yet: a KeySources whose branch, title, and body are all populated and all keyless resolves with no error, an empty Text, and the §4.5.3 mark, while TestAResolvedKeyLeavesTheIntentAxisAvailable holds the other direction and TestResolveSurfacesTheFailuresOfTheStepsItComposes keeps an uncompilable intent.key_pattern and a refusing tracker out of the fallback. The gate is green and gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 366, Lived 5, efficacy 98.65%, the same five commented equivalents and the same two known TIMED OUT as the baseline.

tasks.title: Define the claim record schema
tasks.acceptance:
- The claim struct carries every row of the §3.3 field table: id of the form <ISSUE-KEY>#c<n>, text, source (description, acceptance, comment, or note), span, note_id, span_hash, issue_hash, head.
- span_hash and issue_hash are computed by cr, never supplied by the agent.
- note_id is required when source is note.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/intent/claim.go holds §3.3's field table as data in the spec's own row order (id, text, source, span, note_id, span_hash, issue_hash, head) and the Claim struct carries every one of them, with state.Stamp supplying head and the round §2.3.3 adds; TestTheClaimFieldTableIsTheOneTheSpecWrites pins the table against the spec and TestAClaimCarriesExactlyTheTableRows walks the struct reflectively so no row can be added or dropped unnoticed.
