tasks.title: Post only comments anchored to lines
tasks.acceptance:
- Every posted comment is anchored to a line of the diff. v0.1 has no unanchored comment channel: an item with no code location is reported through cr status and never posted, per §1.6.1.
- A review comment spends the reviewer's standing with the author, so volume is a cost in itself, independent of correctness.
- A test asserts an unanchored item cannot reach the payload by any path.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every posted comment is anchored to a line of the diff, because the fence sits on the way in rather than at the payload: internal/finding's Decode refuses a record whose anchor names no path, so an item with no code location never becomes a record (§6.1.2, §4.1.3) and nothing unanchored exists downstream for a draft or a payload to render. No second enforcement point was added, since §1.6.1 needs one fence with no bypass rather than two checks a future author must remember.
- v0.1 has no unanchored comment channel, and today that is held as a negative: a comment is rendered from a record, a record is what the finding package's decoders hand back, and every one of them refuses an item with no code location, so there is no channel to widen. Reporting such an item through cr status is the positive half and belongs to intent-gap-entries and status-coverage-report, both open, and the end-to-end negative against a posted payload belongs to single-review-batching and pre-validate-positions, which build the payload.
- §1.6's economic claim now lives in the code it governs, as a paragraph on internal/finding.Anchor, the type that owns the fence: a review comment spends the reviewer's standing with the author, so volume is a cost in itself, independent of correctness, and an unanchored comment costs the most for the least, because the author has to work out what it is about before judging whether it is right. That is why v0.1 has one comment channel and this field is it.
- TestNoUnanchoredItemBecomesARecordByAnyDoor in internal/finding/anchored_test.go asserts an unanchored item cannot reach a record by any path. It reads the door set out of the package's own source with go/ast, taking every exported function whose results carry a Finding, requires that set to match the doors it drives, and feeds each of them, Decode as SourceAgent, Decode as SourceMerge, and DecodePerRole, four shapes of an item with no code location: no anchor key, an empty anchor, an anchor naming no path, and an anchor naming the empty path, asserting a RejectedRecordError naming anchor each time while the same fixture passes once anchored. The guard was verified by temporarily adding an exported Loophole returning []*Finding, which failed the set assertion, and by temporarily deleting the anchor branch from checker.check, which failed eight assertions, both reverted. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 254, Lived 4, efficacy 98.45 percent, the documented baseline unchanged, as a doc comment and a test add no production branch.

tasks.title: Block posting above the comment cap
tasks.acceptance:
- post.max_comments (default 20) caps the comments in one round. When the cap is exceeded cr blocks posting with exit code 1 and names the count, so the user triages further, per §1.6.2.
- cr never silently drops comments to fit.
- The cap report is an honesty disclosure and survives --quiet per §11.1.
- A test queues twenty-one comments and asserts exit 1 with the count named and nothing posted.
tasks.closed_reason:
- post.max_comments caps the comments of one round in internal/finding/cap.go, where CommentCapFor measures the round's queued records against the resolved setting and the built-in default of 20 comes from internal/config's §2.7 table rather than a second path to the value, which the cli test reads out of config.Resolve before it queues anything.
- Above the cap CommentCap.Err returns a *CommentCapExceededError naming the count, the cap, and the overflow, and internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto ExitValidation, so posting is blocked with exit code 1 and the message tells the user how many comments to triage away.
- cr never silently drops comments to fit, and the refusal is structural rather than remembered: the cap call hands back a two-int decision and no shape in the package can carry a subset of the queue, which TestNothingCarriesAFittedQueueBackFromTheCap holds open by reading the package's own source and failing any function whose signature names CommentCap and hands back a Finding — verified against a deliberately added FitToCap helper before it was deleted again.
- The cap report is CommentCap.Disclosure, made whether or not the cap was exceeded and taking no flag at all, so no caller has an answer to give --quiet, and cap.go declares the HonestyDisclosure interface as the shape §11.1's later shared writer consumes rather than building that writer here. TestTheCapReportIsAnHonestyDisclosureOnEitherPath pins the text under the cap, at it, and over it, and pins that the block carries the disclosure whole.
- TestQueueingPastTheCommentCapExitsWithTheValidationCode queues twenty-one comments against the default cap of 20 and asserts exit code 1 wrapped and unwrapped with the count 21 and the cap named in the message, while TestTheCapBlocksOnlyTheCountAboveIt covers nineteen, twenty and twenty-one. Gremlins killed all six cap.go mutants including both the boundary and the negation at the comparison, at Killed 260 and Lived 4, the four known baseline survivors with no new one.
Out of scope: nothing posted cannot be driven end to end because cr post does not exist, so single-review-batching, dry-run-posting and confirm-flag-required must make that assertion. The draft header that renders the count is draft-summary-header, the round summary count is round-summary-writers, and §1.6.3's non-destructive triage is triage-to-fit-non-destructive.

tasks.title: Keep volume triage scoped per request
tasks.acceptance:
- Triaging to fit under the cap is not destructive. A discard dispositioned not-here is scoped to the pull request per §7.4.1, so setting a true finding aside for volume reasons never silences it repository-wide, per §1.6.3.
- A test discards a finding for volume on PR 1 and asserts it still raises on PR 2 in the same repository.

tasks.title: Key waivers by anchor with class
tasks.acceptance:

tasks.title: Interpret the five draft triage verbs
tasks.acceptance:
- Triage happens by editing the file; cr draft and cr post interpret the result. The five rows of the §7.2 table: leaving a block unchanged posts it as rendered; editing the body prose posts it as edited; changing kind=finding to kind=question softens it and records a triage event; deleting the block entirely discards it with disposition not-here and writes a pull-request-scoped waiver per §7.4; setting disposition=wrong in the marker discards it as a false positive whether or not the body remains, writes a repository-wide waiver per §7.4, and counts against the class per §7.3.
- Both discard verbs are observable in the file cr reads back: deletion removes the marker, and wrong is a marker edit that survives precisely because the marker stays. A record carrying disposition=wrong is discarded even when its body is untouched, so the reviewer never has to delete text to express it.
- The two dispositions stay distinct: not-here means the finding is true but not worth a comment on this pull request — the ordinary case under §1.6 — and never counts against the class's precision; wrong means the finding is false, and is the only signal that demotes a class. Collapsing them would demote classes that are always right and merely never worth saying.
- A test drives all five verbs and asserts the resulting disposition, waiver scope, and statistics contribution for each.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Triage is read out of the edited draft.md: internal/draft/ingest.go's Ingest interprets §7.2's verbs from the file alone, and cr draft calls it on every regeneration through internal/cli/regenerate.go's ingestDraft.
- cr draft interprets the result now, and cr post, still a stub, has draft.Ingest as the single interpreter it will call, so the two cannot read one draft two ways.
- A block left unchanged is kept and rendered again as cr renders it, with outcome kept: TestTheFiveTriageVerbsOfSection72's f1 carries no disposition, no waiver and no triaged entry.
- A block whose body prose was edited is kept with the edited body carried into the draft through Triage.Preserved, so it is posted as edited: f2 in the same test is kept, listed in preserved, and its edited sentence is in the regenerated draft.
- Changing kind=finding to kind=question softens the record: Ingest lists it in Triage.Softened, softenForDraft renders it as a question with its label while findings.ndjson keeps it a finding so the next reading of the draft softens it again, and its outcome finding.OutcomeSoftened is reported in cr draft's triaged list; writing that outcome to triage.ndjson as an event is triage-event-writing's.
- Deleting a block discards the record with disposition not-here and writes a pull-request-scoped waiver: f4 is discarded not-here and its waiver sits in the pull request's waivers.ndjson and nowhere else.
- Setting disposition=wrong discards the record as a false positive whether or not its body remains, writes a repository-wide waiver, and counts against the class: f5 is discarded wrong with its waiver in ~/.cr/waivers/<owner>/<repo>.ndjson, its outcome discarded-wrong reports counts_against_class true, and TestAWrongMarkerDiscardsWhetherOrNotTheBodyRemains covers an untouched body, a deleted body, and a wrong that also softened.
- Both discard verbs are observable in the file cr reads back: blocksOf finds no marker for a deleted block, and reads disposition=wrong off the marker that stays, which ParseMarker holds to the grammar.
- A record carrying disposition=wrong is discarded even when its body is untouched: f5's body is never edited in the five-verb test and it is discarded wrong, so the reviewer never deletes text to say it.
- not-here stays the true-but-not-worth-it disposition and never counts against the class's precision: finding.Outcome.CountsAgainstClass is false for discarded-not-here, and its waiver is scoped to the pull request by finding.Waive.
- wrong stays the false-positive disposition and is the demoting signal alongside softened, which §7.3.4 also puts in the numerator: CountsAgainstClass is true for discarded-wrong and softened only, asserted by TestOnlyWrongAndSoftenedCountAgainstTheClass.
- The two are never collapsed: each deletion and each wrong takes its own disposition, waiver file and outcome, and the five-verb test asserts f4 and f5 land in different files with different counts.
- TestTheFiveTriageVerbsOfSection72 drives all five verbs through cr draft and asserts, per verb, the stored disposition, the waiver scope read from the two files of §7.4.4, and the outcome with its counts_against_class contribution; dogfooded on deligoez/cr-qa#1, where softening f1 rendered it with the cited label while state kept it a finding, marking f2 wrong wrote wr1 to the repository file, and git status in the checkout was unchanged.
Out of scope: a disposition of not-here typed by hand, a question turned back into a finding, and every other marker edit are re-rendered from the record rather than aborted; marker-edit-semantics owns those aborts. The waivers carry content_hash "" because cr record stores no anchor hash, which anchor-no-migration owns.

tasks.title: Enforce the marker field edit semantics
tasks.acceptance:
- The six rows of §7.2's marker edit-semantics table: id is immutable and a changed or unknown id aborts; kind finding to question softens, and question to finding is accepted only when the recomputed grade is probed or cited, aborting otherwise per §6.3.3; path, start_line and line are re-validated per §6.1.2 and abort when the anchor no longer resolves; severity is freely editable and recorded as a triage event; disposition set to wrong discards as a false positive, while not-here is written by cr on deletion and is never set by hand; grade is informational, recomputed by cr per §6.2 and ignored, aborting only when the marker's kind contradicts the recomputed grade per §6.3.3.
- Any other marker edit aborts with exit code 1, naming the record id.
- cr post refuses to run when a marker is malformed, naming the line, per §7.2.1.
- A test exercises each row's accept path and each row's abort path.
- Round 12 finding anchor-hash-not-recomputed, assigned here: §7.2 re-validates path, start_line, and line after a marker edit but says nothing about the anchor's content hash, which §9.2 makes part of the anchor and §7.4.1 keys waivers on. The implementation recomputes it whenever the anchor lines change.
tasks.closed_reason:
- id row: draft.refuseUnknownBlocks aborts before any verb is read when a block names a record this round did not render, naming that id and §7.2.3's reason, so a changed id is refused rather than orphaning one record and adopting another; TestABlockOutsideTheQueuedRecordsAborts and the "the id is changed" case of TestAMarkerEditSection72RefusesAbortsWithTheValidationCode assert it.
- kind row: markerEdit.kind softens a finding whose marker reads question, admits question to finding only when the grade cr computed is probed or cited, and otherwise aborts naming §6.3.3; cli.retypeForDraft renders both directions into the next draft without storing either, so the marker goes on saying what the reviewer typed.
- path, start_line and line row: markerEdit.anchor re-validates a moved location through finding.Reanchor, which runs ValidateAnchor and then ResolveAnchor against the §6.1.2 tree the anchor's side names and aborts naming the record id when it no longer resolves, while cli.anchorTrees opens the checkout and the merge base lazily so a run where no marker moved opens neither.
- severity row: markerEdit.severity accepts any of §6.1's four and refuses a fifth word by naming them, and cli.applyRetriage writes the reviewer's value onto the stored record, which cr draft reports as a retriaged row; the triage.ndjson event ledger itself belongs to triage-event-writing and is not written here.
- disposition row: wrong still discards as a false positive with its repository-wide waiver, and not-here now aborts telling the reviewer to delete the block instead, both asserted through the command.
- grade row: nothing reads the marker's grade, which TestEveryRowOfTheMarkerEditTableAcceptsWhatItAdmits shows by writing grade="certain" and reading grade="cited" back out, and its one abort is the kind contradiction of the kind row, supplied by §6.3.3.
- Any other marker edit: draft.MarkerEditError carries the record id, the draft line and the field at fault, and internal/cli/exit.go maps it to ExitValidation, asserted as 1 by every case of TestAMarkerEditSection72RefusesAbortsWithTheValidationCode.
- §7.2.1: the malformed-marker refusal is draft.ParseMarker's, reached through the one reader cr draft and cr post share, and dogfooded at exit 1 with "draft line 11 is a malformed record marker: kind carries no JSON string"; cr post is still a stub command, and post-recomputes-grade wires it and asserts the same refusal at that command.
- Tests: TestEveryRowOfTheMarkerEditTableAcceptsWhatItAdmits covers six accept paths and TestEveryRowOfTheMarkerEditTableAbortsOnWhatItRefuses seven abort paths, with TestAMarkerEditSection72RefusesAbortsWithTheValidationCode and TestAMovedAnchorIsRevalidatedAgainstTheHeadAndRehashed covering the same rows through cr draft.
- Round 12 anchor-hash-not-recomputed: §7.2 re-validates the three location fields and says nothing about the content hash, which §9.2 makes part of the anchor and §7.4.1 keys a waiver on.
- finding.Reanchor recomputes that hash from the tree whenever the anchor lines change, asserted against finding.AnchorContentHash in both the draft and the cli test and dogfooded through the built binary, where moving a marker from 1-1 to 3-4 turned content_hash from "staleaaaaaaaaaaa" into "2b81c12b4d49d424".
Out of scope: §9.2's context window is recomputed nowhere when a marker moves an anchor, so ContextBefore and ContextAfter still describe the lines the anchor left; round 12's finding names the content hash alone, and the same argument applies to the window.

tasks.title: Recompute grades before building the payload
tasks.acceptance:
- cr post recomputes every record's grade and re-applies §6.3 before building the payload, so no draft edit can turn an argued record into a posted assertion, per §7.2.2.
- A test edits a marker to kind=finding on an argued record and asserts posting is refused.
- Carried from intent-finding-on-unmapped-unit (6929636): §4.1.4's forcing of an intent finding on an unmapped unit to a question runs only at cr record. A mapping that changes after recording can leave a recorded finding on a now-unmapped unit, so cr draft and cr post re-apply that forcing alongside §6.3's, and a test records the finding while the unit is mapped, clears the mapping, and asserts the drafted and posted record is a question.
- Carried from evidence-region (f926390): §8.1.7 regenerates the cr-owned regions at post time too, but cr post is still a stub and draft.commentOf, the one path that builds label, provenance and evidence regions, is unexported. cr post builds every posted body through that same path via an exported entry point, never a second renderer, and a test asserts a posted body's evidence region is byte-identical to the drafted one for an untouched block.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cli.buildReview is §7.2.2 in order: roundGrading.regrade recomputes every record's grade from §6.2.1's inputs, the draft is read back only afterwards so §7.2's kind row is judged against the recomputed grade, and §4.1.4's forcing, §6.3's ForceQuestions and RefuseArguedAssertion are applied over the survivors before post.Build assembles the payload; `cr post` stops being a stub for this and writes nothing at all, with `--confirm` and `--reconcile` refusing by name so no caller learns that the §8.5 gate is satisfied by a run that sent nothing.
- TestPostRecomputesTheGradeBeforeItReadsTheMarker hardens a stored question to kind=finding in the marker and asserts `cr draft` admits it on the recorded grade while `cr post` refuses with exit 1 naming f1 and "argued"; dogfooded on the built binary, which printed `draft line 11, record f1: kind asks for "finding" on a record cr graded "argued"` and left findings.ndjson byte-identical.
- Carried finding intent-finding-on-unmapped-unit: §4.1.4 ran only at `cr record`, so a mapping replaced or cleared inside a round left a recorded intent finding asserting against a claim the round no longer maps to its unit.
- roundGrading.forceUnmapped re-applies it at `cr draft` and at `cr post` from one read of the round's units and mapping, and TestClearingTheMappingMakesARecordedIntentFindingAQuestion records the finding while u1 is mapped, clears mapping.ndjson, and asserts both the regenerated draft's marker and the payload's comment read as a question; dogfooded through the binary, where clearing the mapping turned the reported comment from {"id":"f2","kind":"finding"} into {"id":"f2","kind":"question"}.
- Carried finding evidence-region: §8.1.7's regions are regenerated at post time too, and draft.commentOf was the one path building label, provenance and evidence while `cr post` had no way to reach it.
- draft.PostBodies is that exported entry point and calls commentOf once per record rather than rendering anything itself, with §8.1.5 applied there because post time is the first moment it can honestly be required; TestAPostedBodyIsTheDraftedBlockThroughTheSamePath compares each posted comment against the drafted block byte for byte over one record of each grade, so the label, the citations and the probe region are all covered.
Out of scope: `cr draft` does not recompute grades, only `cr post` does, which is what §7.2.2 assigns and what makes the test above meaningful; the consequence is that a hardening `cr draft` admits can be refused by `cr post`, and if that surprise is unwanted the spec section rather than the implementation is what would have to change.

tasks.title: Abort on an unknown marker id
tasks.acceptance:
- v0.1 has no manual-comment channel in the draft. A block whose id is unknown aborts with exit code 1 rather than being adopted as a new record, per §7.2.3.
- Every record in the corpus carries a role, an axis, and a grade cr computed, and a hand-written block can carry none of them. A comment the reviewer wants to make in their own name is written on GitHub directly, after posting.
- A test adds a hand-written block and asserts exit 1 naming the unknown id.
tasks.closed_reason:
- v0.1 has no manual-comment channel in the draft, and draft.refuseUnknownBlocks is where that is enforced: it walks the blocks of the file the reviewer saved, finds the earliest one naming a record the round did not render, and stops the ingest there.
- That refusal is a MarkerEditError carrying the unknown id, which internal/cli/exit.go maps to ExitValidation, so a block cr never rendered aborts with exit code 1 instead of being adopted as a record; it landed with marker-edit-semantics in 34733f7 because §7.2's immutable `id` row and §7.2.3 are the same block seen from two sides, and this task is what holds it to §7.2.3's own obligation.
- The refusal names why rather than only what: its message says §7.2.3 gives v0.1 no manual-comment channel in the draft, because a hand-written block carries none of the role, axis and cr-computed grade every record in the corpus has, and §6.2 would have nothing to compute a grade from.
- It also names where the comment does belong, telling the reviewer to restore the id cr wrote and write a comment of their own on GitHub after posting, which is dogfooded through the built binary: both `cr draft` and `cr post` answered a pasted block with `draft line 31, record f9: id names no record this round rendered, and §7.2.3 gives v0.1 no manual-comment channel in the draft; restore the id cr wrote, and write a comment of your own on GitHub after posting` at exit 1.
- TestAHandWrittenBlockAbortsNamingTheUnknownID adds a well-formed block of the reviewer's own beside an untouched round and asserts exit 1 naming f9 through both commands §7.2 gives the draft, and TestAHandWrittenBlockIsRefusedBeforeAnyVerbIsRead adds a deletion beside it and asserts neither record moved and no waiver was written, since the refusal is made before any verb is read.

tasks.title: Write triage events idempotently per key
tasks.acceptance:
- Triage events are written idempotently: re-running a command overwrites the event for its key rather than appending a second one, so regenerating a draft per §7.1.6 or running cr post twice cannot inflate a count, per §7.3.1.
- cr draft writes one raised event per record it queues, and writes the outcome event directly for a record it discards at draft time. cr post --confirm writes exactly one outcome event per queued record, drawn from kept, softened, discarded-not-here, and discarded-wrong; cr post without --confirm writes none, since it changes nothing.
- Round 8 finding triage-event-key-permits-contradiction: outcome events key on (PR, round, record id) with the action as a value, so a later run replaces the earlier outcome; raised stays a separately keyed event. With action inside the key a record could carry both kept and discarded-wrong against a single raised — reachable through the ordinary retry after §8.4.2 — inflating §7.3.4's demotion rate on exactly the class the retry touched.
- Round 8 finding triage-event-key-permits-contradiction: cr post --confirm writes its outcome events after the network call, and a call rejected per §8.4.2 leaves no outcome event behind.
- A test drives a rejected post followed by a re-triage and asserts one outcome event survives.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Triage events are written idempotently per §7.3.1: internal/finding/triageevent.go's mergeTriageEvents overwrites in place the event a written one shares a key with and appends only the keys the file did not hold, so regenerating a draft per §7.1.6 or running cr post twice cannot inflate a count; TestRewritingAnEventLeavesOneOfIt drives three runs of one round and asserts two events, and the dogfood against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1 left triage.ndjson at two lines across three cr draft runs.
- cr draft writes one raised event per record it queues: internal/cli/draft.go calls recordDraftTriage after publishDraft, and TestADraftRaisesWhatItQueuedAndSettlesOnlyItsDiscards asserts f1..f5 raised on the first run.
- cr draft writes the outcome event directly for a record it discards at draft time: recordDraftTriage hands triaged.discardedSettlements to finding.RecordOutcomes, and the same test asserts f4:discarded-not-here and f5:discarded-wrong after the reviewer's deletion and wrong marker, while the softened f3 gets none because it stays queued.
- cr post --confirm writes exactly one outcome event per queued record, drawn from kept, softened, discarded-not-here and discarded-wrong: internal/cli/triage.go's recordPostTriage settles every record the draft was rendered for through triaged.settled, and TestThePostSeamSettlesEveryQueuedRecordOnce asserts exactly those four actions against four raises; the send itself belongs to confirm-flag-required, which calls this seam.
- cr post without --confirm writes none, since it changes nothing: TestAPostWithoutConfirmWritesNoTriageEvent asserts the ledger byte-identical across a run whose draft carried a discard, and the dogfood left triage.ndjson at md5 5f6765f5d9362f767ee3ba3c1fd104b2 before and after.
- Round 8 finding triage-event-key-permits-contradiction, the key: triageKey is the record id, the pull request and the round, with the action held as a value on the event, so a later run replaces the earlier outcome.
- Round 8 finding triage-event-key-permits-contradiction, the raise: the key's fourth field is whether the event is the raise, so raised stays a separately keyed event and survives every outcome written against it.
- With action inside the key a record could carry both kept and discarded-wrong against a single raised, reachable through the ordinary retry after §8.4.2 and inflating §7.3.4's demotion rate on exactly the class the retry touched: TestARetriedPostLeavesOneOutcomeAgainstOneRaise writes kept and then discarded-wrong for one record and asserts the ledger holds f1:raised and f1:discarded-wrong alone.
- Round 8 finding triage-event-key-permits-contradiction: cr post --confirm writes its outcome events after the network call, and a call rejected per §8.4.2 leaves no outcome event behind — recordPostTriage is documented and positioned as the post-call seam, and nothing on cr post's validating path reaches a triage writer.
- A test drives a rejected post followed by a re-triage and asserts one outcome event survives: TestARetriedPostLeavesOneOutcomeAgainstOneRaise asserts the ledger holds only the raise at the point the rejected call returns, then writes the retry's outcome and asserts one outcome stands.

tasks.title: Carry the full field set per event
tasks.acceptance:
- Every event carries class, axis, role, grade, rule id when present, the PR, the round, and the head, per §7.3.1.
- Round 8 finding unnameable-triage-event: a severity edit, which §7.2's marker table calls freely editable and recorded as a triage event, has a nameable representation. severity is added to the fields every event carries and a severity edit is recorded on the record's single outcome event rather than as an event of its own, so §7.3.1's closed five-name vocabulary and its exactly-one-outcome rule both hold.
- The five action names are the complete vocabulary the §7.3 statistics are computed from.
- A test edits only severity and asserts the change is observable in exactly one event.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/triageevent.go's TriageOccasion.event fills every one off the record and the occasion together, so no caller can write an event that carries less: class, axis, role and grade from the record, rule from it when a rule of §2.6 produced it and absent otherwise, and the PR, round and head from the occasion; TestATriageEventCarriesEverythingSection731Requires asserts the whole struct against a literal and TestTheEventsWireFormIsSection731sFieldSet asserts the wire form's key set against specEventFields, an independent transcription of §7.3.1's sentence, in both directions — so a field that is declared and never filled fails the first and a field that belongs to no sentence fails the second.
- The representation is the value on the events §7.3.1 already requires, and it is nameable because the raise and the outcome say different things: TestASeverityEditIsObservableInExactlyOneEvent edits only the marker's severity and the ledger reads f1:raised:high then f1:kept:low, so the change is the difference between two events a reader can point at rather than an event nobody could name.
- TriageEvent.Severity is written on every event by that one constructor, and the outcome event carries the reviewer's value because ingestDraft applies §7.2's severity row before buildReview settles anything — TestTheEditedSeverityIsTheOneTheRecordCarries holds the record, the regenerated marker and the raise to the edited value together; no sixth action name was added, TriageActions still returns the five and RecordOutcomes still refuses anything outside them, and no second outcome event is written, which TestASecondConfirmedRunLeavesTheSeverityEventWhereItWas measures by running `cr post --confirm` twice and finding the ledger where the first run left it while the review was sent twice.
- TriageActions is the one list, TriageAction.Valid reads only it, and RecordOutcomes refuses an action outside it before anything reaches the ledger: TestTheVocabularyIsFiveNamesAndAnOutcomeIsFourOfThem holds the list to raised, kept, softened, discarded-not-here and discarded-wrong, admits the four outcomes, refuses `hardened`, the empty action and `raised`-as-an-outcome, and asserts the ledger stayed empty through all three; TestASeverityEditIsObservableInExactlyOneEvent then walks every event a real `cr draft` and `cr post --confirm` wrote and holds each action to Valid.
- TestASeverityEditIsObservableInExactlyOneEvent is that test: the round is drafted, the marker's severity alone is changed from high to low, `cr post --confirm` runs against a `gh` shim, and the ledger is asserted as the exact list [f1:raised:high f1:kept:low] — which says three things at once, that the new value reached exactly one of the two events, that the ledger gained no event of its own for the edit, and that no other event moved.

tasks.title: Report triage statistics per class
tasks.acceptance:
- cr stats --repo <owner/repo> reports per class and per rule: raised, kept, softened, discarded as not-here, and discarded as wrong, per §7.3.2.
- The statistics are computed from the repository's triage.ndjson across pull requests.
- A test seeds events across two PRs and asserts the per-class and per-rule breakdowns.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `cr stats --repo <owner/repo>` is built in `internal/cli/stats.go`: it resolves the repository through §11.1's global `--repo`, reads the ledger lock-free through `finding.TriageEvents` per §2.3.2, and prints §7.3.2's five counts — raised, kept, softened, discarded as `not-here`, discarded as `wrong` — once per class and once per rule, in the order §7.3.2 names them. `finding.Tally` in `internal/finding/triagestats.go` computes both cuts in one pass so a class and the rules that produced it cannot disagree, and it refuses an action outside §7.3.1's five rather than letting it fall through no arm of the switch and silently shrink §7.3.4's denominator.
- The statistics are computed from `~/.cr/repos/<owner>/<repo>/triage.ndjson`, which §2.2 makes repository state shared by every pull request, so one read answers for all of them; the command takes no `<pr>` and has no way to narrow to one. §9.3 therefore has nothing to say about it, the same answer `cr rules suggest` gets and for the same reason, and it is entered in `movedHeadRuns` as `readsNoRound`. §9.3.5's round scoping does not reach it either: triage.ndjson is not one of §2.3.3's eight per-PR files, so `TestEveryStampedReadIsRoundScopedOrDeclared` needs no cross-round exemption for it.
- `TestStatsCountsEveryActionPerClassAndPerRuleAcrossPullRequests` in `internal/cli/stats_test.go` seeds four records across PR 7 and PR 9 — the later spanning two of its own rounds, since a round index is per pull request — and asserts the whole per-class and per-rule breakdown through the command's own JSON: `unchecked-error` 3/1/1/0/1 and `missing-test` 1/0/0/1/0 per class, and `no-dropped-error` 2/1/1/0/0 per rule, where the rule row counts two of the three records the class row counts because `f4` carries no rule id. Two further tests cover the empty repository, which answers with §12.3's empty arrays rather than refusing, and the refusal of a sixth action name.

tasks.title: Report every class first seen
tasks.acceptance:
- class is agent-composed, so a reworded slug would silently escape the waiver and posted-index keys of §7.4.1 and §9.3.6. cr reports every class first seen in a round as new, in the round summary and in cr stats, so drift is visible rather than silent, per §7.3.3.
- A test reruns a round with a reworded class slug and asserts the new-class report fires.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `class` is agent-composed and nothing downstream re-derives it: §7.4.1 keys a waiver on `(anchor.path, class, content hash)` and §9.3.6's posted index on the same class, so a slug reworded between rounds escapes both keys silently and the finding returns as if it had never been waived or posted. That is the whole reason this report exists rather than a nicety — `finding.NewClasses` and `finding.FirstSeenClasses` in `internal/finding/newclass.go` are what make the reword observable at the two moments a reader could still act on it.
- `cr` reports every class first seen in a round as new, in both places §7.3.3 names. In the round summary: `cr draft` computes the list through `newDraftClasses` off the ledger as it stands before the round's own §7.3.1 events are written, and `writeNewClasses` puts it under `new_classes` in `rounds/<n>/summary.json` through `UpdateRoundSection`, on every run and empty included — a round that raised no new class and a round whose report was never written would otherwise read alike. The run prints it too. In `cr stats`: `first_seen` names every class with the pull request and round the ledger first held it on, so `unchecked-error` at pr 7 round 1 sits beside `dropped-error` at pr 12 round 1 under the same rule and the drift is a comparison the reader can make. `NewClasses` excludes this pull request and round from what counts as prior history, so §7.1.6's regeneration cannot turn a class new once and old ever after, and `FirstSeenClasses` orders by the ledger's own position rather than by `at`, because a re-run overwrites an event under its key and rewrites its timestamp — regenerating an old round's draft would otherwise hand "first seen" to a round that merely happened second.
- `TestARewordedClassSlugIsReportedAsNewInTheSummaryAndInStats` in `internal/cli/newclass_test.go` gives the repository a history on pull request 3, drafts round 2 of pull request 7 raising the same `unchecked-error` and asserts nothing is reported, then rewords that one record's class to `dropped-error` at the same anchor with the same prose and reruns the round: the report fires in the command's own output, in `summary.json`'s `new_classes`, and in `cr stats`'s `first_seen`, which names `unchecked-error` at pr 3 round 1 and `dropped-error` at pr 7 round 2. `TestARegeneratedRoundReportsTheSameNewClasses` drafts one round three times and asserts the answer never moves.

tasks.title: Compute the demotion rate as bound
tasks.acceptance:
- The demotion rate for a class is (discarded-wrong + softened) / raised over that class's events in the repository's triage.ndjson. Discards dispositioned not-here are excluded from the numerator, because they carry no evidence that the class is imprecise, per §7.3.4.
- A class whose rate exceeds stats.demote_threshold (default 0.6) over at least stats.min_samples (default 8) raised events is listed as a demotion candidate.
- Marking a false positive wrong costs the reviewer an extra edit while plain deletion is free, so discarded-wrong is systematically under-counted and the demotion rate is a lower bound on imprecision. cr reports it as a lower bound and never presents it as a measured precision, per §7.3.5.
- A test asserts the not-here exclusion and the lower-bound wording.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `TriageCounts.DemotionRate` in `internal/finding/demotion.go` divides the counted outcomes by the class's raises, and both come from the repository's whole `triage.ndjson`: `cr stats` reads it across every pull request through `finding.TriageEvents`, and `finding.Tally` gives the per-class counts the rate is taken over. The numerator walks §7.3.1's action vocabulary through `TriageActions()`, skips the raise, and adds an outcome only when `Outcome.CountsAgainstClass()` admits it — which is `discarded-wrong` and `softened`, so the rate is `(discarded-wrong + softened) / raised` as §7.3.4 writes it. A class with no raises returns 0 rather than dividing by zero, and is on no list anyway.
- `not-here` never enters that numerator, and it is excluded by construction rather than by a subtraction: `Outcome.CountsAgainstClass()` is the one place the decision is spelled and `DemotionRate` reads it instead of restating it, so no second opinion about the disposition can exist in the tree. The reason is not arithmetic — §7.2 makes `not-here` the ordinary case of a true finding not worth a comment on this pull request, so it is no evidence that the class is imprecise. `TestTheDemotionRateExcludesNotHereFromItsNumerator` seeds two classes with the identical shape of history, 10 raises and 7 discards each, differing only in disposition: `imprecise` comes out at 0.70 and `unwelcome` at 0.00.
- `finding.DemotionCandidates` lists a class when its rate exceeds `stats.demote_threshold` and its raises are at least `stats.min_samples`, both resolved through §2.7's layers by `statsSample` in `internal/cli/stats.go` and defaulting to 0.6 and 8 in `internal/config/config.go`'s settings table. "Exceeds" is read strictly and the minimum as "at least", because §7.3.4 words the two bounds differently; applying the `<=` → `<` mutation by hand makes `borderline` at exactly 0.6 a candidate and `TestAThinSampleAndAnExactThresholdAreNotCandidates` fails, so the boundary is held by a test rather than by a comment. `TestTheSampleComesFromTheResolvedConfiguration` moves both settings from a repository config and watches the candidacy follow.
- The rate can only understate imprecision, and the report says so in the words §7.3.5 gives: `finding.DemotionBound` reads "§7.3.5: a lower bound on imprecision, not a measured precision — marking a false positive `wrong` costs an extra edit while deleting the block is free, so `discarded-wrong` is under-counted". It is a constant so every renderer says it identically, and it is emitted whether or not the run found a candidate — the caveat is a fact about the statistic, not about this run's results.
- `cr` presents the number as a lower bound at every door and as a precision at none. The JSON field is `rate_lower_bound`, so a reader who copies one number out of the document keeps the caveat in the key; `demotion_rate_bound` carries the sentence beside it; and the terminal rendering prints the same sentence under the candidate list. `TestTheDemotionRateIsReportedAsALowerBoundAndNotAsPrecision` asserts all three on the printed document rather than on the rendering — an agent reads the document, and §7.3.5 binds what the number may be presented as to any reader — and also asserts that no field anywhere in the payload is named `precision`.
- `internal/cli/demotion_test.go` holds both halves. The `not-here` exclusion is `TestTheDemotionRateExcludesNotHereFromItsNumerator`'s paired fixture above, where a numerator that merely counted discards would put both classes on the list at 0.70 and demote one that has never once been wrong; the lower-bound wording is `TestTheDemotionRateIsReportedAsALowerBoundAndNotAsPrecision`'s three assertions on the document. Dogfooded against a seeded ledger through the built binary: `speculative-nil 0.70 over 10 raise(s)` is listed, `style-nit` (10 raised, 7 `not-here`) is not, and `rare-race` (5 raised, 5 `wrong`, rate 1.00) is not either, because 5 is under the minimum of 8.

tasks.title: Report accurate classes rarely worth posting
tasks.acceptance:
- A class whose not-here rate exceeds stats.demote_threshold over the same sample is reported separately as a volume candidate: it is accurate but rarely worth posting, and the remedy is to stop raising it, not to soften it, per §7.3.6.
- Both candidacies are reports to the user, not automatic changes. cr never alters a rule's kind by itself, per §7.3.7.
- A test asserts a high not-here class appears as a volume candidate and not as a demotion candidate.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `TriageCounts.NotHereRate` and `finding.VolumeCandidates` in `internal/finding/volume.go` list a class separately when its `not-here` discards exceed `stats.demote_threshold` over at least `stats.min_samples` raises — the same `finding.Sample` §7.3.4's demotion candidacy is drawn over, read as the same two settings rather than as a second number arrived at separately, so a project that moves either knob moves both lists together. `cr stats` prints it under its own heading and emits it as `volume_candidates`, apart from `demotion_candidates` and unranked against it. Each candidate carries §7.3.6's own sentence in `VolumeRemedy` — "accurate but rarely worth posting — the remedy is to stop raising it, not to soften it" — on the candidate rather than only in the surrounding prose, because that is the whole reason for a second list: the class is not imprecise, so softening it would turn a true finding nobody wanted into a question nobody wanted. The two rates share a denominator and no outcome at all, since §7.2's dispositions mean opposite things, and a volume candidate carries no lower-bound caveat: §7.3.5's under-counting is about the `wrong` marker costing an edit that plain deletion does not, while `not-here` is what cr itself writes when a block is deleted.
- Both candidacies are values returned to the caller and printed, and nothing else. Neither `internal/finding/demotion.go` nor `internal/finding/volume.go` nor `internal/cli/stats.go` opens a file for writing; there is no flag on the command that would have it act on a list, and its doc comment says so. `cr stats` closes its output with "§7.3.7: both lists are reports; cr changed no rule", for the reason `cr rules suggest` prints the same kind of line — a list headed "candidates" invites the reading that something has been decided.
- `TestStatsChangesNothingIncludingTheRuleItProposesDemoting` fingerprints every file under `~/.cr` byte for byte across a run that produced one demotion candidate and one volume candidate — the run that would act on them if any run did — with a rule file carrying `"kind":"finding"` planted first, so the assertion has the field §7.3.7 names and not merely the absence of one. The whole tree rather than the rule file alone is deliberate: a run that altered no rule while quietly rewriting the ledger it had just read would satisfy a narrower guard and break the same sentence.
- `TestAnAccurateButUnwantedClassIsAVolumeCandidateAndNotADemotionOne` in `internal/cli/volume_test.go` seeds two classes with the identical shape of history — 10 raises, 7 discards, 3 keeps — differing only in the disposition of the discards: `unwelcome` appears in `volume_candidates` at a `not_here_rate` of 0.7 and is absent from `demotion_candidates`, while `imprecise` appears in `demotion_candidates` at 0.7 and is absent from `volume_candidates`. `TestAVolumeCandidacyIsDrawnOverTheSameSampleAsADemotion` holds the shared minimum. Dogfooded through the built binary against a seeded ledger: `style-nit 0.70 over 10 raise(s)` under volume candidates and nowhere else, `speculative-nil 0.70 over 10 raise(s)` under demotion candidates and nowhere else, and `rare-race` (5 raised, 5 `wrong`, rate 1.00) on neither list because 5 is under the minimum of 8.

tasks.title: Define the anchor field set
tasks.acceptance:
- An anchor carries path, side, start_line, line, a normalised content hash, and up to three lines of context on each side, per §9.2.
- The content hash is the normalised hash per §1.4 of the lines from start_line to line inclusive, treated as one text — so a single-line anchor and a multi-line anchor hash by the same rule.
- Valid side values are RIGHT and LEFT.
- A test asserts a one-line and a three-line anchor hash by the same function.
- Round 12 finding unordered-range-fields, assigned here: nothing requires start_line <= line. The implementation rejects an anchor whose range is inverted or empty.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/anchor.go holds §9.2 anchor rules beside the Anchor struct internal/finding/finding.go already carries, with path, side, start_line, line, content_hash and the two context windows, and ValidateAnchor bounds each window at contextWindow, three lines a side, with TestAnAnchorRecordsAtMostThreeLinesOfContextOnEachSide asserting that three passes and a fourth on either side does not.
- AnchorContentHash joins the anchored lines with a single LF and hands the whole text to text.NormalisedHash, so §1.4 runs once over the range and there is no branch on the line count at all — TestTheContentHashBranchesOnNothing reads that off anchor.go own source and proves the walker fires by asserting ValidateAnchor next door does branch.
- ValidateAnchor closes side against anchorSides, git.Right and git.Left, because git.Side is a defined string any untyped constant reaches, and TestAnAnchorNamesOneOfSection92sTwoSides accepts the two and refuses the empty value, right, Right, "RIGHT ", MIDDLE and BOTH with the offending value quoted back.
- TestAOneLineAndAThreeLineAnchorHashByTheSameFunction asserts the properties a special-cased one-line path would break rather than restating strings.Join — §1.4 normalisation reaches both sizes, a three-line anchor hashes as the one-line anchor carrying the same LFs, and neither the first line alone nor the reversed order reaches that digest.
- Round 12 unordered-range-fields is answered where §9.2 leaves the two numbers unordered, ValidateAnchor being the single place the pair is read as a range before §6.2.2 containment and §8.3.3 payload ordering rely on it, wired into checker.check in internal/finding/validate.go and proven on every door by TestAnAnchorRunningBackwardsNeverBecomesARecord.
- ValidateAnchor rejects line < start_line as inverted and start_line < 1 as the empty range that names no line of any file, an inclusive range making start_line == line a legal one-line anchor rather than an empty one and §9.2 required start_line ruling out GitHub optional one, with TestAnAnchorRangeRunsForwardsFromALineOfTheFile pinning both boundaries.

tasks.title: Resolve anchor sides against two trees
tasks.acceptance:
- RIGHT anchors a line in the head. LEFT anchors a removed line and is used only for records about deletions, per §9.2.1.
- Every record in findings.ndjson has an anchor; an item with no code location never becomes a record, per §4.1.3.
- A test resolves a RIGHT anchor against the head and a LEFT anchor against the merge base, and asserts a LEFT anchor pointing at a head-only line fails.
- Carried from anchor-schema: internal/gh/threads.go converts a GitHub diffSide with a raw git.Side(n.DiffSide) and validates nothing, so an unexpected value silently yields a thread anchor whose side matches no hunk in §3.5.3. The conversion is validated or the thread is refused.
tasks.closed_reason:
- §9.2.1's first half is where §6.1.2 puts it: internal/finding/anchor.go's ResolveAnchor sends a RIGHT anchor to the head and a LEFT one to the merge base, through a Trees pair of readers, so RIGHT anchors a line in the head and LEFT a line the head no longer has.
- The second half, that LEFT is used only for records about deletions, is documented rather than enforced, and ResolveAnchor says why: whether a record is about a deletion is a judgement about what it says, which §2.1 leaves to the agent and invariant 1 keeps cr out of. What cr establishes is the location, and a line the change added is not in the merge base to be anchored.
- Every record in findings.ndjson has an anchor already, and nothing was rebuilt: internal/finding/fields.go marks the anchor row Required, checker.check walks that table on every door and then hands the anchor to ValidateAnchor, which refuses one naming no path as an item with no code location per §6.1.2 and §4.1.3.
- The test that would catch the rule's removal already exists as well: TestNoUnanchoredItemBecomesARecordByAnyDoor in internal/finding/anchored_test.go reads the set of exported functions handing back a Finding out of the package's own source and drives all four shapes of an unanchored item through each, so a new door is a failing test rather than a reopened comment channel.
- TestARightAnchorResolvesAgainstTheHeadAndALeftOneAgainstTheMergeBase resolves a RIGHT anchor against the head and a LEFT anchor against the merge base over a real two-commit repository built by twoTrees, whose branch rewrites a line, adds a file and deletes one, so each side resolves the file only its own tree holds and is refused the other's by name. Swapping the two readers was verified to fail it in three places.
- TestALeftAnchorPointingAtAHeadOnlyLineIsRefused asserts the failure the two trees exist to produce: the head's lines 7 to 9 are four lines the change added, the merge base holds five, and the LEFT anchor is refused naming the tree and its length, with the boundary either side of line 5 pinned and the same ranges resolving on RIGHT.
- TestASideNamingNeitherTreeResolvesAgainstNothing drives six near-miss sides through readers that fail the test if they are opened at all, because refused and read-the-head-anyway are the same error to a caller and different faults.
- The carried finding is fixed at its root: §9.2's vocabulary is now closed once, by git.ParseSide beside the two constants, and both readers of an outside value go through it, ValidateAnchor for an agent's NDJSON side and internal/gh for GitHub's diffSide, so the set cannot be closed twice and drift.
- internal/gh/threads.go's raw git.Side(n.DiffSide) is gone: threadNode.anchor now returns an error, and an unknown value refuses the thread and aborts the ingest naming the thread id and quoting the value, rather than dropping it. Dropping is the quiet answer and it is the expensive one, because a thread with a side matching no hunk attaches to no unit under §3.5.3, suppresses nothing under §3.5.4, and cr repeats a concern a colleague already raised with nothing in the run reporting it; §3.5.1 admits no exception either.
- TestAThreadWhoseDiffSideNamesNeitherTreeIsRefused covers six unplaceable values, asserts no partial thread set is handed back, and asserts RIGHT and LEFT still ingest unchanged. One existing payload, TestOnlyGitHubsOwnBotTypeIsTaggedBot's, was completed with the diffSide GitHub declares non-null; no assertion of any existing test changed.
- gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 586, Lived 13, Not covered 39, Timed out 6, efficacy 97.83 percent: all eight new mutants killed, the thirteen commented equivalents unchanged, and the two ParseSide mutants gremlins first reported as not covered are killed by TestParseSideAdmitsRightAndLeftAndNothingElse in internal/git.

tasks.title: Record anchor context without migrating it
tasks.acceptance:
- An anchor is bound to the head it was produced against. cr never migrates an anchor across a head change in v0.1. Migration is the first thing v0.2 adds, and guessing at it silently is worse than declaring the round stale per §9.3, per §9.2.2.
- The context window and content hash are recorded even though v0.1 never migrates, so that a v0.2 migration has what it needs from rounds v0.1 produced, per §9.2.3.
- A test asserts a head change produces stale records and no migrated anchor, while the context window survives on disk.
- Measured 2026-09-11 on deligoez/cr-qa#1: `cr record` stores every anchor with `content_hash: ""` (all four records), so the waiver key §7.4.1 builds from a draft discard shrinks to path plus class and keeps suppressing after the code under it changes. A test asserts a recorded anchor carries the hash of its lines at the recorded head, and that a waiver written from it carries the same hash.
tasks.closed_reason:
- An anchor is bound to the head it was produced against: internal/cli/recordanchors.go stampAnchors resolves every accepted anchor against anchorTrees at meta.json's recorded head (and the merge base against it), and cr brief's §9.3.4 invalidation rewrites only a record's state field in raw JSON, so nothing re-reads an anchor at a later head.
- cr never migrates an anchor across a head change: TestAHeadChangeStalesTheRecordsAndMigratesNoAnchor in internal/cli/anchorstamp_test.go records f1 at lines 42-44, commits a head inserting five lines above them, runs cr brief, and asserts the stored anchor is equal field for field to the one recorded (still 42-44, same hash); a hand mutant writing a moved 47-49 anchor during invalidation turns it red.
- Migration stays v0.2's: no code path added here computes a new position, and stale is what the head change produces, asserted by the same test (state stale after the increment).
- The context window and content hash are recorded per §9.2.3: finding.Reanchor became finding.StampAnchor in internal/finding/anchor.go, which validates and resolves the anchor and then stamps the normalised hash of start_line..line and up to three lines of context on each side, cut at the file ends; cr record calls it for every record before any write, and §7.2's marker edit in internal/draft/edits.go reaches the same function. TestStampAnchorRecordsTheHashAndAWindowCutAtTheFileEnds covers top, middle and bottom of a file, and a +1 window mutant turns it red.
- That recording is for a v0.2 migration: v0.1 reads neither value back for positioning, and the head-change test asserts the context window (handler lines 39-41) survives on disk after the round goes stale.
- TestAHeadChangeStalesTheRecordsAndMigratesNoAnchor asserts the head change produces a stale record, no migrated anchor, and the context window still on disk.
- The 2026-09-11 measurement was re-checked before changing anything: at 8cdf48b cr record did not compute the hash at all, it stored the agent's value unchanged (dogfood record with content_hash 0123456789abcdef came back as 0123456789abcdef), so an agent that omitted it stored "" exactly as measured on cr-qa#1. After the fix the dogfood record stored {"content_hash": "aa43f4175e6650c7", "context_before": ["package lib", "", "func Load() {"], "context_after": ["}"]} for lib.go:4.
- TestARecordedAnchorCarriesTheHashOfItsLinesAndItsWaiverTheSame records aRecord's anchor (typed hash 0123456789abcdef), asserts the stored content_hash is AnchorContentHash of handler lines 42-44 at recordHead with context 39-41 and 45-47, then deletes the block from cr draft and asserts the pull-request waiver §7.4.1 writes carries that same hash; removing the stampAnchors call turns it red. recordedHome now builds a deterministic commit whose id is recordHead (103679608f0a…) so the 19 record fixtures that broke under the stamp resolve their anchors.

tasks.title: Define the seven record states
tasks.acceptance:
- A record's life in v0.1 ends when it is posted. Everything after that — the author replying, pushing, and the reviewer verifying, resolving, or withdrawing — is the re-review half of the loop, and lands in v0.2 per §1.3.
- The seven states of the §9.1 table: draft (recorded, not yet queued), queued (rendered into the current draft), duplicate (§6.4.3), suppressed (§3.5.4), discarded (deleted during triage, waiver written, disposition set), posted (sent to GitHub, thread created), stale (abandoned unposted when the head moved, §9.3.4).
- Terminal states are posted, discarded, duplicate, suppressed, and stale. Every other state is open per §1.1, per §9.1.2.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A record's life ends at posting, and StatePosted is where internal/finding/state.go's vocabulary stops: nothing follows it, and the type's doc says so in the words §9's opening paragraph uses.
- The four states the re-review half would need — verified, resolved, accepted, withdrawn — are unrepresentable rather than merely absent, because State is a struct around an unexported name that nothing outside state.go can build and ParseState is the only door in from a string; TestTheSevenStatesAreTheOnesTheSpecWrites puts all four through it and reads the §1.3.6 pointer back out of the error, so a later contributor cannot widen the set by writing a literal anywhere in the tree.
- The seven of the §9.1 table are StateDraft, StateQueued, StateDuplicate, StateSuppressed, StateDiscarded, StatePosted and StateStale, each documented with the meaning and cross-reference the table gives it, held in table order by the states literal and handed out only as a copy by States(); ParseState round-trips every name, MarshalJSON and UnmarshalJSON carry them to and from findings.ndjson under the same check with §6.1's row switched to omitzero, and TestTheSevenStatesAreTheOnesTheSpecWrites and TestAStateOutsideTheTableNeverReachesARecord pin the exact set, the copy, and the refusal of an eighth on the wire.
- §9.1.2's five — posted, discarded, duplicate, suppressed, stale — are the one list written out, in the order that item writes them, and State.Terminal() reads only that literal.
- §1.1's open set is derived from the terminal list rather than restated, by State.Open() and by OpenStates(), so §10.2.4's "no record remains in draft or queued" cannot drift from it; TestOpenIsEveryStateThatIsNotTerminal asserts over the whole table that no state falls into both halves or neither, that the derived open set is exactly draft and queued, and that the zero State is neither open nor terminal.

tasks.title: Enforce the exhaustive transition table
tasks.acceptance:
- Transitions are exhaustive. The six rows of the §9.1 transition table: new record to draft by cr record; draft to duplicate or suppressed by cr record; draft to queued by cr draft; queued to discarded by cr draft or cr post --confirm; queued to posted by cr post --confirm or cr post --reconcile on adopt; draft or queued to stale by cr brief on a new head per §9.3.4.
- A transition not listed is rejected with exit code 4, naming the record and its current state.
- cr merge is not a producer: it runs on role output files before any record exists, and §6.4.3 marks duplicates as cr record writes them.
- A table-driven test asserts every listed transition succeeds and a representative sample of unlisted ones exits 4.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/transition.go holds §9.1's transition table as six rows in the spec's own three columns, so a cell holding several values stays one row and the decision is a lookup into what those rows expand to, closed by default because §9.1 says a transition not listed MUST be rejected.
- Row one, creation to draft by cr record, is spelled with a From type rather than a State: Creation is a value no State can equal, and the zero From is Existing of the zero State, which no row names, so state.go's deliberate reading of the zero State as neither open nor terminal is left intact.
- Row two, draft to duplicate and draft to suppressed by cr record, puts §6.4.3's duplicate marking and §3.5.4's thread suppression at the command that writes the record.
- Row three, draft to queued by cr draft, and row four, queued to discarded by cr draft and by cr post --confirm, are listed with their actors, which is why the actor is part of the key rather than context around it.
- Row five, queued to posted by cr post --confirm and by cr post --reconcile, gives the reconcile the one move §9.1 allows it and refuses it the discard row four gives cr post --confirm, and the on-adopt qualifier stays a precondition cr post checks before it asks.
- Row six, draft to stale and queued to stale by cr brief, is §9.3.4's move, and the new-head qualifier is likewise a fact about the run that §9.1 gives no state to read from.
- MayTransition returns an IllegalTransitionError for every triple the six rows do not list, naming the record, the state it is in and the actor that asked, with a §12.4 hint listing what §9.1 does allow out of that state, and internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto ExitState, the first error to reach §11.2's code 4, asserted by TestAnUnlistedTransitionExitsWithTheStateCode over five ways the table can be misread.
- cr merge is left no way to be a producer: Actor's only field is unexported so no command outside internal/finding can be one, and TestCrMergeIsNoProducerOfRecordState reads every Actor composite literal out of the package's own non-test source and matches the set against §9.1's third column, then drives cr merge's own door, DecodePerRole, and finds its records in no §9.1 state and a supplied state refused by §6.1.4.
- TestEveryTransitionIsTheTableAndNothingElse is table-driven over §9.1 transcribed by hand rather than read from the implementation, and walks the whole cross product of nine From values, eight To values and six actors, asserting the ten listed cells pass and all 422 others are refused.
- TestARefusalNamesTheRecordAndItsCurrentState covers the queued, posted, creation and no-state renderings, the terminal case where §9.1 lists no move out, and the error's fields as fields rather than as text.
- Gate green and gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 466, Lived 10, efficacy 97.90 percent with the same three known TIMED OUT, and all ten survivors are the previously classified equivalents in cli/context.go, config/config.go, finding/fields.go, finding/id.go, finding/state.go, note/note.go and profile/none.go, none of them in transition.go.
Out of scope: §9.1.1's transitions.ndjson journal is transition-journal, §9.3.4's stale sweep is new-round-invalidation, and the six commands are their own tasks, so nothing here performs or records a transition. internal/finding/validate.go lines 100-103 carry the DocPerRole doc comment sentence twice, a stray duplication left by an earlier unit.

tasks.title: Journal every transition with its actor
tasks.acceptance:
- Transitions are recorded in transitions.ndjson with a timestamp, the head SHA, and the actor, per §9.1.1.
- A test asserts every transition of the §9.1 table leaves exactly one journal line.

tasks.title: Compare the current head every command
tasks.acceptance:
- cr compares the current head to meta.json's recorded head on every command that reads per-PR state, and reports both when they differ, per §9.3.1.
- The stale-round report is an honesty disclosure and survives --quiet per §11.1.
- A test asserts every state-reading command emits the comparison.
- Found by answer-command, assigned here: cr answer reads meta.json for the issue key, so §9.3.1 binds it even though it writes no per-PR state and §9.3.2's refusal therefore does not. The command set this task enumerates is derived from what actually reads per-PR state, not from a hand-kept list.
- Derived 2026-09-12, not a hand-kept list: state.Layout.Briefed is the one door onto a round, and its production callers are internal/cli's draft.go, record.go, rulescheck.go, cells.go, test.go, claims.go, probe.go, sandbox.go and mapcmd.go plus internal/review/run.go; internal/note/answer.go's issueKeyOf reaches meta.json through Layout.ReadMeta instead, which is why cr answer is bound too. Every one of them needs the current head, and gh/pr.go already argues it must be GitHub's headRefOid rather than the local checkout's, so each call site needs a gh read it does not have today. The cheap way in is a package-level currentHead seam in internal/cli whose test default echoes the recorded head, installed once in output_test.go's crHome so no existing fixture has to change.
tasks.closed_reason:
- state.Layout.Briefed now takes a state.CurrentHead the compiler will not let a caller omit and returns a state.Round carrying meta.json's recorded head beside the one GitHub reports, so §9.3.1's comparison is made by the one door every command that reads per-PR state comes through, and Round.Disclosure names both heads whenever they differ.
- state.Round.Disclosure is §11.1's stale-round report in finding.HonestyDisclosure's shape, TestTheStaleRoundReportIsAnHonestyDisclosureTheRefusalRepeats asserts both the interface and that §9.3.2's refusal opens with the same sentence, and internal/cli carries it in the `honesty` field of cr rules check and cr answer, which is the channel quiet-honesty-exemptions will hold the exemption for.
- TestAMovedHeadRefusesEveryWriterAndIsDisclosedToEveryReader runs every command leafCommands finds in the tree against a round whose head really moved and requires each of them to answer §9.3, so a command added later has no row, fails, and has to be given one.
- cr answer is bound and answers through answerHonesty rather than through §9.3.2's refusal: it reads meta.json for the issue key, writes only §3.6's context store, and prints both heads beside the note it stored.
- The command set is derived rather than enumerated: TestTheRoundHasOneDoorAndMetaJSONHasFourReaders reads the callers of Briefed and of the raw ReadMeta beneath it out of the source, and TestEveryFileHoldingARoundAnswersSection93 requires every file that holds a round to name RefuseStale or Disclosure.
- Briefed is reached from exactly internal/cli/head.go's briefedRound and internal/review/run.go's Run, which is what closes the set from the other end: a command cannot obtain a round without supplying the current head.
- ReadMeta has exactly four production readers, each outside §9.3.1's reach for its own reason — Briefed itself, cr brief's two, and note.issueKeyOf, whose command answers §9.3.1 through answerHonesty instead.
- Both suppliers of the current head read GitHub's headRefOid as gh/pr.go argues they must: internal/cli's currentHead seam through ghClient, and review.Sources.currentHead through the client already on its sources.
- The seam's test default is installed once in output_test.go's crHome and echoes the round's own recorded head, so no existing fixture changed shape, and probeFixture puts the gh shim on the PATH as well because three probe tests spawn the built binary.

tasks.title: Refuse writes when the head moved
tasks.acceptance:
- When the heads differ, every command that writes per-PR state refuses with exit code 4, naming both heads; cr brief is the only way forward, per §9.3.2.
- cr post --reconcile is exempt: it anchors nothing and only matches the §8.4.3 payload hash against the PR's existing reviews.
- A test moves the head and asserts every writing command exits 4 while cr brief and cr post --reconcile proceed.
tasks.closed_reason:
- state.Round.RefuseStale raises §9.3.2's StaleRoundError naming both heads, exitCodeFor maps it onto §11.2's code 4, and every command that writes per-PR state calls it immediately after the door hands back the round: cr record, cr claims record, cr cells record, cr map record, cr draft, cr post, cr review, cr sandbox create, cr test and cr probe run.
- The refusal is a method on the round the comparison produced, so it cannot come apart from it, and its hint names `cr brief <pr> --repo <owner>/<repo>` — measured against deligoez/cr-qa#1 with the round recorded at 294b636 and GitHub answering be7e2c75, where all ten printed "§9.3.2 refuses every write to per-PR state until the round moves with it: run `cr brief 1 --repo deligoez/cr-qa`" and exited 4, and `cr brief 1` then opened round 2 at be7e2c75 and `cr draft 1` succeeded.
- cr post --reconcile is exempt and stays exempt by ordering rather than by a second check: newPostCmd refuses every unbuilt flag before any state is read, so the moved head produced §11.2's code 2 naming the flag, and TestPostReconcileIsExemptFromTheStaleHeadRefusal asserts no StaleRoundError is in that chain, which is what will fail if the flag's behaviour is later written on the other side of the round read.
- TestAMovedHeadRefusesEveryWriterAndIsDisclosedToEveryReader moves the head with two real commits on the head branch and gh answering the second, requires exit 4 and both heads from every writer, requires cr rules check and cr answer to run and disclose, and requires cr brief to open round 2 at the new head; its table is compared against leafCommands, so a command added later fails until it is given an answer.

tasks.title: Increment the round on head change
tasks.acceptance:
- cr brief increments meta.json's round index if and only if the current head differs from the recorded head, and then stores the new head, per §9.3.3.
- A same-head cr brief is idempotent.
- A test asserts the index moves exactly once per distinct head.
tasks.closed_reason:
- brief.roundOf compares the head GitHub reports against meta.json's recorded head and returns recorded.Round+1 only when they differ, and brief.metaOf writes that index back with the new head, so the store and the increment are one write.
- A same-head brief returns the index it read, which internal/brief/idempotence_test.go asserts by walking the whole state root and comparing it byte for byte across two runs, and which was dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1: two briefs at head be7e2c75 both reported round 1 and meta.json still reads round 1.
- TestTheRoundIndexMovesExactlyOncePerDistinctHead briefs three times at one head, twice at a second, twice at a third and once back at the first, reading the round off meta.json each time and asserting 1,1,1,2,2,3,3,4; with the head comparison removed from roundOf the same-head repeats report 2 and 3.

tasks.title: Stale records before clearing the mapping
tasks.acceptance:
- On the increment every record still in draft or queued moves to stale, mapping.ndjson is cleared, and cr brief recomputes units and threads for the new head, per §9.3.4.
- Claims are carried forward unchanged; cr brief re-reads the issue text and re-runs the §3.3.3 drift comparison, and never re-extracts.

tasks.closed_reason:

That direction is the one §8.1.2 wants; adding probe to the list closes the reverse for free.

- render.ProbeEvidence keeps kind, target, filter (absent when unfiltered), result and a fenced output_tail under §5.5's own names with nothing composed beside them, asserted whole by TestTheFilterReachesTheEvidenceRegionAndNothingIsClaimedBesideIt and TestAnUnfilteredRunCarriesNoFilterRow; the probe is read out of probes.ndjson by cli.readProbes and carried as draft.Provenances.Probes.

- For a gap probe the region shows the test file beside its output and the result, which is the material the author needs to tell a wrong behaviour from a wrong test (TestTheMutationPatchAndTheGapTestBothReachTheRegion asserts the gap test reaches the region whole).
- capped() cuts the input at post.max_probe_input_bytes on a rune boundary and the row then reads "input (truncated to N of M bytes by post.max_probe_input_bytes):"; the key is render.MaxProbeInputSetting, added to config's table with default 4096 (tests.output_tail_bytes' default, since the spec names the key only in round 9's finding and gives no default), resolved by cr draft through §2.7's layers and asserted end to end by TestTheProbeInputCapIsReadFromTheConfiguration via CR_POST_MAX_PROBE_INPUT_BYTES=8.
- TestTheMutationPatchAndTheGapTestBothReachTheRegion asserts the mutation patch and the gap test both reach the region whole, and TestATruncatedInputIsAnnounced plus TestATruncatedInputIsCutOnACharacterBoundary assert the announcement, the exact-cap boundary, a negative cap, and a cut inside a multi-byte character.
- render.gapLimit carries §5.4.4's own sentence ("a failed gap probe means either the behaviour is wrong or the supplied test is wrong, and cr cannot distinguish the two") as a "limit:" row, so the limit reaches the reader in the posted comment and not only the spec.
- The limit row stands beneath a gap probe's result and never in a mutation probe's region, asserted by TestTheMutationPatchAndTheGapTestBothReachTheRegion.
- internal/render/separation_test.go's recordKeepers now lists probe, with a comment naming why: render imports probe for this region.
- That keeps the dependency in §8.1.2's direction, renderer reads record, and TestNoRenderingDecisionCanReachStoredState already fails if probe ever imports render.
- Adding probe to the list costs nothing today (probe imports no render) and closes the reverse edge by construction; a Reserved sequence in a probe's input, output or a citation path is refused naming the record (TestAnEvidenceRegionCarryingTheReservedSequenceIsRefused), and a probed record whose probe probes.ndjson lacks stops cr draft with exit 3 (draft.MissingProbeError, TestADraftOfAProbedRecordWithoutItsProbeExitsThree; exitCodeFor re-measured at cognitive 50 over 151 statements).

tasks.title: Validate suggestion ranges within one hunk
tasks.acceptance:
- A suggestion maps to a contiguous line range that exists in the PR diff on the RIGHT side, per §8.2.1, and the range is within one hunk, per §8.2.2.
- A suggestion failing validation blocks posting with exit code 1 and names the record id, per §8.2.4.
- A test covers an out-of-diff range, a range spanning two hunks, and a LEFT-side range.
- Round 12 finding suggestion-range-unbound, assigned here: the implementation bounds the suggestion's line count against the hunk it sits in rather than accepting any contiguous range.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/suggestion/validate.go admits a suggestion only when the record's anchored range is contiguous on the RIGHT side and falls inside the head range of one RIGHT-side hunk of that path, per §8.2.1 and §8.2.2, and TestARangeInsideOneHunkIsAdmitted asserts both hunk edges and both hunks of the fixture.
