- TestARangeOutsideOneHunkIsRefusedNamingTheRecord covers a line the diff does not carry, a file it does not touch, a LEFT-side anchor, a hunk that adds no line, a range spanning two hunks, a backwards range, and a range starting at line 0.
- Round 12's suggestion-range-unbound is closed by binding the replaced range to anchor.start_line..anchor.line in the package doc and by bounding that range against one hunk, so a contiguous range whose ends sit in two hunks is refused rather than accepted.

tasks.title: Warn on mismatched suggestion indentation
tasks.acceptance:
- cr never infers intent about indentation. When the leading whitespace of the suggestion's first line differs from that of the first replaced line, cr warns and shows both, and still posts when the user leaves the block in place, per §8.2.3.
- A test asserts the warning appears and the post proceeds.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/suggestion/indent.go infers nothing: WarnIndentation compares the leading whitespace of two lines and returns a warning or nil, it never edits a suggestion or refuses one, and Validate still passes the mismatching record so §8.2.4 blocks nothing on indentation.
- WarnIndentation reads the suggestion's first line and the first line the anchored range replaces out of the round's hunks, returns both whole on IndentationWarning, and internal/cli/indentation.go carries them into cr draft's warnings field, where String quotes both so a tab and four spaces are told apart on a terminal.
- TestAReindentingSuggestionIsWarnedAboutAndStillDrafted drives a rule whose fix re-indents through cr rules check, cr record and cr draft, and asserts the printed warning shows both lines while draft.md still carries the suggestion block and the stored record still carries the replacement; TestASuggestionIndentedLikeItsLineIsNotWarnedAbout and TestAnIndentationMismatchDoesNotBlockPosting hold the other two halves.

tasks.title: Post every comment as one review
tasks.acceptance:
- All comments in a round are posted as one GitHub review, so the author receives a single notification, per §8.3.1.
- The review event is COMMENT in v0.1; cr never emits APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES, per §8.3.2.
- A test asserts one review-creation call for a multi-comment round and that no other event value is reachable.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/post/review.go turns a round's queued records into one Review and posts it through a single Create call: Build makes one comment per record, Request names the one reviews endpoint, and there is no per-comment door for a caller to loop over, so three comments are one call and one notification.
- The event is an unexported constant with no parameter and no setter, so every payload cr builds carries COMMENT: Build writes it and Payload writes it again over whatever the struct holds.
- Neither verdict event exists as a string anywhere in what cr ships, which is what makes emitting one unreachable rather than merely unintended.
- TestAMultiCommentRoundIsOneReviewCreationCall counts the calls a three-comment round makes through a recording Sender and asserts the one argument vector, TestAnEventWrittenOntoTheReviewDoesNotReachThePayload writes each verdict onto the struct and reads COMMENT back out, and TestNoStringCrShipsHoldsAVerdictEvent parses every non-test Go file and finds neither verdict in any string literal.

tasks.title: Compute the payload hash over preimage
tasks.acceptance:
- The exact posted payload is written to rounds/<n>/posted.json before the network call, and updated with returned thread ids after it, per §8.3.3.
- The payload hash is computed over an explicit pre-image, never over a JSON serialisation whose field order or spacing is unspecified: each comment contributes its path, start_line, line, side, and body joined by LF, in that order; the comments are ordered by path ascending, then start_line, then line, then side with LEFT before RIGHT, then record id by numeric suffix; the per-comment texts are joined by LF; and the payload hash is the normalised hash per §1.4 of the result.
- The review body is excluded, so embedding the hash in it per §8.4.3 cannot change the value being embedded.
- A test fixes the hash for a known three-comment payload and asserts reordering the input does not change it.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/posted.go's writePosted publishes review.Payload()'s exact bytes to rounds/<n>/posted.json and answers with the path post.Request sends as --input, and adoptThreads adds the returned thread ids to that same document through state.UpdateRoundSection, which leaves the payload fields standing; the network call between them arrives with confirm-flag-required, which is the task that mints §8.5's confirmation.
- internal/post/hash.go's Comment.preimage joins one comment's path, start_line, line, side and body with LF in that order, a single-line comment contributing the 0 the payload carries for its absent start_line.
- compareComments orders the comments by path ascending, then start_line, then line, then side where LEFT sorts before RIGHT, then the record id through finding.IDSuffix, falling back to the whole id string so the order stays total for an id cr did not write.
- Review.Preimage joins the per-comment texts with LF, sorting pointers into the slice so the request itself keeps the order §8.3.1 queued it in.
- Review.Hash is text.NormalisedHash of that pre-image, which is §1.4's six steps and its sixteen-character lowercase digest, reached through the one entry point that normalises inside.
- The pre-image reads r.Comments alone, so TestTheReviewBodyReachesNoDigest sets a body holding the hash and gets the same value back, which is what makes §8.4.3's embedding constructable at all.
- TestThePayloadHashIsFixedAndSurvivesReordering pins 420012ebffc2b992 for the three-comment round aRound builds, a digest computed outside the tree, and asserts a reversed comment slice hashes to it unchanged.

tasks.title: Pre-validate every comment position before posting
tasks.acceptance:
- The GitHub review-creation call is atomic: it either creates the review with all its comments or creates nothing. cr therefore pre-validates every comment position per §8.2 before the call, per §8.4.1.
- A test asserts an invalid position is caught before any network call is attempted.
tasks.closed_reason:
- post.Create sends one review-creation call for whatever the round holds, so the comment count reaches GitHub as the payload's length and never as a number of calls, which is the atomicity §8.4.1 rests on and which TestAMultiCommentRoundIsOneReviewCreationCall pins.
- internal/cli/positions.go's validatePositions holds every queued record to suggestion.Validate against the round's hunks, and buildReview calls it after the forcings and the draft's discards and before buildPayload renders anything; a round carrying no suggestion reads no diff at all, which is the guard indentationWarnings already makes at draft time.
- TestAnUnplaceablePositionStopsThePostBeforeAnythingIsSent anchors a record at line 400 of a fixture whose diff spans lines 3 to 7, runs cr post, and gets a suggestion.RangeError naming f1 at exit 1 with nothing printed, while TestAPlaceablePositionReachesThePayload posts the same record at line 4 into the payload.

tasks.title: Report rejected positions with record ids
tasks.acceptance:
- If the call is rejected, no state is marked posted. cr reports every position GitHub named invalid, with the record id it belongs to, and exits 4, per §8.4.2.
- A test asserts findings.ndjson holds no posted state and no triage outcome event after a rejection.
tasks.closed_reason:
- If the call is rejected, no state is marked posted: §9.1's only edge into posted and §7.3.1's outcome events both sit past the network call, and internal/cli/rejected.go's rejectedPost is the only thing on the rejection branch; TestARejectedCallNamesEveryPositionAndMovesNothing asserts every record of findings.ndjson still queued after a refused call.
- cr reports every position GitHub named invalid, with the record id it belongs to, per §8.4.2: internal/post/reject.go's Rejection decodes GitHub's own document and attributes each error entry to the records it could be about — every comment of the round when the entry names a field and no comment, and the comments on the named path when its words name one — so no position is reported without a record id and none is attributed on evidence the API did not give. Measured against gh api search/issues that the document arrives on stdout, so internal/gh/run.go's CommandError now keeps it.
- cr exits 4: exitCodeFor maps *post.RejectedError onto ExitState, deliberately ahead of the 3 a gh.CommandError takes, and TestARejectedCallNamesEveryPositionAndMovesNothing asserts the code; TestOnlyGitHubSayingNoIsARejection asserts the two failures that are not §8.4.2's still code 3.
- A test asserts findings.ndjson holds no posted state and no triage outcome event after a rejection: TestARejectedCallNamesEveryPositionAndMovesNothing drives a real cr draft round, refuses the call with the 422 document gh would have written, and asserts both — every stored record queued, and the ledger still holding only f1:raised and f2:raised.

tasks.title: Embed the hash beneath axis disclosure
tasks.acceptance:
- To make a round identifiable after the fact, cr embeds the payload hash as an HTML comment in the review's own body before posting, per §8.4.3.
- Above it the body carries the disclosure of §4.5.4 — the active axes, and the disabled and unavailable ones with their reasons — so the honesty obligation reaches the author and not only the reviewer's terminal.
- The review body is not a line comment and is unaffected by §1.6.1.
- A test asserts both the disclosure and the hash comment appear in the review body.
- §8.4.3's disclosure is every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, with its reason — not only the disabled and unavailable axes. A skipped role and the unavailable reinvention half reach the author too.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr embeds the payload hash as an HTML comment in the review's own body before posting, per §8.4.3: internal/render/reviewbody.go's PayloadHashComment writes `<!-- cr:payload-hash <hash> -->` on the Reserved sequence §8.1.3 already refuses an agent body for, and internal/cli/post.go's discloseInBody sets it on the review the payload is marshalled from; TestTheEmbeddedHashIsThePayloadHashOfTheComments asserts the embedded value equals review.Hash(), and that moving the body leaves the hash unchanged, which is what §8.3.3's comment-only pre-image buys.
- Above it the body carries the disclosure of §4.5.4, so the honesty obligation reaches the author and not only the reviewer's terminal: ReviewBody writes the active axes and then one line per entry that did not run, and the hash comment last; TestTheReviewBodyCarriesTheDisclosureAboveTheHash asserts the order by position rather than by presence, and TestThePostedPayloadCarriesTheBody asserts it again in the marshalled payload.
- The review body is not a line comment and is unaffected by §1.6.1: ReviewBody takes no anchor and the body is set on the Review rather than appended to its Comments; TestTheReviewBodyIsNotOneOfTheComments asserts the payload holds one comment per queued record and none of them is the body, and TestTheDisclosureIsNotRenderedIntoAComment asserts no comment body carries the disclosure or the marker.
- A test asserts both the disclosure and the hash comment appear in the review body: TestTheReviewBodyDisclosesEveryLensThatDidNotRun and TestTheEmbeddedHashIsThePayloadHashOfTheComments do it through buildPayload over a real cr draft round.
- §8.4.3's disclosure is every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run with its reason, not only the disabled and unavailable axes: discloseInBody reads coverage.Lenses.Disclosures() from status.go's lensesOf, the one derivation of §4.5.4 in the tree, so the posted body and cr status cannot disagree about what did not look; the cost was paid rather than avoided, since lensesOf needs the round's head and, when a symbol index exists, the round's diff, so halfHunks now reads that diff only when the index arrived — measured byte-identical cr status output against a binary built from HEAD.
- A skipped role and the unavailable reinvention half reach the author too: TestTheReviewBodyDisclosesEveryLensThatDidNotRun asserts an unavailable axis, §4.3.1's reinvention half, §4.4.1's symbol half and a role skipped per §4.6.4 all present in the body with their reasons, over a fixture that arranges for none of them.

tasks.title: Reconcile an unresolved post by hash
tasks.acceptance:
- If the outcome is unknown — a timeout, a dropped connection, or a response cr cannot parse — cr sets post_unresolved on meta.json and never retries automatically, per §8.4.4.
- cr post <pr> --reconcile lists the PR's reviews, matches the embedded payload hash of §8.4.3, and either adopts that review as posted or clears post_unresolved for a retry. Posting twice is a worse failure than posting late.
- A test simulates a timeout, then reconciles to an adopt and to a clear, asserting the posted index is written only on adopt.
tasks.closed_reason:
- postOutcome is §8.4's fork: GitHub's error document, read off gh.CommandError's standard output by post.Rejection, is §8.4.2's refusal and is returned as it stands, while everything post.Rejection answers nil for -- a timeout, a dropped connection, a response cr cannot parse -- sets post_unresolved on meta.json through setPostUnresolved and returns an error naming `cr post <pr> --reconcile`; there is no branch in it that sends again, and TestARejectionIsNotAnUnknownOutcome asserts the refusal leaves the flag alone while TestAnUnresolvedPostingIsReconciledToAnAdoptAndToAClear's fixture asserts a killed call sets it.
- `cr post <pr> --reconcile` is built: reconcilePost reads the payload §8.3.3 wrote before the call, takes §8.4.3's hash off it, lists the pull request's reviews through gh.Client.Reviews, and either adopts the review whose body embeds that hash -- walking §9.1's `queued` → `posted` row under ActorPostReconcile and appending §9.3.6's index entries -- or clears post_unresolved for a retry; dogfooded against a scratch pull request, where the clear run printed `"adopted": ""` with post_unresolved going True → False and the record left `queued`, and the adopt run printed `"adopted": "https://github.com/deligoez/cr-qa/pull/1#pullrequestreview-2"`, `"records": ["f1"]`, moved the record to `posted` and wrote the index entry.
- Posting twice is guarded at three points rather than asserted: the hash is taken from the payload that was sent and never from a rebuild of the round, so an edit since the call cannot turn a posted round into an unmatched one; a round whose posted.json holds no payload, or names a different number of records than comments, is refused rather than cleared, because clearing is what invites the second post; and a second `--reconcile` over an adopted round changes nothing, since the records are already `posted` and AppendPosted keys by §7.4.1.
- TestAnUnresolvedPostingIsReconciledToAnAdoptAndToAClear drives one fixture through both answers GitHub can give and asserts posted-index.ndjson is written on adopt and empty on clear, with the records left `queued` and post_unresolved cleared in the clear case; the timeout it starts from is produced through postOutcome rather than declared, so the §8.4.2/§8.4.4 fork is what the fixture exercises.

tasks.title: Print the payload without any write
tasks.acceptance:
- cr post without --confirm validates, prints the full payload, reports "posted": false, and exits 0 without any network call, per §8.5.1.
- Validation runs before the confirmation gate. A cr post whose payload fails validation exits 1 whether or not --confirm was given; only a payload that passes validation reaches §8.5.1's exit 0, per §11.2.
- A test asserts a dry run makes no network call and that an invalid payload exits 1 under both flag settings.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `cr post` without `--confirm` validates, prints the whole payload -- §8.3.2's event, §8.4.3's review body and every comment's position and text, in the JSON document and in the terminal alike -- reports `"posted": false` through §12.6's embedded posting, and exits 0 without sending anything; dogfooded against a scratch pull request, where the run printed the body carrying `<!-- cr:payload-hash c7df7ce5b77ec239 -->`, the comment at `lib.go:5 RIGHT`, `"posted": false` and `exit=0`, and the terminal rendering closed with `not posted: nothing was sent to GitHub`.
- The flag is read once at the top of newPostCmd and acted on last, at the end of buildReview, so every refusal §8 and §6.3 make stands above the gate and the gate decides what becomes of a payload rather than whether one is checked.
- An invalid payload exits 1 under both flag settings: dogfooded on the same scratch pull request, where a question body holding no "?" gave §8.1.5's refusal and `exit=1` both with and without `--confirm`, and TestAnInvalidPayloadExitsOneUnderBothFlagSettings asserts the same over ExitValidation while also asserting the refusal is the payload's rather than the unbuilt flag's.
- Only a payload that passed every validation reaches §8.5.1's branch: the valid scratch round gave `exit=0` and the printed payload without the flag, and §11.2's code 2 naming the unbuilt write with it, because §8.5.2's call is still sendReview's to fill in -- it takes the gh.Confirmation minted from the flag and from nothing else, so confirm-flag-required adds a body rather than moving a branch.
- TestADryRunPrintsThePayloadAndSendsNothing recomputes §8.4.3's hash from the printed comments and matches it against the hash embedded in the printed body, so a document that dropped or reordered a comment could not agree with itself, and asserts over every gh invocation the run made that none carries a request body; TestAnInvalidPayloadExitsOneUnderBothFlagSettings drives one invalid round both ways and asserts exit 1 each time.

tasks.title: Require confirm for every network write
tasks.acceptance:
- Invariant 3: --confirm is required for every network write, on every round, per §8.5.2.
- There is no configuration setting, environment variable, profile field, or alias that removes the gate or supplies --confirm implicitly, per §8.5.3.
- A test attempts to supply the gate through each of the four channels and asserts all four fail.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/send.go's sending.send is the network write, and it is reachable only from the one branch of buildReview that read --confirm: the token is minted by gh.Confirm at internal/cli/post.go and nowhere else (nowrite_test.go's mintSites), post.Create takes a post.Sender that only a gh.Confirmation satisfies, and a Confirmation built anywhere else is the zero value whose Write refuses — so no shape of the call omits the flag, on any round. TestConfirmSendsOneReviewAndSettlesTheRound drives a real `cr post 7 --confirm` against a `gh` shim and measures one review-creation call carrying --input rounds/2/posted.json, the records in state posted, §9.3.6's index entry, §8.3.3's thread ids and §7.3.1's outcome events; TestARejectedCallMarksNothingPosted drives the same command against a refusing shim and measures exit 4 with none of them written.
- §2.7's protection already closes two of the four channels and this task closes the other two: a config key or CR_ variable whose name carries the word confirm or gate is refused by config.checkProtected with exit code 3, an unknown key in a profile is not read at all because profile.Parse decodes §2.4's table and nothing else, and the flag has no second spelling — TestThePostCommandOffersTheGateExactlyOneSpelling reads `cr post` off the tree and holds it to no cobra alias anywhere in the command surface, no shorthand on --confirm, and exactly the two local flags §11 names, so an invented one is §11.2's malformed invocation.
- TestNoChannelButTheFlagSuppliesTheConfirmationGate attempts all four in one table — post.confirm in ~/.cr/config.json, CR_POST_CONFIRM=true, confirm and post.confirm in the resolved profile, and --yes on the command line — and asserts each the same way, at the write door rather than about the code: a `gh` shim on the run's own PATH records every invocation and none of the four produced one carrying a request body, the runs that completed reported "posted": false, and no record left state queued. The fence beneath it is internal/cli/noghbinary_test.go and internal/gh/noghbinary_test.go, whose TestMain puts a refusing `gh` at the front of each test binary's PATH: a test in this tree that reaches the production binary now fails with that refusal instead of a network call, which is measured by TestNoTestInThisPackageCanReachTheProductionGh at both doors and by TestAShimOnTheTestsOwnPathOverridesTheFence for the override every real test needs.

tasks.title: Report confirmation without claiming human reading
tasks.acceptance:
- cr never claims that a human read the draft. The only fact it can establish is that --confirm was given, and the round summary records exactly that and the payload hash, and nothing more, per §8.5.4.
- cr never reports whether draft.md changed as evidence of human involvement: §8.1.2 requires the agent to rewrite every body before the human sees it, so the file has always changed and the signal measures nothing.
- Any output describing the gate says that confirmation was given, never that the review was read.
- A test greps gate-related output for read-claiming wording and asserts none appears.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr never claims that a human read the draft: no literal in cr post's line, its JSON document or its summary share names a reading, a reader or a human, which gatehonesty_test.go TestTheGateReportsConfirmationAndNeverAReading asserts over a real dry run and a real confirmed post against a gh shim.
- The round summary records that --confirm was given and the payload hash and nothing more about the gate: internal/cli/summary.go adds summaryConfirmGiven ("confirm_given") to summaryOwners under cr post, and internal/cli/reconcile.go's writeAdopted writes it with posted and payload_hash, so it is present on exactly the rounds a sent or adopted review finalised and absent (never null) on a dry run or a refused call (summary_test.go TestAnUnpostedRoundSummaryOmitsThePayloadHashAndStillValidates); the --reconcile path writes it too because post_unresolved has one setter, postOutcome, reached only from send, which takes the gate's confirmation. The key is spelled after the flag because citedregister_test.go's §6.2.4 fence forbids the literal "confirmed". Before this commit summary.json held posted and payload_hash and no statement that --confirm was given; posted stays because §10.3 lists it as a count, and the test pins cr post's share to exactly those three keys.
- cr never reports whether draft.md changed as evidence of human involvement: no summary key, document field or line mentions the draft. gatehonesty_test.go TestTheGateReportsConfirmationAndNeverAReading rewrites f1's body in draft.md (§8.1.2's agent rewrite) before both runs, then requires cr post's share of summary.json to be exactly confirm_given, payload_hash and posted, and requires none of them, the gate line, or the document to match readClaiming (which includes draft, edited, changed, modified). Hand mutant: adding `DraftChanged bool json:"draft_changed"` to posting made that test fail on both runs ("the dry run's \"draft_changed\" claims a reading"), reverted to the identical revision.
- Output describing the gate says confirmation was given: internal/cli/output.go posting gains ConfirmGiven (json confirm_given) and line() now prints "posted: --confirm was given, and the review was sent to GitHub" and "not posted: --confirm was not given, and nothing was sent to GitHub"; post.go and send.go set it at the two emit sites. Dogfooded on a local scratch repo with a self-contained gh shim: before, the confirmed post printed "posted: the review was sent to GitHub" and the dry run "not posted: nothing was sent to GitHub"; after, the lines above, JSON `"posted": true, "confirm_given": true`, and summary.json `"confirm_given": true`; git status --porcelain in the repo under review stayed empty.
- A test greps gate-related output for read-claiming wording: gatehonesty_test.go's readClaiming regex (read, reader, reviewed, approved, human, draft, edited, changed, ...) with underscore as a separator is applied to the dry and confirmed runs' gate line, their JSON documents without the payload, and cr post's summary share, and TestReadClaimingCatchesTheForbiddenWording shows it convicting five forbidden sentences including `"draft_edited": true` and passing the required line and "already posted". output_test.go and dryrun_test.go assert the new wording.

tasks.title: Report coverage units with claim mapping
tasks.acceptance:
- cr status <pr> reports units total, units with a complete row of cells, units with gaps, and units flagged oversized per §3.4.5, per §10.1.1.
- It reports claims total, claims mapped to units, and the unimplemented-claim entries of §4.1.3, which appear here and nowhere else because they are never posted, per §10.1.2. This includes the surviving set-aside stamp count required by the §4.1.7 carry-forward rule.
- It reports active axes, disabled and unavailable axes with reasons, and skipped roles with reasons per §4.5.4, per §10.1.3.
- A test asserts all three sections against a fixture holding an oversized unit, a gap entry, and a skipped role.
- §10.1.3 reports active axes and every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, with its reason.
- Carried from oversized-unit-split: internal/unit records Cluster.Oversized per §3.4.5, but nothing renders it. The coverage report is where an oversized unit must appear as such, so a reader knows the cap did not bind there.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr status is no longer a stub: statusOf counts §10.1.1 through coverage.RowsOf over the round's units and cells, and a dogfood run against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1 printed "units: 5 total, 1 with a complete row of 3 active role(s), 1 with gaps, 1 oversized" shapes for both the gap case and, once every cell was recorded, "complete": 5, "gaps": 0.
- intentCoverageOf reports §10.1.2's three numbers — claims total, claims mapped to at least one unit, and §4.1.3's unimplemented-claim entries read whole out of intent-gaps.ndjson rather than re-derived, so the entries the report shows are the ones §10.2.3 will read.
- The same report carries SetAside, the count of those entries still holding a §4.1.8 stamp, which is §4.1.7's carry-forward reported from the surviving side since cr map record names only the stamps a re-derivation dropped.
- §10.1.3's first clause is roundAxes, which re-derives activation.Activate from meta.json's recorded profile and issue key through the new intent.Recorded, so the active, disabled and unavailable axes reported are the round's rather than a fresh resolution's; a dogfood run under the generic profile printed the disabled test axis with its §4.5.2 reason.
- skippedRoles derives §4.6.4's roles as the corpus minus meta.json's active set, each carrying the axis's own §4.5.4 sentence verbatim, and the same dogfood run printed "role test-adequacy skipped, per §4.6.4: axis test disabled, per §4.5.2: ...".
- TestStatusReportsCoverageIntentAndTheLensesThatDidNotRun asserts all three sections from one run against a fixture holding an oversized unit with no cells, two §4.1.3 gap entries one of which is set aside, and the test-adequacy role skipped, and TestTheStatusTextCarriesTheCountsAndEveryLensThatDidNotRun asserts the terminal rendering carries the same.
- roundHalves completes §4.5.4's list by computing the reinvention half of §4.3.1 and the symbol half of §4.4.1 the way cr review computes them, over a symbol index at the round's head and the round's own diff, and the four kinds reach the reader through the honesty channel §11.1 exempts from --quiet.
- unit.Unit's Oversized now renders: coverage.Rows.Oversized reaches the payload's coverage.oversized field and the text line's "N oversized", so a reader is told where §3.4.5's cap did not bind.

tasks.title: Report findings by state with probes
tasks.acceptance:
- cr status reports findings and questions by state, severity, and grade, per §10.1.4.
- It reports probes run, and probes that changed a finding's grade, per §10.1.5.
- It reports waivers applied and duplicates suppressed in the current round, per §10.1.6 — an honesty disclosure that survives --quiet per §11.1.
- It reports notes retracted in the current round per the §3.6.6 same-round rule.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/statusrecords.go's recordTalliesOf is §10.1.4 over the round's findings and questions, and statusResult.Records carries the total beside one tally per value of §9.1's seven states, §6.1's four severities and §6.2's three grades, zeros included, with a stored value outside a vocabulary given a row of its own so each count sums to the total.
- probesOf is §10.1.5: Run is the round's probe records read through state.ReadStamped, and Graded is the distinct probes standing behind a record graded probed, which §6.2's table makes unreachable without one.
- duplicateDisclosure counts §6.4.3's retained duplicates off findings.ndjson and waiverDisclosure reads §6.4.4's count out of the round summary through the new state.ReadRoundSection, both appended to statusResult.Honesty, which is the one channel §11.1 exempts; TestStatusDisclosesTheWaiverAndDuplicateCountsUnderQuiet asserts `cr status --quiet` prints the identical list.
- internal/cli/statusnotes.go's unstandingNotesOf reports every note the round's cells or records cite that no longer stands, the cell by §4.5.5's note_id and the record through the claim §3.3.1 gave a note_id, in the round the retraction happened in per note.Standing's reading of §3.6.6.

tasks.title: Decide completeness from four conditions
tasks.acceptance:
- A round is complete when all four §10.2 conditions hold: the current head equals the head the round was recorded against per §9.3.1; every unit has a complete row of cells for every active role, and every one of those cells was filled for that unit's current unit hash per §3.4.6; every claim is mapped to at least one unit; and no record of the current round remains in draft or queued.
- A claim carrying an unimplemented-claim entry per §4.1.3 blocks completeness until it is either mapped, or set aside through cr claims set-aside per §4.1.8. The entry is not a record, so §10.2.4 never reaches it; this condition is the only thing that makes an unimplemented claim block, which is what §4.1.3 relies on.
- A test asserts each of the four conditions blocks independently.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/coverage/completeness.go's Complete answers §10.2 over one Conditions value carrying all four, and its HeadMoved field is §10.2.1: §9.3.1's comparison of the round's recorded head against the pull request's current one, reported by headReason when the two differ.
- Conditions.Rows is §10.2.2, counted by RowsOf, which counts a row complete only when every active role filled a cell whose unit_hash is the unit's current §3.4.6 hash, so Rows.Gaps is the whole condition and rowReason names the failing count.
- Conditions.Unsettled is §10.2.3's blocking set, the round's claims that its mapping maps to no unit, and claimReason names each one.
- Conditions.Records is §10.2.4, and recordReason lists every record whose finding.State.Open reports it non-terminal per §9.1.2, naming the open states through finding.OpenStates rather than spelling them.
- TestAnUnimplementedClaimBlocksUntilItIsMappedOrSetAside asserts a claim carrying §4.1.3's entry blocks while it sits in Unsettled and stops blocking once §4.1.8's set-aside stamp takes it out.
- recordReason reads only findings.ndjson's records, so §4.1.3's entry is never among them and §10.2.4 cannot reach it.
- claimReason is therefore the only reason an unimplemented claim contributes, which is the dependence §4.1.3 states.
- TestEachOfTheFourConditionsBlocksCompletenessOnItsOwn breaks one condition at a time against a round on which all four hold and asserts exactly one reason, naming the §10.2 item it came from.

tasks.title: Print the verdict beside missing lenses
tasks.acceptance:
- cr status prints the completeness verdict and, when it is false, the exact reason, per §10.2.
- A verdict of complete is printed together with every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, because completeness across three axes is not completeness across four, and neither is completeness with a role that never looked.
- cr never approves the PR, and never describes a complete round as a settled review: v0.1 ends at posting, and whether the author addressed anything is outside what it can observe.
- A test asserts a complete verdict carries the missing-lens list and that no approval or settled wording is reachable.
tasks.closed_reason:
- statusOf builds coverage.Conditions from the round and hands coverage.Complete's verdict to statusHonesty, which prints it into the honesty channel through coverage.Lenses.Verdict; TestAnIncompleteVerdictCarriesTheExactReason asserts the false verdict names the §10.2.2 and §10.2.3 items that blocked the round.
- The verdict sentence is reachable only through Lenses.Verdict, which appends every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run after it, so a renderer holding the verdict alone cannot print the claim without the list that qualifies it; TestACompleteVerdictIsPrintedWithEveryLensThatDidNotRun asserts the complete round prints its disabled axis, both unavailable lens halves and its skipped role beside the sentence.
- coverage.verdictLine's two branches say only `round complete, per §10.2` and `round not complete, per §10.2: <reason>`, so no output of cr names an approval or calls a round settled.
- TestNoApprovalOrSettledWordingIsReachableOnACompleteRound runs the complete round through both output shapes and asserts neither carries any of eleven approval or settled words, after asserting the verdict sentence was printed at all.

tasks.title: Assign every summary count a writer
tasks.acceptance:
- cr merge, cr draft, and cr post each accumulate their own counts into rounds/<n>/summary.json, which is created by cr merge and finalised by cr post, per §10.3.
- Every round records counts for raised, deduplicated, suppressed by thread, waived, forced to question, drafted, posted, discarded as not-here, and discarded as wrong, plus the comment count against post.max_comments per §1.6.2, the probe cap state, and the payload hash of §8.3.3 — so the history of a review is reconstructable from state alone.
- Round 8 finding unassigned-writer: cr record is added to the writer list and assigned the deduplicated and thread-suppressed counts, since it is what stamps duplicate from duplicate_of per §6.4.3 and writes state suppressed per §3.5.4 — cr merge emits duplicate_of but never stamps state, and cr draft and cr post see only queued records.
- Round 8 finding missing-summary-count: the §9.3.6 already-posted drop count is a distinct key, kept separate from waived so the two suppression reasons stay distinguishable in the reconstructable history §10.3 promises.
- A test asserts every listed count has a named writer and that a shape assertion over summary.json passes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr merge (writeMergeCounts), cr draft (publishDraft through draftSummary.counts) and cr post (writeAdopted, reached from markPosted on --confirm and adoptAsPosted on --reconcile) each write their own counts into rounds/<n>/summary.json through writeSummary in internal/cli/summary.go, which goes through state.UpdateRoundSection so every other field is left byte for byte; cr merge runs first and its write creates the document, and cr post's write after the network call returned is the finalisation.
- summaryOwners records all of them: raised, waived and already_posted to cr merge; deduplicated and suppressed_by_thread to cr record; forced_to_question, new_classes, drafted, discarded_not_here, discarded_wrong, comments (count against post.max_comments) and probe_cap (count against probe.max_per_round) to cr draft; posted and payload_hash to cr post. Dogfooded on a scratch repository through merge, record, draft, two dry runs and --confirm: the final summary held all fourteen keys, and payload_hash 9381b6d7e3086b99 equalled the hash embedded in the sent review body.
- cr record is on the writer list: recordRetiredCounts counts StateDuplicate and StateSuppressed over the round's stored records after appendRecords, and writes deduplicated and suppressed_by_thread as ownerRecord, because stampStates is the only place either state is written.
- 9.3.6's drop count is summaryAlreadyPosted ("already_posted"), a key of its own beside summaryWaived ("waived"), both owned by cr merge; TestEverySection103CountHasANamedWriter asserts the two keys differ.
- internal/cli/summary_test.go's TestEverySection103CountHasANamedWriter lists 10.3's counts independently of the table and asserts each has one of the four writers and a stated shape; TestTheSummaryWriterTableIsEnforcedAtTheWrite asserts writeSummary refuses another writer's key, an unlisted key and a key written twice, before anything is written; TestTheRoundSummaryCarriesEveryPrePostWritersCounts runs merge, record and draft over a real fixture and passes assertSummaryShape, which decodes every section strictly into a shape stated apart from the writers' types, with raised 3, deduplicated 1, waived 1, drafted 1, comments 1 of 20 and probe_cap 1 of 10; TestConfirmFinalisesTheRoundSummary passes the same shape assertion after --confirm with posted 2 and the sent payload's hash. labelunreachable_test.go's refused-draft check now reads draft.md as empty, since cr record's write opens the round directory and 2.3's EnsureRound creates an empty draft.md with it.

tasks.title: Replace summary sections rather than accumulating
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding non-idempotent-accumulation: each writing command replaces its own section of summary.json on every invocation rather than adding to it, so the file is a function of current state and re-running a command is idempotent. Which keys belong to which writer is stated, mirroring §10.3's writer list.
- None of the writers is once-per-round: §7.1.6 contemplates regenerating the draft, §8.5.1 makes a dry run the normal precursor to cr post --confirm, and re-running cr merge after fixing one role's output is the obvious recovery path. Additive accumulation would inflate the waived, deduplicated, and drafted counts, making the round summary the one place where re-running a command silently changes the record.
- A test runs cr merge twice, cr draft twice, and cr post twice, and asserts every count is unchanged from the single-run case.
tasks.closed_reason:
- writeSummary in internal/cli/summary.go replaces a writer's whole section on every run: completeOwnership refuses a run that leaves out any count summaryOwners gives that writer, and every count is computed from the round's state (raised over the files handed to this merge, deduplicated and suppressed_by_thread over the stored records, drafted and the two discard counts over the round's records, the caps over queued records and the round's probes, posted over the records in posted), so the document is a function of current state and a re-run writes the same values.
- summaryOwners in internal/cli/summary.go states which keys belong to which writer: raised, waived and already_posted to cr merge; deduplicated and suppressed_by_thread to cr record; forced_to_question, new_classes, drafted, discarded_not_here, discarded_wrong, comments and probe_cap to cr draft; posted and payload_hash to cr post — 10.3's writer list with cr record added per round 8.
- writeSummary's doc comment records that none of the writers is once-per-round: 7.1.6 regenerates the draft, 8.5.1 makes the dry run the ordinary precursor to --confirm, and re-running cr merge after fixing one role's output is the recovery path.
- The same comment records that additive accumulation would inflate waived, deduplicated and drafted and make the summary the one place a re-run silently changes the record; summarizeDraft counts discards off the round's records rather than this run's triage for the same reason, since a regeneration after a deletion sees no deletion, and the dogfood run showed discarded_not_here staying at 1 across two regenerations after the deletion.
- internal/cli/summary_test.go's TestRerunningEveryWriterLeavesTheRoundSummaryUnchanged runs cr merge twice, cr draft twice before and twice after a block deletion, and cr post's dry run twice before one --confirm, and asserts the summary equals the single-run case, with discarded_not_here still 1 and the dry-run summaries byte-identical; TestAWriterMustReplaceItsWholeSection asserts a partial section is refused before anything is written, and hand-disabling that check turned it red.

tasks.title: Record the payload hash once built
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding unpostable-round-summary: the payload hash is recorded only once cr post --confirm has built a payload and is absent otherwise, and an unfinalised summary is a valid terminal state for a round. A round that is drafted and never posted, or run only through §8.5.1's dry run, has no posted payload, and whether the key is absent, null, or holds the dry-run hash was undetermined.
- A test asserts an unposted round's summary omits the key entirely and still validates.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The payload hash is recorded only once cr post --confirm has built and sent a payload: summaryPayloadHash is written solely by writeAdopted in internal/cli/reconcile.go (landed in 88912a9), which runs after the network call returned on --confirm and after an adoption on --reconcile, and never on the dry run or on 8.4.2's refused call; the summaryPosted/summaryPayloadHash doc comment in internal/cli/summary.go states that an unfinalised summary is a valid terminal state for a round.
- The undetermined choice is settled as absent: a round drafted and never posted, or run only through 8.5.1's dry run, keeps a summary with neither payload_hash nor posted, never null and never the dry-run hash; dogfooded on a scratch repository, where a round after two dry runs embedded payload hash b3c329358c607f58 in the printed body while summary.json held twelve keys and no payload_hash or posted.
- internal/cli/summary_test.go's TestAnUnpostedRoundSummaryOmitsThePayloadHashAndStillValidates takes a round through a dry run and a --confirm GitHub refuses, then asserts the summary passes assertSummaryShape (every section decodes strictly into its stated shape and none is null), omits payload_hash and posted entirely, and does not contain the dry run's hash; hand-applying a mutant that writes cr post's section with the hash on the dry run turned it red.

tasks.title: Document the full loop in skill
tasks.acceptance:
- skills/cr/SKILL.md ships with the release and documents the full loop: brief, review fan-out, merge, record, probe, draft, human read, post — and that v0.1 stops there, so a moved head means a new round per §9.3, per §13.1.
- It documents the argued rule, that it cannot be overridden, and when to escalate to a probe instead of asserting, per §13.2.
- It documents that every network write needs --confirm, that cr cannot prove the human read the draft, and that the human is therefore the one who must, per §13.4.
- It documents that citations is the machine-readable evidence field and evidence is prose, so a finding without citations is graded argued and posted as a question, per §13.7.
- It documents the comment economy of §1.6: fewer comments, each anchored to the line it concerns, per §13.8.

tasks.title: Document triage verbs with marker semantics
tasks.acceptance:
- SKILL.md documents the draft triage verbs, the marker edit semantics of §7.2, and the difference between discarding as wrong — a marker edit, repository-wide, counted against the class — and as not-here, which is plain deletion, scoped to the pull request, and counted separately, per §13.3.
- It documents the role, profile, and rule file formats, and how to add each, per §13.5.
- It documents that a comment written by hand more than twice belongs in the rule corpus, with a detect block when the violation is mechanically matchable, per §13.6.
- A test asserts SKILL.md names every command of §11.

tasks.title: Depend only on three external commands
tasks.acceptance:
- cr builds as a single binary whose only runtime dependencies are git, gh, and the configured tracker command, per §14.1.
- A test asserts the binary runs with no other executable on PATH beyond those three.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/dependencies_test.go TestTheRunnersStartNothingButGitAndGh parses the two runner files that nowrite_test.go already confines os/exec to, and asserts each one names its program as a plain string literal, internal/git/run.go starting git and internal/gh/run.go starting gh, one invocation each. That closes what an import scan cannot see, because a call naming a variable reads the same to it as a call naming a literal, and a fourth dependency added inside a runner would therefore pass it untouched. crBinary makes the single-binary half a fact rather than a reading, one go build of ./cmd/cr producing one regular file, and that file is what the second criterion runs. The tracker is the third dependency and is treated differently on purpose, because §3.1.1 makes it argv the user configures and §3.1.4 lets --intent-file replace it outright.
- TestTheBinaryRunsWithNothingButGitAndGhOnPath runs that binary on a PATH of one directory holding a symlink to git, a symlink to gh and nothing else, with the directory listing asserted to be exactly those two names, and exercises --version, --help, every registered command with --help, cr init and cr config, in an environment carrying only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR and CR_HOME, the allowlist internal/git and internal/gh had already settled on. jira, the §3.1.2 default tracker, is installed on this machine and deliberately absent from that PATH, and cr config prints the default argv naming it while it stays unreachable, which is what makes the default a default rather than a dependency of every command. Run by hand, that PATH cannot resolve even sh, so the strip is total.

tasks.title: Release archives through GoReleaser on tags
tasks.acceptance:
- Releases are produced by GoReleaser on a v* tag via .github/workflows/release.yml, publishing archives for darwin and linux on both amd64 and arm64, per §14.2.
- go install github.com/deligoez/cr/cmd/cr@<tag> installs the same version as the tag, per §14.4.
- A dry-run GoReleaser build produces all four archives.
tasks.closed_reason:
- .github/workflows/release.yml fires on a push of a v* tag and nothing else, and its goreleaser-action step runs release --clean, so a tag is the only thing that publishes. .goreleaser.yml's one build matrix is now darwin and linux across amd64 and arm64 exactly, the windows entry the pre-spec scaffolding carried having gone with the zip format_overrides that existed only for it. TestAVersionTagIsWhatTriggersARelease pins the trigger and the release verb, and TestTheBuildMatrixIsExactlyTheFourTheSpecNames asserts both sets by ElementsMatch rather than by containment, so adding a platform fails as loudly as losing one, verified by putting windows back and watching it fail. The before-hooks were raised from go test ./... to the gate verbatim, with the release runner installing golangci-lint and deadcode, because a tag is the one moment a mistake cannot be taken back.
- Section 14.4's install path resolves to the module path plus the package directory, and TestTheReleaseBinaryIsTheOneGoInstallNames asserts every half of it, that go.mod declares module github.com/deligoez/cr, that the build's main is ./cmd/cr, and that its binary is cr, so the package go install fetches at a tag and the package GoReleaser builds at that tag are the same one. The version half is asserted where this task can reach it, that the ldflags carry -X github.com/deligoez/cr/internal/cli.version={{.Version}}, the variable root.go prints. go version -m on the archived darwin/arm64 binary confirms both, path github.com/deligoez/cr/cmd/cr and the -X flag applied, and the extracted binary printed cr version 0.0.0-SNAPSHOT-befaac8.
- goreleaser release --snapshot --clean --skip=publish --skip=announce produced exactly four archives and no others, macOS_x86_64.tar.gz, macOS_arm64.tar.gz, linux_x86_64.tar.gz and linux_arm64.tar.gz, down from the six the same command produced before the change. The strengthened before-hooks ran inside that run, all three gate steps passing, and TestEveryGateStepRunsInCIAndAtRelease now derives those steps from the tasks.json quality_gate string rather than restating them, so a future gate change fails until the hooks and the CI workflow both carry it. Mutation testing held at the baseline, Killed 305, Lived 5, efficacy 98.39 percent, unchanged because this unit adds no branching Go code.

Out of scope: section 14.3's Homebrew formula belongs to homebrew-formula, and goreleaser check reports the existing brews block as deprecated in favour of homebrew_casks, which that task should settle. Section 14.5's manifest belongs to skill-marketplace-manifest. Section 14.6 belongs to version-injection, which also owns a real gap this task could only measure, that go install applies no ldflags, so an installed binary prints cr version dev unless root.go falls back to runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo, whose main module version does carry the tag.

tasks.title: Publish the Homebrew formula on release
tasks.acceptance:
- A release updates the Homebrew formula in the deligoez/homebrew-tap repository so that brew install deligoez/tap/cr installs the binary as cr, per §14.3.

tasks.title: Inject the tagged version at build
tasks.acceptance:
- cr --version prints the tagged version, injected at build time via -X github.com/deligoez/cr/internal/cli.version, per §14.6.
- A test asserts an unset version renders as a development marker rather than an empty string.

The buildinfo mod line does carry the tag, so internal/cli reads runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo() as a fallback when the injected version is unset, and a test drives a real go install to assert the tag reaches cr --version.

tasks.title: Expose the skill through the manifest
tasks.acceptance:
- The skill ships inside this repository at skills/cr/SKILL.md, and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json exposes it as an installable plugin, per §14.5.
