tasks.title: Record a round's merged findings
tasks.acceptance:
- cr record <pr> <file> reads the merged NDJSON, validates every line through internal/finding's Decode, and appends the surviving records to findings.ndjson under the per-PR lock, per §11's command table and §9.1's new-record-to-draft transition.
- Validation is the existing one rather than a second copy: a missing required field, an unknown unit, or a borrowed role is refused with exit code 1 naming the file, the one-based line, and the field, and nothing is written when any line is refused.
- A test drives a good file and a file whose third line is bad, asserting the first writes every record and the second writes none and names line 3.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr record <pr> <file> is registered in internal/cli/record.go and root.go: it reads the NDJSON the agent names, hands every line to internal/finding's Decode with the current round's unit ids, stamps §9.1's draft state through MayTransition(Creation -> StateDraft, ActorRecord), and appends the survivors to findings.ndjson under layout.LockPR, per §11's command table and §9.1's first transition row.
- Validation is finding.Decode's and nothing else: TestRecordRefusesTheThreeFaultsSection613Names drives a missing required field, a unit belonging to the round before, and a role borrowed from another role's §4.6.2 output file, and asserts each arrives as the same finding.RejectedRecordError carrying the file, the one-based line and the field, mapped by internal/cli/exit.go onto exit code 1.
- Nothing is written when any line is refused, and that is atomicity by construction rather than rollback: Decode returns no records at all on the first fault, so the single state.AppendStamped publish never runs. TestARefusedLineLeavesFindingsExactlyAsItWas records a round first, then hands in a four-line file whose third line drops evidence, and asserts the error names line 3 and that findings.ndjson is byte-identical afterwards, so neither the two good lines above the fault nor the good line below it were stored.
- TestRecordStoresEveryRecordOfAnAcceptedFile drives the good file and asserts every record reached findings.ndjson in file order, each carrying the three fields the agent may not supply: state draft (§6.1.4), and the head and round of meta.json (§2.3.3).
- state.AppendStamped was added because WriteStamped restamps every record it is handed, which would rewrite earlier rounds' head and round on every append; TestAnAppendLeavesEarlierRoundsAsTheyWere holds the first round's stamp across a second append, per §9.3.5.
- The unit set is scoped to the round because §3.4.6 makes a unit id round-scoped, so roundUnitIDs filters units.ndjson by meta.json's round and a record naming the previous round's unit is refused.
- Dogfooded against a scratch CR_HOME with a hand-written merged.ndjson: two records stored with state, head and round written by cr; refusals for a bad third line, an out-of-round unit and a supplied grade all exit 1 leaving the file byte-identical.

tasks.title: Detect the repository from its remote
tasks.acceptance:
- cr derives owner/repo from the repository under review, so §11.1's --repo is an override rather than the only source, and every PR-scoped command works without it.
- The remote is read through internal/git's pinned runner, never a second exec path, and a repository with no remote, several remotes, or a non-GitHub remote is refused with a named next step rather than a guess.
- A test covers detection from an ssh remote and an https remote, the --repo override winning over both, and each refusal.

tasks.title: Reject a class that is not kebab-case
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by record-command's dogfood run: finding.ValidateClass exists but Decode never calls it, so cr record stores a class like "Not Kebab" without complaint.
- Every door that admits a record rejects a class outside [a-z0-9-]+ with exit code 1, naming the file, the one-based line and the field.
- §6.4's dedup key is built from the class, so a non-canonical class silently splits one group in two; the guard belongs at the door, not at the key.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Reproduced with the built binary before the fix: on a scratch round, a role file carrying `"class":"Not Kebab"` on line 3 went through `cr merge` at exit 0 and `cr record` at exit 0, and findings.ndjson stored `"class": "Not Kebab"` beside a kebab-case record; ValidateClass was called only by internal/rule for a rule file, and by no record door.
- internal/finding/validate.go's shared checker (201f239) now calls ValidateClass right after §6.1.3's required-field walk, so both doors, Decode (cr record, agent and merge sources) and DecodePerRole (cr merge), refuse the class with finding.InvalidClassError, which internal/cli/exit.go already maps to exit 1 with a hint. Measured on a binary built from that tree on the same round: `cr merge` and `cr record` both exit 1 with `review-correctness.ndjson line 3: class "Not Kebab" is not kebab-case; §6.1 fixes the form at [a-z0-9-]+` and hint `§6.1 wants a kebab-case class; correct that record's class in the file`, naming the file, the one-based line counting the blank line, and the field. TestEveryDoorRefusesAClassThatIsNotKebabCase drives every entry of the `doors` table that TestNoUnanchoredItemBecomesARecordByAnyDoor reconciles against the package source, so a door added later is held to the class too; making the check a no-op turns it red. The full suite ran green in a clean clone with only this change applied, so no existing fixture carried a non-kebab class.
- §6.4.1's dedup key reads the class byte for byte, so before the fix "Not Kebab" and "not-kebab" on one anchored line would have formed two groups; after it the first spelling cannot be recorded, so one defect class stays one group.
- The guard sits at the door and not at the key: the dedup key of §6.4.1, the waiver key of §7.4.1, the §9.3.6 posted index and cr stats' §7.3.3 first_seen report all read records that came through Decode, and none of them normalises or re-checks a class, so a record refused at the door never reaches a key in the first place.

tasks.title: Exit 3 on input a command cannot read
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by record-command's dogfood run: a missing input file, or a pull request with no state directory, exits 2 rather than §11.2's 3, because os.ReadFile and state.ReadPR return bare errors that exitCodeFor does not map.
- A shared unreadable-input error type carries the path and maps to ExitFile, so every command that reads a caller-named file answers the same way.
- Exit 2 stays what §11.2 says it is: the command line was wrong, not the file.
- The same holds for a state file a command requires inside an existing state directory: measured, `cr record` on a round with no mapping.ndjson exits 2; it exits 3 and the hint names the command that writes the file (`cr map record`).
- The write side answers the same way: measured 2026-09-12 by the mutation slice, `cr record` against a read-only pull-request directory fails inside state.writeAtomic with a bare `cannot create a temporary file in <dir>` and exits 2, telling the user to retype a command line that was right. Every §2.3 write failure is a file failure and exits 3.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A missing input file and a pull request whose state lacks a file now exit 3: measured on the built binary, `cr record 1 missing.ndjson --repo o/r` went from exit 2 to exit 3, and a round missing probes.ndjson from 2 to 3, because every caller-named read goes through readInput and every state read through Layout.ReadPR, both returning state.FileError.
- state.FileError is the shared type: it carries the path, FileFailure panics on an empty hint, and the exit code table maps it to ExitFile as its last row, so cr record, cr merge, cr claims record, cr map record, cr cells record and cr probe run with --patch or --test all answer the same way.
- Exit 2 stays the malformed invocation: exitCodeFor falls back to ExitUsage only for an error no row claims, and gh.AnswerError, which measured 2 before and 3 after, joined the table so it no longer falls through.
- The state file a command requires inside an existing state directory is covered: `cr record` on a round with no mapping.ndjson measured exit 2 on a build of HEAD before this change.
- It now exits 3 with `hint: ... and cr map record is the command that writes it`, held by TestAMissingStateFileExitsWithTheFileCodeAndNamesItsWriter.
- The write side answers the same way: `cr record` against a read-only pull-request directory measured exit 2 with the bare `cannot create a temporary file` on the HEAD build, and exit 3 after.
- Every 2.3 write failure is a file failure: writeAtomic's four failures and WriteNamedFile return state.FileError, held by TestAWriteThatCannotLandExitsWithTheFileCode and TestAWriteThatCannotLandIsAFileFailure.

tasks.title: Refuse to blank a recorded issue key
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by brief-payload's dogfood run: a cr brief whose intent.key_pattern no longer matches silently rewrites meta.json's issue_key to empty, orphaning every claim already recorded under the old key, since §3.3 forms each claim id as <ISSUE-KEY>#c<n>.
- A brief that would replace a non-empty recorded issue key with a different one, or with none, refuses with exit code 4 and a hint, rather than writing.
- A test records claims under one key, then briefs again with a pattern that matches nothing, and asserts meta.json and claims.ndjson are both untouched.
- Also found by dogfooding: with a tracker-backed profile, cr brief runs the tracker command and fails on a 404 before --intent-file can help, and the error never says --issue is what would have avoided it. The message names it.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The defect brief-payload's dogfood run found is reproduced and closed: a `cr brief` whose intent.key_pattern no longer matched rewrote meta.json's issue_key to empty and said nothing, orphaning every claim recorded as <ISSUE-KEY>#c<n> per §3.3, and internal/brief's refuseRekey now refuses that write.
- A brief that would replace a non-empty recorded issue key with a different one, or with none, refuses rather than writing: refuseRekey returns brief.KeyRewriteError from inside roundOf, before §9.3.3's comparison and before persist is reached, so nothing in the state directory is touched.
- It refuses with exit code 4: internal/cli/exit.go maps KeyRewriteError onto ExitState, TestARewrittenIssueKeyExitsWithTheStateCode holds it there through a wrapping, and the dogfood run exited 4 for both a non-matching pattern and an `--issue OTHER-1`.
- It refuses with a hint: the message names the recorded key, the key §3.2 resolved or "no key at all", the pattern in force, the `cr brief --issue CR-1` that keeps the recorded key, and the state directory to remove to start the pull request over under a new one.
- A test records claims under one key and then briefs again with a pattern that matches nothing: internal/brief/rekey_test.go's TestABriefRefusesToReplaceARecordedIssueKey records CR-7#c1, then re-briefs under `ZZZ-[0-9]+` and under `--issue OTHER-1`.
- That test asserts meta.json and claims.ndjson are both untouched, compared byte for byte before and after rather than field by field, so a rewrite that re-derived the same values would not pass it.
- Also found by dogfooding and now fixed: a tracker-backed profile made `cr brief` run the tracker command and fail on a 404, and the message carried only the command line, the exit status and the tool's stderr.
- The message names `--issue`: intent.CommandError.Error now ends with §3.2's resolution order and `--issue <KEY>` as what corrects a key cr read off the branch, alongside §3.1.4's `--intent-file <path>` for the tracker that cannot be reached whatever the key, and TestAFailedTrackerCommandNamesTheFlagsThatGetPastIt holds both, with and without stderr.
- Dogfooded against an isolated CR_HOME and a local scratch repository with a self-contained gh shim; the refusal printed "round of pull request 1 is recorded under issue key CR-1 and §3.2 resolved no key at all from intent.key_pattern \"ZZZ-[0-9]+\"", meta.issue_key stayed 'CR-1' and claim CR-1#c1 stayed recorded, and `cr brief --issue CR-1` then ran and reported round 1.
- Invariant 2 verified by hand: `git status --porcelain` in the scratch repository was empty and both refs were unchanged after every run.
- The gate is green at 6 commits: `go test -race -count=1 ./...`, `golangci-lint run` at 0 issues, `./scripts/deadcode.sh` silent, and `gofmt -l internal cmd` empty.

tasks.title: Destroy a sandbox whose registration is gone
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by baseline-resolution's dogfood run: when the repository under review has been re-cloned or force-pushed, git worktree remove fails with "is not a working tree" and cr sandbox create then refuses because the directory exists, leaving no way out of cr but rm -rf under ~/.cr by hand.
- cr sandbox destroy falls back to removing the sandbox directory when the registration is already gone, so §5.1.5 has no state it cannot clear.
- A test registers a worktree, removes the registration behind cr's back, and asserts destroy still leaves nothing and that create afterwards succeeds.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Reproduced with the built binary on a scratch repository whose clone was deleted and re-cloned under an existing sandbox: `cr sandbox destroy 1` exited 3 with `fatal: '.../pr-1/sandbox' is not a working tree` and `cr sandbox create 1` then exited 4 with `.../pr-1/sandbox already exists`, so the state was unrecoverable from inside cr.
- internal/sandbox/destroy.go's removeDirectory (3709831) asks git.WorktreeRegistered (22baf72, `worktree list --porcelain -z` compared through resolved symlinks, since git lists /tmp as /private/tmp) whether the repository still lists the sandbox; a listed one is removed through git as before, an unlisted one is deleted by state.Layout.RemoveOrphanedSandbox under the state root and the registrations are pruned. removeSandbox is shared with the §5.1.6 recreation, which takes the same fallback. On the same scratch state the rebuilt binary's destroy exited 0 with `"removed": true`, create exited 0, a second destroy exited 0, `.git/worktrees` was gone, and `git status --porcelain` in the repository under review was byte-identical (empty) before and after.
- TestDestroyRemovesASandboxWhoseRegistrationIsGone creates a sandbox, deletes `.git/worktrees/sandbox` behind cr's back, and asserts Destroy succeeds, leaves neither the directory nor the registration, and that Create afterwards succeeds at the same path; forcing the git branch always makes it fail with git's "is not a working tree". TestWorktreeRegisteredAnswersForTheRegistrationNotTheDirectory holds a worktree named through a symlink as registered, a foreign path and an orphaned directory as not, and comparing unresolved paths fails it. Forcing the fallback for a registered worktree survives: RemoveAll plus prune reaches the same end state as `worktree remove --force` for every sandbox cr creates, so that mutant is equivalent on what the tests can observe.

tasks.title: Test the mapping package where its mutants can die
tasks.acceptance: internal/mapping carries its own test file; today it has none, and gremlins reports all five of its mutants NOT COVERED because default-mode gremlins runs only the mutated package own tests, so nothing in that package can ever be killed. The package is load-bearing: 4.1.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.2.1 all read this one join, and 4.1.6 forbids any second opinion about which claim covers which unit. The tests drive its decode and its refusals directly rather than through internal/cli, so a defect is named at the file that holds it. A gremlins run scoped to ./internal/mapping reports zero NOT COVERED mutants, and every surviving mutant is classified in the closure reason.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/mapping/mapping_test.go (093a633) is the package's test file for mapping.go, the one file in it that had none: gap_test.go, join_test.go and setaside_test.go already existed, and `go test -coverprofile ./internal/mapping` measured Decode, check, id, listed, written and RejectedPairError.Error at 0.0% at entry and every one at 100% after (package 77.3% to 100.0%).
- The acceptance's "today it has none" was stale when this unit started: three test files were in the package, and what nothing in the package reached was mapping.go alone, which internal/cli/mapcmd_test.go drove from outside.
- The join the four sections read is held where it is decided: Decode refuses an unknown claim or unit id against the round's own ids, and Unmapped, ClaimsOf, Gaps and SetAside keep their existing in-package tests, all of which the hand mutants below exercise.
- The new tests call Decode and RejectedPairError directly: the decoded order with blank lines skipped, an empty mapping as [], a missing claim or unit in all three spellings (absent, null, "") refused as required, an unknown id refused on its line counting blank lines with the round's ids listed and "none" for a round holding none, a line with both ids wrong reported by its claim, the rendered error, and a supplied stamp refused through state.DecodeStamped.
- Every operator gremlins can mutate in internal/mapping (13 sites) was applied by hand and killed by the package's own tests: mapping.go:100 err!=nil->== by four Decode tests; :138 ==0->!=0 by TestAnUnknownIdInARoundHoldingNoneSaysNone and TestDecodeRefusesAnUnknownIdOnItsLineNamingWhatTheRoundHolds; :156 >0->>=0 by its absent_claim and absent_unit subtests; :156 >0-><=0 by four tests; join.go:22 by TestAUnitMappedToZeroClaimsOfItsRoundIsUnmapped; join.go:47 (both) by TestTheClaimsOfAUnitAreItsRoundsPairsInRecordedOrder; gap.go:68, :74 and :133 (both) by TestAReDerivationKeepsTheSetAsideOfAClaimStillUnmapped; setaside.go:58 and :62 by all four SetAside tests; dropping the null check and swapping the claim-first order were killed too. No mutant survived, so none needs classifying. gremlins itself was not run by this unit, because pgrep cannot see the process table from a subagent, so the zero NOT COVERED figure is for the orchestrator's quiet-window run to confirm.

tasks.title: Refuse a force-named setting the way argued and forcing are refused
tasks.acceptance: config.protectedTokens holds argued and forcing but not force, so a name like CR_POST_FORCE_FINDINGS is not refused by name even though the deny-list comment claims a setting that would override 6.3 cannot be addressed. It is inert today because fromEnv maps only known keys, so it overrides nothing; the gap is that the list is one synonym short of what it says about itself, and the next reader tests the claim rather than the list. Adding force needs carriers entries for enforce, reinforce and workforce, so the change is not a one-line addition and a test drives each carrier through unrefused. Found by argued-forcing-unoverridable, whose unit left it rather than editing a closed task with that blast radius.

tasks.title: Hand the head symbol index to hunk clustering
tasks.acceptance: brief/brief.go calls unit.Clusters with a nil SymbolIndex on every run, so the symbol branch of hunk clustering never runs outside tests and every pull request clusters by adjacency alone. The nil was deliberate while no index existed; internal/unit/symbols.go says so, calling a nil index every run until the head symbol index exists. symbol-index-build has since built that index, and nothing handed it over. It does not satisfy unit.SymbolIndex yet: Indexed can be answered, but Enclosing needs the span each symbol covers, and the index records only the line a symbol is declared on. The index gains the spans or an adapter derives them, cr brief passes the built index where it now passes nil, and a file the index cannot serve still falls through to adjacency without an error. A test drives cr brief over a diff whose hunks sit inside one function and asserts they form one unit by symbol, where adjacency alone would split them.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr brief no longer passes a nil SymbolIndex: brief.go's unitsOf builds 4.3.1's head index through symbol.Head, the same one cr review attaches candidates from, and hands it to unit.Clusters, so the symbol branch of 3.4.4 now runs on every brief whose profile names a language cr indexes.
- The deliberate nil is gone with its reason: the index exists, and a nil now reaches clustering only as headSymbols' nil interface for a head whose profile names no language cr can scan.
- internal/unit/symbols.go and cluster.go no longer call a nil index every run's state; both comments name *symbol.Index as the implementation and a nil index only as a head cr cannot index.
- symbol-index-build's index reached no clustering caller before this; deadcode ./... lists none of Indexed, Enclosing, cover or bodyEnd, so all four are reachable from main through cr brief.
- The index gains the spans rather than an adapter deriving them, because a declaration line alone cannot say where a body ends and a derived bound (up to the next declaration) would name a function for trailing top-level code; internal/symbol/span.go bounds each body at the brace that closes the first brace opened outside parentheses, skipping strings and comments, and Enclosing names the innermost span keyed name@line so two same-named methods stay two symbols.
- A file the index cannot serve falls through without an error: a profile with no indexable language yields a nil interface (headSymbols never wraps a nil *Index), a file outside the index is not Indexed, and a body the scan cannot bound gets no span, all covered by TestABodyTheScanCannotBoundEnclosesNothing, TestTheIndexCoversTheFilesItWasBuiltOver and the plain-profile half of the brief test.
- TestTwoHunksInsideOneFunctionAreOneUnitBySymbol drives brief.Run over a repository whose change edits lines 5 and 24 of one Go function and asserts one unit formed by symbol with ranges 2-8 and 21-26, and two adjacency units under a profile with no symbols.lang; passing nil again fails it, and a dogfood cr brief with the dev binary on a laravel-pest scratch repository formed u1 by symbol over total()'s two hunks (7-13, 26-32) and u2 by symbol for label() (36-41), where adjacency would have joined 26-32 with 36-41.

tasks.title: Record the hits cr review attaches in the rule ledger
tasks.acceptance: cr review evaluates each rule's detect block and attaches the hits to the prompts it emits, but does not append them to rule-stats.ndjson. 2.6.1 item 6 requires every hit to be appended with the rule id, path, line, round and head, and 6.2.5 stamps a citation origin: rule only by matching it positionally against that ledger, so a citation resting on a hit cr review found and did not record grades as the agent's own. cr review records its hits through rule.RecordHits, the same writer cr rules check uses, and running cr review twice at one head leaves one ledger entry per hit. A test records a finding citing a line only cr review hit, and asserts the citation is stamped origin: rule. Found by the unit closing citation-origin-stamping, running beside the unit that built cr review.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr review now appends every hit it attaches to rule-stats.ndjson: internal/review/attach.go's detect evaluates the detectors once and hands the same hits to rule.RecordHits before rule.Attach places them on units, so the prompts and the ledger are fed from one list.
- Each entry carries 2.6.1 item 6's rule id, path, line, round and head plus the pull request and a UTC timestamp, which is what 6.2.5's positional match reads; a mutation passing nil to RecordHits fails both new tests, so the stamp now depends on cr review's write and not on an earlier cr rules check.
- The writer is rule.RecordHits, the one cr rules check uses, keyed so a rerun overwrites; TestReviewRunTwiceAtOneHeadLeavesOneLedgerEntryPerHit runs cr review twice with no cr rules check and reads three entries off the file's bytes, and TestTheRuleLedgerHasOneWriter still passes unchanged because the call reaches state.UpdateRuleStats only through rule's update.
- TestACitationOfALineOnlyReviewHitIsOfRuleOrigin runs cr review and then cr record on a finding citing lib.go:4 and asserts origin rule, grade cited and kind finding; a dogfood run with the dev binary over a scratch repository read three hit entries in rule-stats.ndjson after two cr review runs and cr record stamped the citation origin rule.
- The gap sat between two units' packages, so the tests drive both commands end to end through the CLI; their reviewedHome helper records the unit as cr brief does (head lines 1 to 7 under the diff's three lines of context), because detectedHome's 3-to-7 unit is refused by review.Run's stale-unit check while cr rules check never checks it.

tasks.title: Apply a rule's profiles list in the rule package, once
tasks.acceptance: 2.6's table gives a rule a profiles list, empty meaning all, and internal/review/attach.go is the only place that reads it. cr rules check evaluates every rule regardless, so a rule scoped to another profile reports hits there that cr review, on the same pull request, never shows. The check moves into the rule package beside Rule.Applies, which already answers globs and exempt, and every command that evaluates rules asks it. A test resolves a rule scoped to profile A under profile B and asserts cr rules check and cr review both report no hit from it, and both do under profile A.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A rule's profiles row is now answered in one place, internal/rule/profiles.go: Rule.InProfile reads it (empty means all, the empty id of an unmatched round is named by no list) and ForProfile keeps the resolved corpus's rules that apply under one profile, replacing the inline check review/attach.go carried.
- cr rules check no longer evaluates a rule scoped to another profile: roundMatchers compiles rule.ForProfile(corpus, profileID), and reverting that one call fails the beta rules-check subtest while the review subtests stay green, so the test separates the two commands.
- Both evaluating commands ask rule.ForProfile after resolution (review/attach.go's detect and cli/rulescheck.go's roundMatchers are the only rule.Compile callers outside tests); it lives in its own file because TestDetectionCanReadNothingButTheDiff fences detect.go's imports, and TestARuleAppliesOnlyUnderTheProfilesItNames pins the row including that a per-repository rule scoped elsewhere still shadows the global rule of its id.
- TestARuleScopedToAnotherProfileHitsInNeitherCommand scopes no-panic to alpha, resolves the round to beta and to alpha in separate homes, and asserts cr rules check's hits and cr review's prompt hit lines and ledger entries are 0 under beta and 3 under alpha, driving both commands end to end through the CLI.

tasks.title: Give the rule fix generator a caller outside its tests
tasks.acceptance: rule-fix-suggestion closed with Matcher.Replacement, Matcher.Suggest, confirmedBy and placeable written and tested, and deadcode still lists all four as reachable from tests alone: no command generates a suggestion from a rule fix. That is the signal CLAUDE.md names, a function the closing task was meant to wire staying test-only. The command that turns a confirmed rule-produced record into one carrying suggestion_origin: rule calls Suggest, placing it where 2.6.2 item 2 and 8.2's validation run before drafting. After this closes none of the four appears in deadcode ./... output. A test drives a real rule with a fix block through the command and asserts the drafted block carries the generated suggestion and its machine-generated label.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/rulefix.go's suggestRuleFixes gives Matcher.Suggest its first caller outside a test: it collects the rules the round's records name, keeps the matchers carrying a fix block, evaluates them over the round's hunks, and hands each record the hit its own citations confirm.
- The test-only signal is gone rather than silenced: deadcode ./... listed Matcher.Replacement, Matcher.Suggest, confirmedBy and placeable at entry and lists none of the four now, and all four still exist, with placeable reading §8.2 through internal/suggestion so the rule path and the post path cannot drift apart.
- internal/cli/record.go calls suggestRuleFixes between acceptRecords and appendRecords, so §2.6.2 item 2's generation and §8.2's placement both run before the record is stored and long before cr draft renders it, and the record that fails validation keeps its finding and loses only the replacement.
- deadcode ./... at exit holds 45 entries against 48 at entry, and the three that left are Matcher.Suggest, confirmedBy and placeable, with Matcher.Replacement leaving as Suggest's callee.
- The output was read rather than counted: no line of it names internal/rule/fix.go, and the one line naming internal/suggestion is Validate, which cr post will call.
- TestARuleFixReachesTheDraftAsAMachineGeneratedSuggestion drives a real use-of-panic rule carrying fix.replace and fix.with through cr rules check, cr record and cr draft, and asserts draft.md carries the fenced suggestion block and the machine-generated label, while TestASuggestionSection82RefusesIsDroppedAndItsRecordIsNot asserts the LEFT-anchored record reaches the draft with no block at all.

tasks.title: Refuse an intent-axis finding on a unit no claim maps to
tasks.acceptance: 4.1.2 raises a unit mapped to no claim as an unmapped-unit item, and 4.1.4 makes that item a question, never a finding. cr record nonetheless accepts a record from an intent-axis role with kind: finding anchored on such a unit, and nothing downstream turns it back, so a finding with no claim to rest on reaches the draft asserting that the unit fails a requirement nobody stated. cr record refuses it with exit 1, naming the record and the unit, or forces it to a question, whichever 4.1.4 supports on reading. A test records an intent-axis finding on an unmapped unit and asserts it never reaches findings.ndjson as kind: finding. Found by the unit closing review-prompt-contract.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr record now applies 4.1.4 itself: internal/cli/unmappedintent.go's forceUnmappedIntent reads the round's unmapped units from mapping.Unmapped over mapping.ndjson, the same derivation 4.1.2's item is raised from, and acceptRecords calls it after the axis is stamped and the grade computed.
- An intent-axis record written as kind finding on such a unit is moved to kind question before the single append, so nothing downstream has a finding to turn back; a round with no mapping recorded maps every unit to zero claims and is forced the same way, and only the intent axis and only toward the question register are touched.
- Forcing was chosen over refusal because 4.1.4 says the unmapped unit MUST default to a question: a default is cr's to apply, the record is re-shaped rather than the file rejected (P2, and 6.3.1's precedent for argued records), and a refusal would have made the agent rewrite the kind cr already knows.
- TestAnIntentFindingOnAnUnmappedUnitIsStoredAsAQuestion records the same intent finding, graded cited so 6.3 forces nothing, with and without a mapping pair for u1 and asserts findings.ndjson holds kind question unmapped and kind finding mapped; disabling the call fails only the unmapped subtest, and a dogfood cr record with the dev binary stored the record as kind question.
- The gap sat between cr review's prompt contract, which already raises the unmapped item as a question, and cr record, which never read the mapping for the kind; the test drives cr record end to end through the CLI over a real mapping file.

tasks.title: Name why a profile-less role was skipped
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by quiet-honesty-exemptions dogfood (2026-09-13): coverage.skipReason renders a role skipped on an active axis as "its profiles list names  and this round resolved profile ..." when the role's profiles list is empty, so the §4.6.4 sentence names nothing and sends the reader to a list that is not the cause.
- The reason says what actually excluded the role when its profiles list is empty, reusing the clause that decided rather than rewording it, and the same sentence reaches cr review's fan-out and cr status through the one shared derivation.
- A test skips a role with an empty profiles list on an active axis and asserts the sentence carries no empty name and states the deciding reason.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The dogfood defect is reproduced and gone: on a local scratch repo briefed under the generic profile with a self-contained gh shim, then given a global role error-paths on the correctness axis with "profiles": [] after the brief, the binary before 9671aea printed "role error-paths skipped, per §4.6.4: its profiles list names  and this round resolved profile generic; the role looks only under a profile it names" from both `cr status` and `cr review --axis intent`; the binary at 9671aea prints "role error-paths skipped, per §4.6.4: this round's active roles, which `cr brief` recorded per §4.5.1, do not name it, though its axis correctness ran and its profiles list is empty, which admits every profile; run `cr brief` again to record the round's active roles anew" from both, and git status --porcelain in the repo under review stayed empty. Re-running `cr brief` at the same head was measured to record ["error-paths","convention","correctness","intent-coverage"], so the sentence's fix is true.
- The reason says what actually excluded the role, reusing the clause that decided and reaching both commands through the one derivation: internal/coverage/skipped.go's skipReason now asks activation.ActiveRoles about the role alone instead of restating its profiles clause; when the definition admits the role (an empty list, or one naming the resolved profile), what decided is meta.json's recorded active set and notRecordedReason names it, and a list excluding the profile keeps its original sentence. No second path was added: cr review (internal/review/run.go skippedOf) and cr status (internal/cli/status.go lensesOf) both still call coverage.Skipped, and TestASkippedRoleReachesBothTheFanOutAndTheStatusReport stays green.
- A test skips a role with an empty profiles list on an active axis and asserts no empty name and the deciding reason: internal/coverage/skipped_test.go TestASkippedRoleOnARunningAxisIsGivenTheReasonThatDecided covers an empty list, a list naming the resolved profile and a list naming another, asserting the exact sentences and that the empty-list reason carries no "names  "; internal/cli/skippedrole_test.go TestAnEmptyProfilesRoleIsSkippedForTheReasonThatDecidedInBothReports writes the role after statusHome's brief and asserts cr review and cr status report the same SkippedRole with that reason and both honesty arrays carry its disclosure. Hand mutant `len(...) < 0` in skipReason restored the old sentence and failed both tests; reverted to the identical revision.

tasks.title: Refuse a complete verdict over zero units
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by quiet-honesty-exemptions dogfood (2026-09-13): cr status prints "round complete, per §10.2" on a round with zero units, because every condition over an empty set is vacuously met, so a reader is told a review is complete that reviewed nothing.
- A round with zero units is not reported complete, and the verdict names why through coverage.Lenses.Verdict so the sentence still cannot be produced without the lenses.
- A test briefs a round whose diff yields no units and asserts the verdict is not complete and states the reason, in both output shapes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The dogfood defect is reproduced and gone: on a local scratch repo whose head branch is one empty commit over main, briefed with a self-contained gh shim, the binary before edb3b91 printed `"completeness": {"complete": true, "reasons": []}` and "round complete, per §10.2" with "units: 0 total"; the binary at edb3b91 prints `"complete": false` and "round not complete, per §10.2: §10.2.2: this round formed no unit from its diff, so no cell was filled and there is no row of cells its coverage could be complete over" in both shapes, and git status --porcelain in the repo under review stayed empty.
- A round with zero units is not reported complete and the verdict names why through coverage.Lenses.Verdict: internal/coverage/completeness.go's rowReason returns that §10.2.2 reason when Rows.Units is 0, so Complete() yields complete false with the one reason, and cr status still reaches the sentence only through lenses.Verdict(verdict.Complete, verdict.Reason()) in internal/cli/status.go, unchanged; no second path was added. This reads §10.2.2's "every unit has a complete row" as unmet by a round that formed no unit rather than met vacuously; the spec text is unchanged.
- A test briefs a round whose diff yields no units and asserts both output shapes: internal/cli/emptyround_test.go's emptyRoundHome runs `cr brief` over a checkout whose head is an empty commit (requiring the brief's units to be empty), and TestARoundThatFormedNoUnitIsNotReportedComplete asserts the JSON completeness (complete false, exactly that reason), and that both the document's honesty and a real terminal (throughATerminal) carry the not-complete line, never "round complete, per §10.2", and still carry the lens convention/reinvention line beside it. internal/coverage/completeness_test.go TestARoundThatFormedNoUnitIsNotComplete covers the predicate with and without active roles. Hand mutant `c.Rows.Units < 0` failed both tests; reverted to the identical revision.

tasks.title: Refuse a record id already held
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by unit-containment-predicate dogfood (2026-09-13): cr record accepted a second record carrying id f1 while f1 was already held, and §6.1 makes the id stable for the life of the PR, so a draft marker, a waiver, the posted index and a triage event naming f1 could reach either record.
- cr record refuses, with exit 1 naming the id and both lines or the stored record, a batch whose ids repeat within the file or collide with a record already stored for the pull request, and writes nothing.
- A test records f1, then a batch carrying f1 again, and asserts the refusal and that findings.ndjson is byte-identical afterwards; a second test repeats an id inside one batch.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The measured defect is reproduced and closed: with the new call in internal/cli/record.go acceptRecords replaced by a nil error, TestARecordIDAlreadyStoredIsRefusedAndNothingIsWritten shows the second batch carrying f1 accepted, and with it restored the batch is refused, so a draft marker, waiver, posted index entry or triage event naming f1 can reach only the one record §6.1 keeps stable.
- cr record refuses in internal/cli/recordids.go refuseHeldIDs, called in acceptRecords right after finding.Decode and before any lock or write: an id repeated within the file exits 1 as a RejectedRecordError on field id naming the id, its line and the line of its first use, and an id held by a record stored in any round (findings.ndjson read whole, declared in roundscope_test.go's crossRoundReaders) exits 1 naming the id, the line, and the stored record's round and head; the check lives at cr record's acceptance rather than in the Decode door because the stored ids are pull request state the decoder is never handed, and cr record is the only command that adds a record to findings.ndjson, so no door bypasses it. Dogfood refusal quoted: `rec2.ndjson line 2: id "f1" is already held by the record stored for this pull request in round 1 at head d2fe88e…; §6.1 makes a record id stable for the life of the pull request, so give this record an id no stored record holds`, exit 1, findings.ndjson shasum unchanged.
- internal/cli/recordids_test.go TestARecordIDAlreadyStoredIsRefusedAndNothingIsWritten records f1, then a batch of f2 and f1, and asserts the refusal on line 2 field id with exit 1 and findings.ndjson byte-identical afterwards, so the fresh f2 was not written either.
- internal/cli/recordids_test.go TestARecordIDRepeatedWithinOneBatchIsRefused hands one batch f1, f2, f1 and asserts the refusal on line 3 naming line 1 with exit 1 and nothing stored; both tests go red with the call removed.
